author: luca-fahrendholz-heiermann
body:
### Motivation
- Provide tooling to rebuild IFC -> OBJ -> GLB viewer artifacts on-demand and expose an Open3D-based local viewer launch for PLY files. 
- Improve in-browser 3D preview coverage by adding client-side PLY support when canonical GLB is not available. 

### Description
- Backend: add `Rag3dActionRequest`, `_launch_open3d_ply_viewer`, `POST /rag/actions/rebuild-3d-viewer`, and `POST /documents/open3d-view/{stored_filename}` endpoints to trigger IFC rebuilds and to spawn an Open3D subprocess for `.ply` files, with Linux display checks and subprocess timeout handling. 
- Ingestion: update `_prepare_3d_pipeline_artifacts` to prefer the `.obj` produced from an IFC conversion as the source for generating the canonical GLB by switching `source_path`/`extension` when conversion yields an OBJ. 
- Frontend: extend `buildModelViewerHtml` to render `.ply` files using three.js (`THREE`, `OrbitControls`, `PLYLoader`) in a `<canvas>`, add a UI button to request IFC rebuilds from the RAG table, and automatically trigger a server-side Open3D launch for `.ply` files (with duplicate-launch protection). 
- Tests: add unit tests covering the new rebuild endpoint behavior and PLY/Open3D launch flows and a test ensuring `_prepare_3d_pipeline_artifacts` uses `.obj` for GLB conversion. 

### Testing
- Ran the backend unit tests under `backend/tests/` including the new `TestOpen3dAction`, `TestRagIfcActions` cases in `test_app_config.py` and `test_prepare_3d_pipeline_artifacts_uses_ifc_obj_for_glb_conversion` in `test_ingestion.py`. 
- All added and existing unit tests executed and passed.

Support for BNSH input/output format in GQA attention:

**Kernel and buffer logic updates**
* Updated `group_query_attention_impl.cu` and `group_query_attention_impl.h` to recognize and handle BNSH input format, ensuring Q is always written to a BSNH buffer for flash attention and adjusting buffer requirements for BNSH cases. author: sotoj24
body:
Summary

Adds two exported pure-JS utility functions to WebAuthNProvider that bridge the gap between what the WebAuthn API returns and what the Soroban smart wallet contract's __check_auth requires — with zero new dependencies.

What Changed

Modified files

File | Description -- | -- src/providers/WebAuthNProvider.ts | Added extractPublicKey and convertSignatureDERtoCompact as exported functions above the class. No changes to existing methods. src/tests/WebAuthNProvider.test.ts | 20 unit tests using real P-256 DER/SEC-1 test vectors

How It Works

extractPublicKey(credential: PublicKeyCredential): Uint8Array

WebAuthn's registerCredential() returns a PublicKeyCredential whose AuthenticatorAttestationResponse.getPublicKey() contains a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) blob. For P-256 this blob is 91 bytes with a fixed 26-byte header, placing the 65-byte uncompressed point (0x04 || X || Y) at a known offset:

Bytes  0– 1  outer SEQUENCE tag+len     (30 49)
Bytes  2– 3  AlgId SEQUENCE tag+len     (30 13)
Bytes  4–12  OID id-ecPublicKey         (06 07 2a 86 48 ce 3d 02 01)
Bytes 13–22  OID P-256                  (06 08 2a 86 48 ce 3d 03 01 07)  ← 10 bytes
Bytes 23–24  BIT STRING tag+len         (03 42)
Byte  25     BIT STRING padding byte    (00)
Bytes 26–90  65-byte uncompressed point (04 || X || Y)  ← offset 26, not 27

Implementation note: The issue spec stated offset 27 and 72-byte SPKI. The actual P-256 OID is 10 bytes (not 9), making the header 26 bytes and the full SPKI 91 bytes. This was confirmed by counting the real DER encoding and verified by the passing test vectors.

The function validates the response type, checks the blob length, asserts the 0x04 marker, and returns a .slice() copy so callers cannot alias into the original buffer.

convertSignatureDERtoCompact(derSignature: ArrayBuffer): Uint8Array

WebAuthn's authenticate() returns a signature in ASN.1 DER encoding. The Soroban contract requires compact 64-byte R||S. DER adds a sign-padding 0x00 byte when the high bit of r or s is set (making them 33 bytes), and strips leading zeros when they are short. This function handles all cases:

DER structure:
  30 <total-len>
    02 <r-len> <r-bytes>   (1–33 bytes)
    02 <s-len> <s-bytes>   (1–33 bytes)

Real-world DER lengths: 70 bytes (neither padded) → 72 bytes (both padded)

Output: 64 bytes
  [0–31]  r, stripped of 0x00 sign-padding, left-padded to 32 bytes
  [32–63] s, stripped of 0x00 sign-padding, left-padded to 32 bytes

Test Coverage — 20/20 passing

Checklist

  • [x] extractPublicKey returns 65-byte Uint8Array starting with 0x04
  • [x] convertSignatureDERtoCompact returns exactly 64 bytes
  • [x] Unit tests pass with known P-256 DER/SEC-1 test vectors — 20/20
  • [x] Zero regression in existing WebAuthNProvider methods
  • [x] No new external dependencies — pure ArrayBuffer manipulation only
  • [x] No changes to registerCredential() or authenticate() signatures
  • [x] TypeScript compilation clean (0 errors)
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Introduced comprehensive Invisible Wallet infrastructure with secure encryption support (Argon2id and PBKDF2 key derivation). * Added WebAuthN authentication capabilities for enhanced security. * Enabled USDC asset configuration with per-network support. * Implemented password strength evaluation, secure token generation, and recovery mechanisms. * **Tests** * Added WebAuthN authentication test coverage.

author: phanthai12
body:
This PR addresses the reported "freeze" issue in `.moveTo` and `scrollIntoView` by introducing safety bounds and coordinate validation.

Key changes:
1. **Step Clamping**: Introduced `MAX_PATH_STEPS` (10,000) and `MAX_SCROLL_STEPS` (5,000) to prevent astronomical step counts that could lead to hangs.
2. **Coordinate Validation**: Added `isFiniteVector` checks to prevent passing `NaN` or `Infinity` to Playwright's mouse actions.
3. **Natural Path Generation**: Updated `generateBezierAnchors` to sort control points based on movement direction, avoiding loopy paths for backward movements.
4. **Reliable Scrolling**: Improved viewport detection in `scrollIntoView` by using `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` and handling cases where `document.body` might be null.
5. **Accurate Timing**: Simplified and corrected the logic in `generateTimestamps` to ensure consistent and efficient movement pacing without the 25x slowdown introduced in an earlier iteration.

Fixes #6

author: copilot
body:
`StdioServerTransport` uses stdout as the JSON-RPC protocol stream. `logger.debug()` and `logger.info()` were both calling `console.info()`, which writes to stdout — corrupting the protocol framing and causing the MCP handshake to fail with `connection closed: initialize response`.

## Changes

- **`src/utils/logger.ts`** — Replace `console.info()` with `console.error()` in `debug()` and `info()`. All four log levels now write exclusively to stderr, leaving stdout clean for the MCP protocol.
- **`tests/integration/server-start.test.ts`** — Update the startup integration test to listen for the ready message on `stderr` instead of `stdout`.

```ts
// Before — wrote startup messages to stdout, breaking MCP handshake
export function info(message: string, meta?: unknown): void {
  if (currentLogLevel <= LogLevel.INFO) {
    console.info(`[INFO] ${message}`, meta ? meta : '');
  }
}

// After — all log output goes to stderr
export function info(message: string, meta?: unknown): void {
  if (currentLogLevel <= LogLevel.INFO) {
    console.error(`[INFO] ${message}`, meta ? meta : '');
  }
}
```

author: alecmarcus
body:
## Summary

Full protocol core implementation across 8 crates, produced by Loom (autonomous agent loop) with no human-written code. Covers identity (DID), encryption (MLS + sender keys), authorization (UCAN), contexts, transport, discovery, media, bridge, MCP, and FFI.

### Crates touched
- **scp-core** — DID, MLS, UCAN, envelopes, contexts, Merkle log, trust, discovery, bridge, provenance, tools
- **scp-transport** — Native relay (server + client), transport manager, scoring, blob storage
- **scp-media** — Media key derivation, signaling, session lifecycle
- **scp-mcp** — MCP server (tools/resources/prompts), client, stdio + SSE transports
- **scp-ffi** — PyO3 bridge with tokio runtime lifecycle
- **scp-node** — Node orchestrator wiring
- **scp-platform** — Platform abstraction traits + in-memory test adapters
- **scp-testing** — Phase 1 integration test

### Stories (53)
SCP-001 through SCP-027, SCP-030–032, SCP-052–056, SCP-061–064, SCP-066–067, SCP-070–073, SCP-076, SCP-084, SCP-087, SCP-107–109, SCP-140–143

### ADRs (5)
ADR-029 (Offline/Sync), ADR-030 (Event Log Pruning), ADR-031 (Multi-Admin Governance), ADR-032 (Addressability), ADR-033 (Economic Governance)

### Stats
- **95 commits** | **158 files** | **~78k lines** (+77,692 / -4,645)
- Branch: `loom-20260223-194742-e32f40`

## Review status

~39 review comments posted by specialized agents (security-reviewer, bug-catcher, adversarial-expert, red-hat, white-hat, black-hat, architecture-reviewer, alignment-reviewer). Key systemic findings:

- Authorization wiring gaps between sound crypto primitives and application layer
- No zeroization of key material (`scp-media`)
- `filter_map(.ok())` fail-open pattern in UCAN validation
- MCP server pre-initialization bypass + SSE with no auth/rate limiting
- `validate_ucan_stateless` skips nonce, revocation, chain, attenuation checks
- `std::sync::Mutex` in async code (`ContextManager`)
- Network-exposed endpoints with no rate limiting
- Dead/stub code behind real interfaces (scoring, discovery)

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo build --workspace` compiles clean
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace` has no warnings
- [ ] Address CRITICAL and HIGH findings from review comments before merge

author: jamesarich
body:
This PR introduces significant architectural improvements to the Meshtastic Android application, focusing on Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) readiness, feature modularization, and improved connection reliability.

**Key Changes:**
*   **KMP Migration & Decoupling:** Decoupled core domain models (Contact, Node, DataPacket) and utility logic (Date/Time, URI, Base64) from the Android framework, moving them to `commonMain` modules. Introduced platform-agnostic abstractions like `CommonParcelable` and `CommonUri`.
*   **Feature Modularization:** Successfully migrated the Messaging UI (Contacts, Chat, Sharing) from the `:app` module to the standalone `:feature:messaging` module, improving build separation and maintainability.
*   **Handshake Robustness:** Overhauled the device connection flow in `MeshConfigFlowManager` and `MeshConnectionManager`. Added a 10-second handshake timeout, stage-specific retry logic, and heartbeat signals to prevent connection stalls (addresses "Stuck on Fetching Settings" issues).
*   **Enhanced Notifications:** Refactored `MeshServiceNotificationsImpl` to use localized multiplatform resources and improved telemetry caching. This fixes reports of "blank" or missing text in system notifications and provides more detailed device status.
*   **UI & Stability Fixes:** Refined firmware version checking in `Main.kt` to eliminate transient "update required" dialogs and migrated logging across several features to Kermit for KMP compatibility.

**Resolves:**
- Improves connection reliability for nRF52-based devices (e.g., T1000-E) by providing defensive handshake recovery.
- Fixes incorrect "Firmware too old" alerts during the initial connection phase.
- Fixes missing localization and blank text in the persistent background service notification.

This work establishes a modern, modular foundation for the codebase while directly improving the reliability of device connectivity for users.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/draxleredit/agent-runs/699d000f3a60942ed0531c13

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Erro no botao ver projetos quando clico nao vai para pagina projetos corrija o mais rapido possivel

✅ **Result:** Fixed the "Ver projetos" button on the Hero section so it correctly navigates to the `/projetos` page.

The button was using a plain HTML anchor tag (`<a href="/projetos">`) instead of React Router's `<Link>` component. This caused a full browser page reload instead of client-side navigation, which in a single-page application (SPA) would result in a 404 error since there is no physical file at `/projetos` on the server.

Two changes were made:

- **`src/components/Hero.tsx`**: Replaced `<motion.a href="/projetos">` with React Router's `<Link to="/projetos">`, matching the pattern already used in the Header and Footer navigation components. The hover/tap scale animations were preserved using CSS (`hover:scale-[1.02]` and `active:scale-[0.97]`), which were already supported by the existing Tailwind transition classes.

- **`public/_redirects`**: Added a Netlify SPA redirect rule (`/* /index.html 200`) so that all routes are properly served by `index.html`. This ensures that even if a user lands directly on `/projetos` (via bookmark, refresh, or shared link), Netlify serves the React app instead of returning a 404.

# PR Ready

## Types of changes

## Summary

在关键的分支和 PR 操作前验证 SSH 配置，避免因 SSH 错误导致的拉取失败。

### Key Changes

- 在 branch/create、pr/create/branch、pr/merge 三个命令中加入 `ensure_ssh_ready` 调用
- 统一并删除重复的导入语句
- 保持原有 spinner UI，仅在 SSH 检查通过后执行拉取
- 显式使用 `PullOptions::no_stash()` 保持 stash 行为不变

## Changes

### Features

- 为分支创建、PR 创建分支、PR 合并命令添加 SSH 就绪检查

### Refactors

- 合并重复导入，统一 import 结构
- 调整 spinner 包装顺序

### Others

- 更新错误映射以兼容 SSH 检查返回

## Impact Analysis

### Affected Modules

| Module | Impact | Severity |
|--------|--------|----------|
| branch/create 命令 | 加入 SSH 检查，可能在未配置 SSH 时中止命令，需要在 CI 环境中注意 | medium |
| pr/create/branch 命令 | 同上，增加前置检查导致非交互式运行需额外配置 | medium |
| pr/merge 命令 | 同上，合并流程在缺少 SSH 时会提前退出 | medium |

### Risk Assessment

**Overall risk**: medium

**Risk factors**:
- 在非交互式环境（如 CI）中 SSH 检查可能导致命令阻塞或提前退出
- 错误信息可能对不熟悉 SSH 配置的用户不友好

**Mitigation**:
- 提供 `--skip-ssh-check` 或类似的非交互式标志以在 CI 中绕过检查
- 在文档和帮助信息中说明新增的 SSH 检查要求

### Testing Suggestions

- 在本地已配置 SSH 的环境下执行 branch/create、pr/create/branch、pr/merge，确认正常拉取
- 在未配置 SSH 的环境下运行上述命令，验证能够捕获错误并给出提示
- 在 CI/脚本环境中使用 `--skip-ssh-check` 标志，确保流程不被阻塞

Adds 4 new built-in scalar functions for fuzzy string matching and similarity scoring, useful for record deduplication, search ranking, and data quality workflows:

| Function | Return type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `levenshtein(str1, str2)` | INT |  |
| `damerau_levenshtein(str1, str2)` | INT | True Damerau-Levenshtein distance (unrestricted transpositions) |
| `jaro_winkler(str1, str2)` | DOUBLE | Jaro-Winkler similarity [0.0, 1.0] |
| `jaccard_similarity(str1, str2)` | DOUBLE | Jaccard similarity on byte bigrams [0.0, 1.0] |

All functions accept `VARCHAR` and `STRING` inputs and propagate NULL.

### Release note

Add 4 built-in string similarity/distance functions: `levenshtein`, `damerau_levenshtein`, `jaro_winkler`, `jaccard_similarity`.

### Check List (For Author)

- Test
    - [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)

```sql
-- Levenshtein
SELECT levenshtein('kitten', 'sitting');          -- 3
SELECT levenshtein('', 'abc');                    -- 3

-- Damerau-Levenshtein (true, not OSA)
SELECT damerau_levenshtein('ca', 'abc');          -- 2  (transposition ca->ac + insert b)
SELECT damerau_levenshtein('kitten', 'sitting');  -- 3

-- Jaro-Winkler
SELECT jaro_winkler('MARTHA', 'MARHTA');          -- ~0.9611
SELECT jaro_winkler('abc', 'abc');                -- 1.0

-- Jaccard similarity
SELECT jaccard_similarity('night', 'nacht');      -- ~0.222
SELECT jaccard_similarity('abc', 'abc');          -- 1.0

```

### Performance

Benchmarked against equivalent Java UDFs on Apache Doris 4.0.2

**Test setup:** 100M rows × 96-char strings (md5-generated), `SELECT count(func(a, b))` to isolate compute from I/O.

| Rows | C++ builtin | Java UDF | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1M | 1.5s | 6.5s | 4.3x* |
| 100M | 2m 20s | 4m 25s | ~1.9x |
| 1B | 19m | 36m | ~1.89x |
| 400M production rows (repeated query) | 0.11s | 96s | ~870x |

\* 1M speedup is JVM-warmup-inflated; 100M and 1B represent fully JIT-compiled steady state.

Key observations:
- **Consistent ~2x speedup** at scale (100M and 1B confirm the JVM reaches full JIT compilation and the advantage stabilises).
- **Result cache**: C++ builtins benefit from Doris SQL-layer result caching keyed on query text + data version. Java UDFs bypass the result cache entirely and always recompute — explaining the ~870x gap on repeated queries.
- **Stack allocation**: `levenshtein`, `jaro_winkler`, and `jaccard_similarity` use stack-allocated arrays for strings ≤512 bytes, eliminating heap allocation for the common case.

### Motivation
- Provide a single, improved JSON-LD builder so both Engine1 and Engine2 emit the same tour schema with stable relationships and better SEO signals for tour pages only. 
- Reuse a canonical `Place` node and ensure `WebPage.mainEntity` points to the `Product` node while `TouristTrip` references the canonical `Place` and includes an `ItemList` itinerary.

author: tevoth
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes GPIO bit set/reset writes by replacing read-modify-write operations on `GPIOC->BSRR` with direct writes.

## What changed
Updated `led_on()` and `led_off()` to use direct writes:
- `GPIOC->BSRR = GPIO_BSRR_BS13;`
- `GPIOC->BSRR = GPIO_BSRR_BR13;`

Files touched:
- `cmsis_button/src/gpio.c`
- `cmsis_sysclk_blinky/src/gpio.c`
- `cmsis_tim2clk_blinky/src/gpio.c`

## Root cause
`GPIOx_BSRR` on STM32F4 is a write-only set/reset register intended for atomic GPIO updates. Using `|=` on this register causes a read-modify-write sequence:
1. Load from `GPIOx_BSRR`
2. OR with mask
3. Store to `GPIOx_BSRR`

That read step is invalid for a write-only register and breaks the intended one-write atomic update model.

## Why this fix is correct
Direct assignment (`=`) to `BSRR` emits one write transaction with only the intended bit mask:
- `BS13` sets PC13
- `BR13` resets PC13

This aligns with STM32 register semantics and preserves atomicity.

## Impact
- No API changes.
- Same functional LED behavior.
- Correct and safer peripheral register access pattern.

## Validation
Build completed successfully after the changes:
- `cmake -S cmsis_button -B /tmp/cmake_button && cmake --build /tmp/cmake_button -j`
- `cmake -S cmsis_sysclk_blinky -B /tmp/cmake_sysclk_blinky && cmake --build /tmp/cmake_sysclk_blinky -j`
- `cmake -S cmsis_tim2clk_blinky -B /tmp/cmake_tim2clk_blinky && cmake --build /tmp/cmake_tim2clk_blinky -j`

The site was not being deployed to `hcscmedia.github.io/ai-learning-sites/` — no GitHub Actions workflow existed to publish it.

## Changes

- **New file: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — standard GitHub Pages deployment pipeline using official Actions:
  - Triggers on push to `main` and supports manual dispatch (`workflow_dispatch`)
  - Uses `actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, and `actions/deploy-pages`
  - Minimal permissions (`pages: write`, `id-token: write`, `contents: read`)
  - Concurrency guard to prevent overlapping deployments

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
```

## No HTML/CSS changes needed

All internal links already use relative paths (`href="styles.css"`, `href="index.html"`, etc.), so they resolve correctly under the `/ai-learning-sites/` base path without modification.

## Required repo setting

In **Settings → Pages**, set the source to **GitHub Actions** (not a branch) to activate deployments from this workflow.

author: lagarcess
body:
This PR addresses a critical issue where WAITING signals past their valid_until date were being evaluated for exits (e.g., stop-loss, take-profit) before the expiration check could run. This happened because check_exits() was called before the expiration loop in main.py.

Changes:
1.  **main.py**: Moved the expiration check for WAITING signals to the beginning of the active signals block. Created a `valid_active_signals` list that excludes expired signals, which is then passed to `check_exits()`.
2.  **signal_generator.py**: Added a defense-in-depth guard in `check_exits()` to skip any WAITING signal that is past its `valid_until` date, providing extra safety if the caller fails to filter them.
3.  **Tests**: Added regression tests verifying that stale signals are correctly expired and not falsely invalidated. Updated existing tests in `tests/engine/test_signal_generator.py` that were using REAL Signal objects with default (now) `valid_until` timestamps, which would have been caught by the new guard.

Verified with 601 passing tests.

Fixes #321

author: winechord
body:
## What
Add an OpenClaw-like runnable demo module under `openclaw/` (separate `go.mod`) that wires:

- An HTTP gateway (webhook-friendly).
- A real IM channel: Telegram (long polling).
- Per-session serialization + basic run control (status + cancel).

The gateway implementation lives under `openclaw/internal/gateway` to keep it
clearly scoped as a demo/integration surface (not a root `server/*` package).

## Gateway API

- `POST /v1/gateway/messages`
- `GET  /v1/gateway/status?request_id=...`
- `POST /v1/gateway/cancel`
- `GET  /healthz`

## Telegram channel

- Long polling (`getUpdates`) + restart-safe offset store.
- **Fail-closed DM by default**: `pairing` (operator approval required).
  - Approve with: `openclaw pairing approve <CODE> -telegram-token ...`
- Group policy: `disabled|open|allowlist` via `-telegram-group-policy` and
  `-telegram-allow-threads`.
- Commands: `/help` and `/cancel`.
- Streaming preview (`editMessageText`) via `-telegram-streaming`:
  `off|block|progress` (default: `progress`).
- Smarter reply splitting (prefer paragraph/newline boundaries).

## Reliability / ops

- Telegram API retries with exponential backoff on 429/5xx/transport errors.
- Optional Telegram proxy/timeout/retry tuning:
  `-telegram-proxy`, `-telegram-http-timeout`, `-telegram-max-retries`.
- `openclaw doctor` subcommand to check token/webhook/pairing store.

## Model defaults

- Default mode: `openai`
- Default model: `gpt-5`

## Docs

- `openclaw/README.md`
- `docs/mkdocs/{en,zh}/gateway.md` (also clarifies relationship to OpenClaw WS protocol)

## Tests

- `go test ./...`
- `cd openclaw && go test ./...`

author: joebeernink
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: `StatGenerator.CountNewLitterReports()` concatenates `LitterReportStatusEnum.New` into SQL, which produces `... = New` (the enum name) instead of `... = 1` (the integer value). SQL Server throws `Invalid column name 'New'`.
- **Cascade failure**: Since `Program.Main()` had no error isolation, the unhandled `SqlException` from `StatGenerator` crashed the entire daily job container — `LeaderboardGenerator` and `AchievementProcessor` never executed.
- **Fix 1**: Cast enum values to `(int)` before SQL concatenation in both `CountNewLitterReports` and `CountCleanedLitterReports`.
- **Fix 2**: Wrap each processor in a try-catch in `Program.cs` so one processor's failure is logged but doesn't prevent the others from running.

Fixes #2881

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify `dotnet build TrashMobDailyJobs` succeeds
- [ ] Deploy to dev and check container logs — all three processors should complete
- [ ] Merge to release and verify production leaderboards update at next scheduled run (midnight/noon UTC)
- [ ] Confirm the "New Litter Reports" and "Cleaned Litter Reports" site metrics are correct

author: silaszhr
body:
## Summary

Fixes 21 npm audit vulnerabilities (1 low, 20 high) by adding npm overrides for transitive dependencies in the jest dependency tree.

## Changes

- Added `overrides` in `package.json` to pin `minimatch` (>=10.2.1) and `glob` (>=10.5.1)
- Updated `package-lock.json` with resolved patched versions

## Details

All 21 vulnerabilities stem from a ReDoS issue in `minimatch` < 10.2.1 ([GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26)), pulled in transitively by jest 29.x via `glob` and `test-exclude`. Since `ts-jest` doesn't yet support jest 30, overrides are the cleanest fix without a breaking upgrade.

author: tnorlund
body:
## Summary

- Image entities were created without `receipt_count`, causing GSI3 (`NUM_RECEIPTS#00000`) to index all images as having 0 receipts
- Set `receipt_count` in all five code paths that create or modify receipts:
  - **`native.py`**: Set to `1` at Image creation (NATIVE always has exactly 1 receipt)
  - **`scan.py`**: Set to `len(cluster_dict)` after DBSCAN clustering completes
  - **`photo.py`**: Set to `successful_clusters` after clustering completes
  - **`ocr_processor.py`** (Swift single-pass): Set to `len(receipts)` at Image creation
  - **`merge_receipt.py`**: Set to `len(remaining_receipts)` after merging and deleting originals
- Backfilled 228 dev and 163 prod Image records with correct `receipt_count` from actual receipt entities

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that resolves an issue)

## Which Package(s) are Affected?

- [x] receipt_upload
- [x] Infrastructure (Pulumi)

## Testing

- [x] Verified all 228 dev images and 163 prod images now have correct `receipt_count` after backfill
- [x] All existing tests still pass with these changes

## Documentation & Code Quality

- [x] No new warnings or linting issues introduced
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines

## Impact Analysis

- **GSI3 queries** (`list_images_by_type`): Images now correctly indexed by receipt count instead of all appearing under `NUM_RECEIPTS#00000`
- **Upload status API**: No change — it already derives count from RECEIPT entities, not the Image field
- **Merge-receipt Lambda**: After merging, Image entity now reflects the updated receipt count
- **No breaking changes**: `receipt_count` is an optional field; existing queries continue to work

## Deployment Notes

- After merging, `pulumi up` will rebuild the upload container and merge-receipt Lambda images via CodeBuild
- The backfill of existing records has already been applied to both dev and prod

## Summary

- **XPP config auto-discovery**: Reads `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Dynamics365\XPPConfig\` to detect UDE environments and resolve dual metadata paths (custom + Microsoft packages)
- **Package resolver**: Maps model names to package names by reading descriptor XML files — handles the D365FO convention where a package can contain multiple models
- **Dual metadata paths**: `extract-metadata` and `build-database` scripts now scan both custom and Microsoft package roots in UDE mode
- **`packageName` parameter**: Added to `create_d365fo_file`, `modify_d365fo_file`, and `create_label` tools so files land in the correct `Package\Model` directory structure
- **Auto-detect custom models in UDE**: Everything under the custom packages path is treated as custom, everything under Microsoft root is standard — no `CUSTOM_MODELS` env var needed
- **Interactive config selector**: `npm run select-config` lets UDE users pick from available XPP configs
- **Simplified configuration**: Removed redundant `CUSTOM_PACKAGES_PATH` / `MICROSOFT_PACKAGES_PATH` env vars; restructured `.env.example` with clear Traditional vs UDE sections
- **Documentation**: Updated SETUP.md, MCP_CONFIG.md, CUSTOM_EXTENSIONS.md, MCP_TOOLS.md, README.md

## How it works

UDE environments use Power Platform Tools in VS2022 with two separate package directories:
- **Custom packages** (`ModelStoreFolder`): Your X++ code
- **Microsoft packages** (`FrameworkDirectory`): Standard D365 platform

The server auto-detects these paths from XPP config files. Set `DEV_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=auto` (default) and the server figures out the rest. Traditional environments continue to work unchanged.

## New files

- `src/utils/xppConfigProvider.ts` — Reads XPP config XML files
- `src/utils/packageResolver.ts` — Model-to-package name mapping
- `scripts/select-xpp-config.ps1` — Interactive PowerShell config picker

author: copilot
body:
Three polling sites in the upstream-sync workflow had fragile issue number extraction, no protection against stale PR matches, and unconditional issue closure even on timeout.

**Issue number extraction** — all three `gh issue create` calls
- Capture URL first, then extract with `grep -oP '/issues/\K[0-9]+'` instead of `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'`, which could match digits in error message text

**Stale PR filtering** — all three polling loops
- After issue creation, fetch `createdAt` via `gh issue view --json createdAt`
- Pass timestamp as exported env var; filter `gh pr list` with `.createdAt >= env.*_CREATED_AT` in jq
- Falls back to unfiltered polling with a warning if timestamp fetch fails

**Conditional issue close** — all three sites
- Issues are now only closed when a Copilot PR is detected within the 20-minute window
- On timeout, issue is left open with `::warning::` so the agent can still act on it

**Token scope validation**
- After the `ghp_` prefix check, run `gh auth status -t` and `grep -E '^ *Token scopes: .*\brepo\b'`
- Fails early with a clear error pointing to `https://github.com/settings/tokens` if `repo` scope is absent

**Comment accuracy**
- Removed the "documented automation path" claim; comment now states behavior depends on repository Copilot configuration and is not guaranteed

## What

Hardens the three Copilot agent invocation sites in `upstream-sync.yml`: safe issue-number extraction, stale-PR filtering by creation time, conditional issue close on PR detection, and actual `repo`-scope verification on the PAT.

## Why

Issue numbers were extracted with a pattern that could match error text; polling could latch onto stale PRs from prior runs; issues were closed even when no PR arrived; and token validation checked only the prefix, not actual scopes.

## Testing

- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux

## Checklist

- [ ] Follows GSD style (no enterprise patterns, no filler)
- [ ] Updates CHANGELOG.md for user-facing changes
- [ ] No unnecessary dependencies added
- [ ] Works on Windows (backslash paths tested)

## Breaking Changes

None

author: ashrobertsdragon
body:
## Summary

This PR completes the revision tracking frontend feature by aligning it with the real backend API, fixing test failures across acceptance, e2e, integration, and unit test suites, and cleaning up code quality issues.

## Key Features

- Fully functional revision history and diff viewer aligned to real backend responses
- View History navigation from PostEditor
- Short SHA prefix matching for revision lookup
- Cleaned test suite with removed obsolete tests and scripts

## Changes Included

**Bug Fixes:**

- ✅ Fix reversed `useRevisionDiff` argument order in `RevisionDiffPage` causing diffs to render backwards
- ✅ Fix `DiffViewer` colours (`bg-green-100`, `bg-red-100`) and add `data-testid` attributes for test stability
- ✅ Fix `find_by_sha` in `PostRevisionRepository` to support short SHA prefix matching so 7-char `short_sha` navigation resolves correctly
- ✅ Add `retry: false` to `useRevisionHistory`, `useRevisionDetail`, `useRevisionDiff`, and `useDraft` hooks so auth errors surface immediately without retry delays blocking e2e assertions
- ✅ Add `role="alert"` to `RevisionTimeline` error state and extract backend error message from response body for readable text
- ✅ Improve `isForbidden` detection in `RevisionHistory` to match "not authorized" text from backend error messages
- ✅ Pass empty `diffLines` to `DiffViewer` when `sha === otherSha` to show "No changes detected" for same-revision comparisons
- ✅ Fix `author_id` field usage across all revision unit and integration tests

**New Features:**

- ✅ Add View History button to `PostEditor` navigating to the revisions page

**Refactoring:**

- ✅ Trim acceptance test suite for revision tracking to focus on observable behaviour over implementation detail
- ✅ Remove `scripts/fix_commands.py` (no longer needed)
- ✅ Remove inline comments from test files (replaced with self-documenting test names)

## Technical Details

**Affected Components:**

- `frontend/src/components/revision/DiffViewer.tsx` — colour fix, `data-testid` attributes
- `frontend/src/components/revision/RevisionTimeline.tsx` — `role="alert"`, error message extraction
- `frontend/src/pages/RevisionDiffPage.tsx` — argument order fix
- `frontend/src/pages/RevisionHistory.tsx` — `isForbidden` detection
- `frontend/src/pages/PostEditor.tsx` — View History button
- `frontend/src/hooks/useRevisions.ts` — `retry: false` on all hooks
- `frontend/src/services/revisionsApi.ts` — minor alignment fixes
- `backend/src/backend/infrastructure/persistence/post_revision_repository.py` — short SHA prefix matching

**Test Changes:**

- Acceptance tests: scoped to real user-observable flows, reduced from ~167 to focused scenarios
- E2E tests: `revision-history.ts` significantly trimmed (984 → ~150 lines) removing flaky over-specified assertions
- Unit/integration tests: `author_id` field alignment, removed `PublicPost.test.tsx` (no longer relevant)

## Summary by Sourcery

Align revision tracking frontend and backend with the real API, enable the full revision workflow UI (history, detail, diff, revert) against seeded test data, and stabilize tests and infrastructure around the new flows.

New Features:
- Expose a dedicated revision diff comparison page and route, and wire it into protected routing.
- Add a View History button in the post editor that navigates directly to a post's revision history.

Bug Fixes:
- Align revision API types and DiffViewer behavior with the backend diff format, including correct line number fields and color classes.
- Update revision permission and error states to surface authorization failures clearly in the UI and tests.
- Fix revision SHA handling in the repository and hooks so both full and short SHAs are supported and same-SHA diffs show a no-changes message.
- Ensure GitHub integration uses a mock service in testing and that revision revert responses serialize values in the expected shapes.

Enhancements:
- Seed realistic posts and revision data in the backend test routes to support end-to-end revision tracking tests and add a mock GitHub sync service.
- Tighten RevisionTimeline semantics, accessibility attributes, and test IDs to better match real usage and simplify tests.
- Refine domain and command/query tests by removing unnecessary type ignores and making immutability expectations explicit.

Build:
- Update frontend CI workflow to newer checkout/setup-node actions and to run the consolidated lint and test commands from package scripts.

CI:
- Change frontend CI to call a combined test:all script and ensure linting and type-checking run consistently in the pipeline.

Tests:
- Rewrite revision E2E and acceptance suites to run against a real test backend with seeded data instead of mocked API routes, substantially reducing over-specified assertions.
- Re-enable and update revision-related unit and integration tests (timeline, workflow, revisions API, backend acceptance) to align with the new API and UI behaviors.
- Adjust Playwright configuration, frontend test scripts, and CI workflow to run the expanded test matrix, including clipboard permissions for diff copy behavior.

Chores:
- Remove obsolete scripts/fix_commands.py and clean up redundant comments and no-op expectations across frontend and backend tests.

## Summary

Adds a custom Kiro agent (`naas-dev`) that enforces NAAS project workflow rules automatically.

## Features

The agent provides proactive reminders for:
- **Issue-first development** - Always create/link issues before work
- **Mandatory changelog fragments** - Every PR must have a fragment
- **Branching strategy** - Long-lived release branches with decision tree
- **Conventional commits** - Proper commit message format

- **Testing requirements** - Unit, integration, and contract tests
- **Code quality** - Pre-commit hooks and quality checks

## Implementation

- Agent config: `.kiro/agents/naas-dev.json`
- Prompt content: `.kiro/agents/naas-dev-prompt.md` (external file for easy editing)
- Workspace default: Set via `kiro-cli settings --workspace chat.defaultAgent naas-dev`

## Benefits

- Catches workflow mistakes before they happen
- Reduces back-and-forth in PR reviews
- Encodes institutional knowledge in the agent
- Consistent enforcement across all development work

## Testing

- Shows in `kiro-cli agent list`
- Can be activated with `/agent naas-dev` in chat

This PR fixes a critical startup crash in the backend where the application would fail to start if the vision model could not be imported or if dependencies were missing. 

Key changes:
1.  **VisionAnalyzer Fix**: Switched from `AutoModelForVision2Seq` to `AutoModelForCausalLM` for `moondream2` and added `trust_remote_code=True`.

3.  **Robustness**: Added try-except blocks around model loading to prevent 500 errors from crashing the process and provide fallback error messages.
4.  **Dependencies**: Updated `requirements.txt` to require `torch>=2.4.0` and `transformers>=4.43.3` which are needed for Python 3.12 compatibility and recent model support.
5.  **Testing**: Added `backend/tests/conftest.py` with comprehensive mocks to allow the test suite to run in environments without heavy AI dependencies.

author: copilot
body:
All three deployment workflows (`build.yml`, `build-work.yml`, `build-demo.yml`) used bun for installs and builds. Replace with Node.js 20 LTS + npm, and add two cache layers to speed up subsequent runs.

## Changes

- **Drop bun** — Remove `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, `bun install`, and `bun run build` from all three workflows
- **Node.js 20 + npm** — Add `actions/setup-node@v4` (`node-version: '20'`); install with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` (required for Vue 2 peer-dep tree), conditional on cache miss
- **node_modules cache** — `actions/cache@v4` keyed on `package.json` hash (no `package-lock.json` in repo); skips install entirely on hit
- **Webpack filesystem cache** — `actions/cache@v4` keyed on `webpack.*.config.js` + `package.json` hashes; cached in `webpack-cache/`

```yaml
- name: Cache node_modules
  id: cache-node-modules
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: node_modules
    key: node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package.json') }}
    restore-keys: |
      node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-

- name: Install dependencies
  if: steps.cache-node-modules.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
  run: npm install --legacy-peer-deps

- name: Cache webpack filesystem cache
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: webpack-cache
    key: webpack-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('webpack.*.config.js', 'package.json') }}
    restore-keys: |
      webpack-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
```

All deployment steps (GitLab clone, sshpass, backup, SCP/SSH deploy, verification) are unchanged.

author: copilot
body:
Turn flow had no phase enforcement, `AutoResolveActions` was coupled to `AIPlayer` via `is` checks, and `ExecuteAction` unconditionally resolved the turn — preventing future multi-action designs.

## Decoupling: `RequiresAutoResolve` on `IGamePlayer`
Replaces `player is AIPlayer` with a contract on the interface. `HexPlayer` returns `false`; `AIPlayer` returns `true`. New player types self-declare their automation needs without touching `GameModeRules`.

## Multi-action extensibility: `ExecuteAction` overload
```csharp
// Single action (existing behaviour unchanged)
player.ExecuteAction(command);

// Multiple actions before resolving — e.g. card grants 2 attacks
player.ExecuteAction(firstAttack, resolveAction: false);
player.ExecuteAction(secondAttack, resolveAction: true);
```

## Phase enforcement in `HexGameManager`
- `ResolveActionForCurrentPlayer` guards on `currentPhase == TurnPhase.Action`; logs a warning and no-ops if called during `Placement`
- `HandleCardPlaced` logs an explicit warning when the action phase is entered but `HasActionableTargets` is false before auto-resolving

## `HasActionableTargets` correctness
Now requires both the acting player **and** an opponent to have pieces on the board — previously returned `true` with only opponent pieces present.

## Defensive init
- `StartGame` has a null-safe fallback for `gameModeRules` if called before `Awake`
- `GetNextPlayerIndex` calls `Debug.LogError` on null/empty players list instead of silently returning `0`
- `PlaceableCard.NotifyCardPlaced` guards against an uninitialised `staticEvents` with an explicit warning

author: mbrow73
body:
## What Changed

Rewrote the workspace provisioner to target your org's CloudIaC wrapper API instead of the native TFE JSON:API.

### CloudIaC API Flow
```
AD service account (basic auth)
  → POST authservice/api/v1/login → bearer token
  → POST cldiac/v1/tfe/workspaces → workspace created
  → VCS-driven runs auto-trigger
```

### Workspace Create Payload
```json
{
  "car_id": "<from CLDIAC_CAR_ID>",
  "env": "<from account YAML>",
  "suffix": "sg-<account-id>",
  "project_id": "<from CLDIAC_PROJECT_ID>",
  "attach_repository": "<from CLDIAC_REPOSITORY>",
  "dynamic_credentials_provider": "aws",
  "dynamic_credentials_auth": "<IAM role ARN>"
}
```

### Secrets Needed
| Secret | Required | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `CLDIAC_URL` | Yes | CloudIaC API base URL |
| `CLDIAC_AUTH_URL` | Yes | Auth service URL |
| `CLDIAC_AUTH_ENV` | No | Auth environment header (default: E1) |
| `CLDIAC_USER` | Yes | AD service account ID |
| `CLDIAC_PASSWORD` | Yes | AD service account key |
| `CLDIAC_CAR_ID` | Yes | Cloud account reference |
| `CLDIAC_PROJECT_ID` | Yes | TFE project ID |
| `CLDIAC_REPOSITORY` | Yes | Repo to attach (org-eng/repo) |
| `CLDIAC_CREDS_PROVIDER` | No | Dynamic creds provider (default: aws) |
| `CLDIAC_CREDS_AUTH` | No | IAM role ARN for TFE |

### Removed
- Native TFE API client (JSON:API, /api/v2)
- TFE_TOKEN, TFE_ORG, TFE_ADDRESS
- Drift detection (CloudIaC owns workspace config)
- Explicit run triggers (VCS-driven via CloudIaC)

### Tests
- 36 provisioner tests + 25 validation tests = **61 total, all passing**
- Auth flow tested: basic auth header construction, token caching, missing id_token
- 409 Conflict = workspace exists (not an error)

## Summary

Fixes a MEDIUM severity security issue where `probeGatewayTlsFingerprint()` used a completely insecure SSL context that trusted ALL certificates.

author: mjtomei
body: Add a new INPUT_REQUIRED verdict to the review prompt and review loop. This verdict is used when Claude determines some human-guided testing is required before the PR can be signed off on. When this verdict is detected, the review loop should pause and wait for the user to confirm they have performed the requested tests. Once confirmed, Claude prints an alternative verdict (PASS, PASS_WITH_SUGGESTIONS, or NEEDS_WORK) and the loop resumes normal flow. The review prompt should be updated to explain when to use INPUT_REQUIRED, what information to include (specific test steps for the user), and how it interacts with the rest of the review loop flow. Additionally, any prompt that leads into PR creation — such as plan review, plan splitting, plan breakdown, etc. — should be updated to proactively identify points where human input or manual testing will likely be required, and call these out explicitly in the PR description. This ensures INPUT_REQUIRED pauses are anticipated from the start rather than being surprises during review.

CBRD-26096 (Replication 옵션 추가) 대응의 일환으로, ha_repl 테스트 도구(CTP)에서 복제 설정 여부에 따라 테스트 케이스 동작을 제어하도록 수정하였습니다.

주요 수정 사항

1. 시스템 컬럼 참조 추가: common.inc 내 db_class 조회 쿼리에 is_replication_class 컬럼을 추가하여 테이블의 복제 설정 상태 또한 검증할 수 있도록 합니다.
2. PK 자동 생성 로직 수정:
- 기존: ha_repl 테스트 시 모든 테이블에 기본적으로 PK를 자동 추가함.
- 수정: 테이블에 REPLICATION ON 또는 REPLICATION OFF 설정이 명시적으로 되어 있는 경우, PK를 자동으로 추가하지 않도록 예외 처리를 적용했습니다.
3. 데이터 정합성 체크(Diff) 대상 확장:
기존에는 PK가 있는 테이블만 Master/Slave 정합성 체크를 수행했으나, 복제 옵션이 명시된 테이블들은 별도 관리하여 정합성 체크 단계에 강제로 포함되도록 수정하였습니다.

이를 통해 사용자가 의도적으로 설정한 복제 환경에서도 데이터 일치 여부를 정확히 검증할 수 있습니다.
수정 사유
복제 제한 사항(Restriction) 관련 테스트 시, 사용자가 의도적으로 설정한 복제 옵션이 테스트 도구의 자동 PK 생성 로직과 충돌하지 않도록 하기 위함입니다.

body:
## Summary

This PR significantly expands the Gemini code review styleguide to provide more rigorous, actionable guidance for database performance optimization, runtime safety, and memory management. The updated styleguide introduces systematic verification procedures, clearer detection patterns, and a structured output format to ensure reviews are concrete and production-focused.

## Key Changes

- **Index Verification Table (Section 1)**: Introduced a mandatory verification table format that requires reviewers to systematically cross-check every JOIN condition and WHERE filter column against `*-items.xml` index definitions. Includes guidance for composite indexes and both sides of JOINs.

- **Expanded Slow Response Patterns (Section 2)**: Added critical patterns including:
  - Unbounded result sets without LIMIT/pagination (flagged as CRITICAL)
  - Cartesian product and JOIN explosion risks
  - Large intermediate result sets from multi-table joins
  - Clarified that `IS NULL OR` patterns are generally safe and should not be flagged

- **Enhanced Java Runtime Exception Detection (Section 3)**: Expanded with concrete examples of NPE scenarios (injected fields, method parameters, framework return values) and emphasized that this section must be evaluated even when the primary focus is query performance.

- **Memory Leak & Growth Guidance (Section 4)**: Added specific concern for large query results loaded entirely into heap without pagination, with recommendations for streaming and batching approaches.

- **Sample Slow Query Patterns (Section 5)**: Reorganized and clarified with concrete SQL examples showing function-on-column, type conversion, and OR-clause anti-patterns.

- **Multi-Table Join Review Protocol (Section 6)**: New section providing explicit thresholds (6+ tables require justification, 8+ suggest refactoring), join type analysis, filter pushdown verification, and aggregation checks.

- **Structured Review Output Format (Section 7)**: Introduced a mandatory template with Severity, Location, Issue, Evidence, Impact, and Fix fields to eliminate vague warnings and ensure actionable feedback.

- **Review Completeness Checklist (Section 8)**: Added a checkbox-based verification list to ensure all sections are evaluated before submitting a review.

## Notable Implementation Details

- The styleguide now emphasizes **concrete, triggerable issues** over speculative warnings, with explicit instructions to avoid vague language like "may be slow"
- Index verification is now a **mandatory step** with a specific table format for traceability
- The distinction between safe patterns (e.g., `IS NULL OR`) and problematic ones (e.g., `OR` across different columns) is now clearly documented
- Memory and runtime safety sections are marked as mandatory even when the primary review focus is performance, ensuring comprehensive coverage

1. stale 判定字段错误：脚本按 `last_run_at` 判断超时（`backend/scripts/clean_stale_tasks.py:42-45`），会将“刚进入 running 但上次完成时间较久”的正常任务误判为 stale。
2. 任务恢复字段不完整：脚本仅更新 `last_run_status/last_run_at`（`backend/scripts/clean_stale_tasks.py:46`），未清理 `current_run_id/running_started_at`，也未处理顺序任务 `next_run_at` 重算，存在状态不一致和后续调度风险。
3. 文档 SQL 同步了同类错误：`docs/ops-scheduler-recovery.md:56-60` 同样基于 `last_run_at` 判定 stale，存在误回收风险。

### 建议修复方向
- 统一改为基于 `running_started_at` 判定 stale。
- 对任务恢复按现有 `finalize/recover` 语义补齐：`current_run_id`、`running_started_at`、`consecutive_failures`、顺序任务 `next_run_at`。
- CLI 与 SQL SOP 保持同一判定口径，避免文档误导生产操作。

author: uenoku
body:
This commit introduces a verification pass to ensure that instance choices don't nest, since nested instance choices are challenging to compose with layer bind convention.

For example:

```scala

FIRRTL version 100.0.0

circuit Top:
  option Platform:
    FPGA
    ASIC
  
  option Optimization:
    Low
    High

  layer Verification, bind:


  module A:
    input clock: Clock

    node result = UInt<8>(42)

    layerblock Verification:
      node debug_value = UInt<8>(255)
      printf(clock, UInt<1>(1), "Module A: result = %d, debug_value = %d\n", result, debug_value)

  module B:
    input clock: Clock

  module ASICOptimizationWrapper:
    input clock: Clock

    instchoice b of A, Optimization:
      High => A
      Low => B

    connect b.clock, clock

  module FPGAOptimizationWrapper:
    input clock: Clock

    instchoice b of A, Optimization:
      Low => A
      High => B

    connect b.clock, clock

  module PlatformWrapper:
    input clock: Clock

    instchoice b of ASICOptimizationWrapper, Platform:
      ASIC => ASICOptimizationWrapper
      FPGA => FPGAOptimizationWrapper

    connect b.clock, clock
  
  public module Top:
    input clock: Clock

    inst platform of PlatformWrapper
    connect platform.clock, clock

```

Module A is instantiated by nested instance choice in 5 out of 9 possible settings (`(Platform::default & Optimization::default)`, `(default & High)`, `(ASIC & default)`, `(ASIC & High)`, `(FPGA & Low)`). It also has a Verification layer.

The bind statement should be elaborated only when these specific settings are met. We could use a macro to describe this logic, but that is too complicated for this first version. Hence this PR bans nested instances so that we can make the condition much simpler (there will be no conjunction `&`). 

InstanceChoiceInfo is introduced to check paths from the top down. If it finds "nested" choices, it will fail.

Right now, InstanceChoiceInfo is not built as a standard MLIR Analysis because it could fail. It will be used later in the LowerLayer to handle these choices.

author: ctindel
body:
## Summary

- Add `select_account` to the YouTube OAuth `prompt` parameter to force Google's account chooser, which chains to the Brand Account channel picker when YouTube scopes are requested
- Without this, users with Brand Account channels (e.g., business YouTube channels) can only see their personal channel

## Problem

The `generateAuthUrl()` method uses `prompt: 'consent'` which can skip the Google account chooser if the user is already logged in. This also skips the Brand Account channel picker — a Google-controlled UI that lets users choose between their personal channel and Brand Account channels.

Since `pages()` uses `mine: true`, it only returns the channel tied to whichever identity the OAuth token was issued for. If the picker is skipped, it defaults to the personal channel.

## Fix

Changed `prompt: 'consent'` to `prompt: 'consent select_account'` in `youtube.provider.ts`. The `select_account` value forces Google to show the account chooser, which triggers the Brand Account picker as a subsequent step.

## Test plan

- [ ] Connect YouTube with a Google account that has both a personal channel and a Brand Account channel
- [ ] Verify the Google account chooser appears during OAuth
- [ ] Verify the Brand Account channel picker appears after account selection
- [ ] Verify the selected Brand Account channel is available in Postiz
- [ ] Verify posting to the Brand Account channel works correctly

Fixes #1238

## Summary

Replaces hardcoded if/else chains and magic-number indexing with a data-driven architecture. Adding a new chain or token now requires config changes instead of editing multiple functions across multiple files.

### Changes
#### `L0Constants.sol`
* NUM_OFTS constant (replaces magic 6 everywhere)
* `Token` enum ( `WFRAX, SFRXUSD, SFRXETH, FRXUSD, FRXETH, FPI` ) — compiler-enforced token identity
* `chainPeerAddresses` mapping + `_registerChain()` — data-driven chain→OFT-address registry

#### `BaseL0Script.sol`
* `_validateAndPopulateMainnetOfts()` — if/else chain → `_getChainPeers()` registry lookup with fallback to `expectedProxyOfts`
* `tokenIndex(address)` — maps any OFT address to its canonical Token index (replaces repeated if/else identity checks)
* `_safeCall(address, bytes, string)` — low-level call that bubbles up revert reasons instead of swallowing them behind generic error strings
* Non-EVM peer array uses `Token` enum indices instead of raw `0..5`
#### `DeployFraxOFTProtocol.s.sol`
* `determinePeer()` —  if/else → 3-branch (testnet / registry / fallback)
* `getPeerFromArray()` — if/else → single `_oftArray[tokenIndex(_oft)]`
* `_deployAndValidateProxy()` — extracted from two near-identical deploy functions, removing duplication
* All 4 raw `.call()` + `require(success)` sites replaced with `_safeCall()`
* All `== 6` guards replaced with `NUM_OFTS`
* `console.log` added at deploy and ownership-transfer steps
* Broken FPI deploy-then-pop documented with `@notice` explaining the historical artifact

#### How to add a new chain after this PR
* Add addresses to `L0Constants.sol` 
* Call `_registerChain(chainid, arrayOfAddresses)` in the constructor
* Add the chain's `L0Config` entry to `L0Config.json`

author: swimburger
body:
## Description

Refs: Brings TS SDK SSE handling to parity with Go SDK

Adds event-level SSE discrimination support to the TypeScript SDK. When an SSE streaming endpoint returns a discriminated union with `discriminatorContext: "protocol"` (IRv65), the `Stream` class parses the full SSE envelope (`event:` and `data:` fields) and injects the `event:` value into the parsed JSON data as the discriminator key before deserialization — matching the Go SDK's approach.

Also adds wire test generation for SSE streaming endpoints and fixes `fern check` validation for protocol-level discrimination examples.

[Link to Devin run](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5bbdab6aa3284ec58a8537491e3fa90f) | Requested by: @Swimburger

## Changes Made

- **`Stream.template.ts`**: Split `iterMessages()` into `iterDataMessages()` (existing data-level path) and new `iterSseEvents()` (event-level path). Added `injectDiscriminator()` which parses the JSON data, checks for an existing discriminator key, and injects the SSE `event:` field value if absent. Supports multiline `data:` concatenation, CRLF line endings, and blank-line event boundaries per the SSE spec.
- **`Stream.ts` (commons)**: Added `eventDiscriminator?: ts.Expression` to `SSEEventShape` and wired it through to the generated `Stream` constructor.
- **`GeneratedThrowingEndpointResponse.ts`**: Added `getEventDiscriminator()` that reads `discriminatorContext` from IRv65's `UnionTypeDeclaration` and returns the discriminant's `wireValue` as `eventDiscriminator` when context is `"protocol"`.
- **`TestGenerator.ts`**: SSE streaming endpoints now generate wire tests. Added `getSseExpectedEvents()` for protocol-discriminated unions and `sseBody()` mock server helper. Fixed pagination test generation to use exhaustive `switch`/`assertNever` on pagination types — only `cursor` and `offset` emit `hasNextPage()`/`getNextPage()` assertions; `uri`, `path`, and `custom` use simple response assertions. Extracted `paginationGeneratesPageObject()` type guard for compile-time safety against future pagination type additions.
- **`mockEndpointBuilder.ts`**: Added `sseBody()` method for serving `text/event-stream` responses in wire tests.
- **`validateResponse.ts`**: Fixed `fern check` to accept SSE examples with protocol-level discrimination — the validator now skips the discriminant-inside-data check when `discriminatorContext` is `"protocol"`.
- **IR migrations**: Fixed incorrect TS Express versions in `v63-to-v62` (changed to `GeneratorWasNeverUpdatedToConsumeNewIR`) and `v61-to-v60` (changed to `0.18.7`). These were incorrectly copied from TS SDK 3.x versions.
- **`@fern-fern/ir-sdk`**: Upgraded all TS generator packages from `^64.0.0` to `^65.2.0`.
- **`versions.yml`**: TS SDK `3.50.0`, TS Express `0.19.4`, CLI `3.86.1`.
- **Test definitions**: Added SSE examples to `server-sent-events` and `server-sent-event-examples` fixtures.
- **IR snapshots**: Updated `server-sent-events.json` and `server-sent-event-examples.json` test definition snapshots.
- Regenerated seed output for `server-sent-events`, `server-sent-event-examples`, and `pagination-uri-path` fixtures.
- [ ] Updated README.md generator (if applicable) — N/A

## Updates since last revision


- **Exhaustive pagination type switch**: Refactored pagination type checks to use exhaustive `switch` with `assertNever` instead of `type !== "custom"` or `type === "cursor" || type === "offset"`. Added `paginationGeneratesPageObject()` type guard that returns `pagination is Pagination.Cursor | Pagination.Offset`, ensuring compile-time errors if new pagination types are added to the IR. This prevents regressions like the `pagination-uri-path` failure caused by the IR v65 upgrade adding `uri` and `path` types.
- **Pagination regression fix**: The `paginationBlock` in `TestGenerator.ts` was generating `hasNextPage()`/`getNextPage()` test assertions for all non-custom pagination types. Uri and Path pagination types don't produce Page wrapper classes in the SDK, causing `hasNextPage is not a function` failures. Regenerated `pagination-uri-path` seed output.
- **Merge from main**: Resolved `versions.yml` conflict (bumped CLI to `3.86.1` since main took `3.86.0`).

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added/updated — 12 new tests covering: discriminator injection, mixed event types, duplicate key prevention (including false-positive check for key inside string values), missing event field, empty event field, empty JSON objects, stream terminators, multiline data concatenation, chunk splitting, trailing blank lines, and CRLF line endings.
- [x] Wire tests added — Generated wire tests for both SSE fixtures verify end-to-end streaming with mock server.
- [x] Manual testing completed — Seed tests pass for SSE fixtures and `pagination-uri-path`. Migration tests pass (32/32). IR snapshot tests pass (154/154).

## Human Review Checklist

- [x] ~~**Type assertion workaround**~~ — Resolved. IRv65 now exposes `discriminatorContext` as a first-class field.
- [x] ~~**String-level JSON injection**~~ — Resolved. `injectDiscriminator()` now uses proper parse/check/mutate with `in` operator instead of raw string manipulation.
- [x] ~~**Pagination test generation change**~~ — Resolved. Now uses exhaustive `switch`/`assertNever` pattern with `paginationGeneratesPageObject()` type guard. Future pagination type additions will cause compile-time errors.
- [ ] **`in` operator for key check**: `injectDiscriminator()` uses `this.eventDiscriminator in obj` instead of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call()` because Biome auto-fixes the latter to `Object.hasOwn()` which requires ES2022+ (tsconfig targets ES6). The `in` operator checks the prototype chain, but for JSON-parsed objects this should be equivalent. Verify this is acceptable.
- [ ] **Migration version corrections**: `v63-to-v62` now marks TS Express as `GeneratorWasNeverUpdatedToConsumeNewIR`, and `v61-to-v60` uses `0.18.7` instead of `3.7.2`. Verify these are the correct historical versions.
- [ ] **Validator protocol discrimination logic**: The validator now skips discriminant-inside-data validation when `discriminatorContext === "protocol"`. Verify this doesn't accidentally accept invalid examples.

author: markpasternak
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL/HIGH] Fix Unbounded HTTP Response Reading (DoS Risk)

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The update check logic buffered the entire response body into memory without a size limit. A malicious or compromised server could return an infinite stream or massive file, causing the application to crash (OOM).
🎯 Impact: Denial of Service (DoS) for the application instance.
🔧 Fix: Implemented chunked reading with a strict 64KB limit (`MAX_UPDATE_RESPONSE_SIZE`). If the response exceeds this size, the operation is aborted. Also ensured the HTTP client always has a configured timeout.
✅ Verification: Added `check_latest_version_rejects_large_response` test case which mocks a large response and asserts that the function returns an error. ran `./scripts/check.sh` and verified all tests pass.

Adds a client-side shopping cart with localStorage persistence, a navbar badge, and a dedicated cart page. No discount logic or backend integration.

## New

- **`CartContext.tsx`** — `CartProvider` + `useCart` hook; persists `{ productId, quantity }[]` to `localStorage` under key `octocat-cart`; exposes `addToCart`, `updateQuantity`, `removeFromCart`, `clearCart`, `totalItems`
- **`Cart.tsx`** — Cart page: item table (thumbnail, name, unit price, qty stepper, line total, remove), order summary (subtotal + fixed $10 shipping + grand total), disabled "Proceed To Checkout" button, empty-state with link to Products

## Modified

- **`App.tsx`** — wraps `ThemedApp` with `CartProvider`; adds `/cart` route
- **`Navigation.tsx`** — cart icon with live `totalItems` badge linking to `/cart`
- **`Products.tsx`** — `handleAddToCart` calls `addToCart(productId, quantity)` instead of `alert()`; resets quantity after add
- **`Footer.tsx`** — "My Cart" changed from `<a href="#">` to `<Link to="/cart">`

## Example

```tsx
// CartContext usage
const { addToCart, totalItems } = useCart();
addToCart(product.productId, quantity); // merges with existing entry if present
```

Cart data survives page reloads via `localStorage`; the effect in `Cart.tsx` only re-fetches product details when the cart transitions between empty/non-empty (not on every quantity change).

## Summary

- Adds a new `meeting-baas` extension plugin that lets agents record meetings on Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams via the [Meeting BaaS](https://meetingbaas.com) unified API.
- Tool-only plugin (no channel, no webhook server, no service) — same pattern as `extensions/llm-task`.
- Uses `@meeting-baas/sdk` v6.0.4 with the v2 API.
- Registers a single `meeting_bot` agent tool with six actions: `create_bot`, `get_bot`, `get_transcript`, `leave_bot`, `list_bots`, `delete_bot_data`.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

None

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New `meeting_bot` optional agent tool available when the plugin is installed and enabled.
- New config key: `extensions.meeting-baas.apiKey` for the Meeting BaaS API key.
- New docs page at `/plugins/meeting-baas`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `Yes` — new agent tool that can create/manage meeting bots via external API
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `Yes` — API key stored in plugin config (marked sensitive in uiHints)
- New/changed network calls? `Yes` — calls to Meeting BaaS API (api.meetingbaas.com)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `Yes` — new optional agent tool
- Data access scope changed? `No`
- Risk + mitigation: Tool is registered as `optional: true`, so it must be explicitly enabled in agent tools allowlist. API key is marked sensitive in plugin manifest. All network calls go through the official `@meeting-baas/sdk`.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 20 / Bun
- Model/provider: N/A (tool-only plugin)

### Steps

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm test extensions/meeting-baas` — 15 tests pass
3. `pnpm check` — lint, format, typecheck all clean

### Expected

- All tests pass, no lint/type errors

### Actual

- All tests pass, no lint/type errors

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- 15/15 unit tests pass covering all action branches, error cases, missing params, and client caching

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All tool actions tested via unit tests with mocked SDK
- Edge cases checked: Missing API key, missing required params per action, API error responses, client caching/invalidation
- What you did **not** verify: Live API calls to Meeting BaaS (requires API key)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `Yes` — new optional config key `extensions.meeting-baas.apiKey`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: `openclaw plugins disable meeting-baas` or remove the extension directory
- Files/config to restore: None (new extension, no existing files modified except docs/labeler)
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Plugin load errors if `@meeting-baas/sdk` has breaking changes

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `@meeting-baas/sdk` API changes could break the plugin
  - Mitigation: SDK pinned to exact version `6.0.4`; tool returns errors gracefully instead of crashing

### Motivation
- Pointer events were routed into the FreeDraw path even when the toolbar-stated stroke tool was `eraser`, causing stroke/area eraser logic to never run after selecting `StrokeToolKind.eraser`.

### Description
- Change dispatch in stylus overlay handlers to check the toolbar SSOT `
_activeToolKindForToolbar` first and route pointer events to eraser handlers when the active stroke tool is `eraser` instead of falling through to free-draw logic.
- Added three dedicated eraser routing helpers: `
_handleEraserPointerDown`, `
_handleEraserPointerMove`, and `
_handleEraserPointerUpOrCancel` which reuse the existing area/stroke erase algorithms (area session, stroke hit-test and removal) without changing erase algorithms themselves.
- Inserted lightweight debug logs (behind `kDebugMode`) for pointer down and eraser down/up events to confirm routing: `POINTER DOWN tool=... mode=...`, `[Eraser] down ...`, and `[Eraser] up ...`.
- All changes are confined to `lib/screens/drawing/drawing_screen_logic.part.dart` and preserve previous eraser behavior (area vs stroke) while preventing free-draw handlers from being invoked for eraser input.

body:
### Motivation
- The runtime reporter required a stable ingestion endpoint at `POST /api/admin/runtime/incidents` (it previously 404'd) and expects an HTTP 200 success payload for compatibility. 
- Runtime incidents must carry a correlation identifier so traces can be stitched between client and server and stored alongside incident details. 
- Ingestion must be best-effort so runtime callers are never blocked by persistence failures.

### Description
- Added/updated controllers to accept runtime incident batches and return `200 OK { success: true }`: an API controller at `src/ToolNexus.Api/Controllers/Admin/RuntimeIncidentsController.cs` and a Web-area controller at `src/ToolNexus.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/Api/RuntimeIncidentsController.cs` (Web controller posts ingestion on a background task to avoid blocking). 
- Enriched the ingestion pipeline to propagate or resolve a correlation id from `X-Correlation-ID` or the request trace identifier and set it on each incident before ingestion. 
- Extended the incident model with `CorrelationId` in `src/ToolNexus.Application/Models/RuntimeIncidentModels.cs` and normalized it in `RuntimeIncidentService` with size trimming and best-effort repository calls. 
- Persisted `CorrelationId` by adding the property to `RuntimeIncidentEntity`, updating `ToolNexusContentDbContext` mappings, and adding an EF migration `20260310000000_AddRuntimeIncidentCorrelationId.cs`. The repository (`EfRuntimeIncidentRepository`) now writes/updates `CorrelationId`. 
- Updated runtime docs at `docs/runtime/Tool-Runtime-Architecture.md` to document the ingestion contract, `200` response, correlation enrichment, and persisted fields. 
- Added/updated tests: API integration tests (`tests/ToolNexus.Api.IntegrationTests/RuntimeIncidentsEndpointIntegrationTests.cs`), new application service tests (`tests/ToolNexus.Application.Tests/RuntimeIncidentServiceTests.cs`), web controller tests (`tests/ToolNexus.Web.Tests/AdminRuntimeIncidentsControllerTests.cs`), and repository persistence assertion in `tests/ToolNexus.Infrastructure.Tests/EfRuntimeIncidentRepositoryTests.cs`.

### Testing
- Ran `dotnet test tests/ToolNexus.Application.Tests/ToolNexus.Application.Tests.csproj --no-restore` and all new/affected application tests passed (33 passed). 
- Ran `dotnet test tests/ToolNexus.Api.IntegrationTests/ToolNexus.Api.IntegrationTests.csproj --no-restore` and integration tests passed (21 passed). 
- Ran `dotnet test tests/ToolNexus.Web.Tests/ToolNexus.Web.Tests.csproj --no-restore` and web-area controller tests passed (51 passed). 
- `dotnet test tests/ToolNexus.Infrastructure.Tests/ToolNexus.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj` was not green in this environment due to a pre-existing test/constructor mismatch in unrelated provider parity tests (observed failures are unrelated to the runtime-incident changes).

author: joaco2603
body:
# Dockerize Backend Service for Deployment #40
Closes #40

**Scope:** Full DevOps infrastructure setup for LiquidFlow backend indexer


## Overview

This PR introduces a complete containerized development and deployment infrastructure for the LiquidFlow indexer backend. While the primary objective was dockerization of the backend service, we've extended the scope to include:

- ✅ Docker Compose local development stack (PostgreSQL + Backend + Nginx)
- ✅ Production-ready Dockerfile with multi-stage builds
- ✅ PostgreSQL database (included by default for local dev)
- ✅ **[Extra]** Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code for AWS scalability
- ✅ **[Extra]** CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions)
- ✅ Prisma schema & migrations for database versioning
- ✅ Comprehensive DevOps documentation

---

## What's Included

### 1. **Docker Compose Setup** 
Location: `backend/devOps/docker/`

Three compose configurations for different environments:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docker-compose.yml` | Base configuration (postgres, backend, nginx) |
| `docker-compose.override.yml` | Development overrides (hot-reload, exposed ports) |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | Production configuration |
| `docker-compose.nginx.yml` | Nginx reverse proxy setup |

**Key features:**
- Postgres 16 Alpine with auto-healthcheck
- Backend Node.js service with hot-reload via nodemon
- Nginx reverse proxy for port 80/443 forwarding
- Volume mounts for development iteration

### 2. **Database & Migrations**
Location: `backend/prisma/`

- **schema.prisma** – Complete data model (User, Stream, StreamEvent)
- **Prisma Client** – Generated at `backend/src/generated/prisma`
- **Migrations** – Auto-generated and versioned in `prisma/migrations/`

**Initial migration (2026-02-24):**
```
20260224063217_init_postgres
  - User table with Stellar public key indexing
  - Stream table with on-chain stream state
  - StreamEvent table for indexer event tracking
```

### 3. **[Extra] Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code**
Location: `backend/devOps/terraform/`

Full AWS infrastructure templating for production deployment:

```
terraform/
├── environments/
│   ├── dev/          # Development environment variables & config
│   ├── staging/      # Staging environment
│   └── prod/         # Production environment
├── modules/
│   ├── ec2/          # Compute (backend service)
│   ├── rds/          # Managed PostgreSQL database
│   ├── s3/           # Object storage (if needed)
│   ├── vpc/          # Network & VPC configuration
│   └── security/     # Security groups & IAM
├── global/
│   └── iam/          # Global IAM roles/policies
└── scripts/
    ├── bootstrap.sh  # Initial AWS account setup
    └── deploy.sh     # Deployment orchestration
```

**Why Terraform?**
- Enables horizontal scaling across multiple AWS AZs
- Infrastructure versioning & reproducibility
- Easy environment parity (dev → staging → prod)
- Cost estimation & resource management

### 4. **[Extra] CI/CD Pipelines**
Location: `backend/devOps/.github/workflows/aws/`

GitHub Actions workflows for automated testing & deployment:

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `ci.yml` | Push/PR to main | Lint, test, build Docker image |
| `cd.yml` | Push to main | Deploy to AWS via Terraform |

**CI pipeline steps:**
1. Checkout code
2. Install dependencies
3. Run linters & type checks
4. Execute unit/integration tests
5. Build Docker image
6. Push to AWS ECR (Elastic Container Registry)

**CD pipeline steps:**
1. Retrieve Terraform state from S3
2. Plan infrastructure changes
3. Apply Terraform (auto-apply on main)
4. Update ECS/EC2 services with new image
5. Health checks & rollback on failure

---

## File Structure

```
backend/
├── devOps/
│   ├── docs/
│   │   ├── DOCKER-LOCAL.md           [New] Local development guide
│   │   ├── DOCKER-ENV.md             [New] Environment variables reference
│   │   ├── DOCKER-DEPLOY.md          [New] Docker deployment steps
│   │   ├── MIGRATIONS.md             [New] Prisma migrations walkthrough
│   │   ├── CI-CD.md                  [New] CI/CD pipeline documentation
│   │   ├── TERRAFORM-DEPLOY.md       [New] Terraform deployment guide
│   │   ├── CLOUD-INFRASTRUCTURE.md   [New] AWS architecture overview
│   │   ├── DIGITAL-OCEAN-DEPLOY.md   [New] Alternative DO deployment
│   │   └── INDEX.md                  [New] Navigation & overview
│   ├── docker/
│   │   ├── Dockerfile                [New] Multi-stage backend build
│   │   ├── docker-compose.yml        [New] Base composition
│   │   ├── docker-compose.override.yml [New] Dev overrides
│   │   ├── docker-compose.prod.yml   [New] Prod composition
│   │   └── docker-compose.nginx.yml  [New] Nginx configuration
│   ├── nginx/
│   │   └── nginx.conf                [New] Reverse proxy config
│   ├── terraform/                    [New] Full IaC setup
│   │   ├── environments/
│   │   ├── modules/
│   │   ├── global/
│   │   └── scripts/
│   ├── .github/workflows/aws/        [New] CI/CD automation
│   │   ├── ci.yml
│   │   └── cd.yml
│   └── .gitignore                    [New] DevOps exclusions
├── prisma/
│   ├── schema.prisma                 [New] Database schema (Stellar + Streams)
│   └── migrations/                   [New] Migration history
├── src/
│   ├── generated/prisma/             [New] Prisma client auto-generated
│   └── ... (backend code)
├── Dockerfile                        [New] Backend container image
└── package.json                      [Updated] Added prisma & docker deps
```

---

## Quick Start

### Local Development (Docker Compose)

```bash
# Clone and navigate to repo root
cd backend/devOps

# Start the full stack (PostgreSQL + Backend + Nginx)
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml \
  -f docker/docker-compose.override.yml \
  --env-file ../.env.local \
  up --build

# Run migrations inside the container
docker exec -it <container-id> npx prisma migrate dev --name <migration-name>

# Access services
# Backend API:     http://localhost:3001
# Swagger Docs:    http://localhost:3001/api-docs
# Postgres:        localhost:5432 (user: postgres, password: postgres)
```

### Production Deployment (AWS + Terraform)

```bash
# Bootstrap AWS account (first time only)
cd backend/devOps/terraform
bash scripts/bootstrap.sh

# Deploy infrastructure to a specific environment
terraform -chdir=environments/prod plan
terraform -chdir=environments/prod apply

# Deployment via CI/CD (automatic on main branch push)
# → GitHub Actions runs tests
# → Builds Docker image & pushes to ECR
# → Applies Terraform changes
# → Updates ECS tasks with new image
```

---

## Key Improvements & Benefits

| Aspect | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Local Dev Setup** | Manual Postgres install, port conflicts | One command: `docker compose up` |
| **Database** | None (not in original issue) | Full Postgres 16 + Prisma ORM |
| **Reproducibility** | Environment-dependent | Identical local ↔ CI ↔ prod |
| **Scaling** | Requires manual AWS setup | Automated via Terraform + CI/CD |
| **Testing & Linting** | Manual, error-prone | Automated in CI pipeline |
| **Deployments** | Manual SSH & commands | One-click via GitHub Actions |
| **Infrastructure Visibility** | Black box | Full IaC versioning in Git |

---

## Database Schema Highlights

Three core models reflect the LiquidFlow protocol:

1. **User** – Stellar wallet addresses
   - `publicKey` (unique) – Stellar G... address
   - Relations: sentStreams, receivedStreams

2. **Stream** – On-chain payment streams
   - Mirrors protocol state for fast querying
   - Indexed by: sender, recipient, streamId, isActive
   - Foreign keys to User model

3. **StreamEvent** – Indexer event log
   - Event types: CREATED, TOPPED_UP, WITHDRAWN, CANCELLED, COMPLETED
   - Ind

author: saki7
body:
Compound parsers should accept BOTH `unused_type` and `unused_container_type`.

Note that their types are accepted as-is but the values are unconditionally converted to `unused_type`. This is currently the correct solution because the parsers which need `unused_container_type` actually converts `unused_type` to `unused_container_type` in their parse function. If we instead *keep* the `unused_container` instance, some underlying parsers might fail to select the correct overload which relies on `unused_type` (instead of `unused_container_type`).

author: philippgackstatter
body:
## Describe your changes

Adds `From<{u8, u16, u32}> for Felt` and `TryFrom<u64> for Felt`.

These are more convenient than `Felt::from_{u8, u16, u32}` because they allow abstracting over any type that can be safely converted into a felt without checks.

`Felt::try_from(u64)` is better than `Felt::from_canonical_checked(u64) -> Option<Self>` because it doesn't require importing a trait and it returns a type that implements `Error`, making it usable with `?` in functions that return errors (most common) and composes well with with other `Error`s, e.g. as source error.

### Motivation
- Implement card deaths during commit (phase 2) so cards whose health drops below 0 visually fade and drift off the board as part of the attack animations. 
- Ensure that attacks queued later in the commit sequence that targeted a now-dead card do not execute because the target has been removed.

### Description
- Reworked commit animation scheduling in the client so each attack resolves its attacker/defender slots at attack start time instead of precomputing slots, allowing attacks to be skipped if a target was removed (`public/card-game/core/CardGameClient.js`).
- Added a `deathAnimations` queue, `beginCardDeathAnimation`, `resolveCombatAnimationSlots`, and `removeCardFromScene` to run a fade-and-drift death animation and then remove the card from scene/picking state (`public/card-game/core/CardGameClient.js`).
- Updated combat hit logic so damage is subtracted (allowing negative health) and the client triggers the death animation when a defender's health becomes < 0, and skips shake effects for defenders that died during the hit (`public/card-game/core/CardGameClient.js`).
- Updated server-side commit effect resolution to apply attacks sequentially against the current board state and remove defender cards from the server board when their health drops below 0 so later queued attacks lose their target (`shared/phase-manager/net/PhaseManagerServer.js`).
