author: bodirsky
body: ## :bird: Fallow land implementation :bird: This PR makes fallow land functional in MAgPIE and updates the croparea initialisation to LandInG. When module 29 (cropland) and module 30 (croparea) were split, the fallow implementation used for the FST paper (Bodirsky et al. 2025) was carried over in a non-functional state, so this is largely a bugfix plus the input data required to make it meaningful. Attention: Due to the data update, this changes the default of the model substantially. Parralel development of old and new version is due to madrat data update not possible ## Input data The croparea initialisation now comes from LandInG instead of FAO/LUH. LandInG distinguishes harvested from physical area, which is what makes two things available to the model that were previously invisible: - **fallow land**, where harvested area < physical area - **multiple cropping**, where harvested area > physical area Because `f30_croparea_initialisation` now holds *physical* cropland excluding fallow, both the total croparea and the crop composition differ from previous input revisions. ## GAMS implementation ### Fallow land (`29_cropland/detail_apr24`) Fallow is now driven by a two-tier penalty on *missing* fallow, replacing the single `s29_fallow_target` / `s29_fallow_penalty` pair: ```gams q29_fallow_short(j2)$(s29_fallow_max > 0) .. v29_fallow_short_missing(j2) =g= vm_land(j2,"crop") * s29_fallow_short_threshold - vm_fallow(j2); q29_fallow_long(j2)$(s29_fallow_max > 0) .. v29_fallow_long_missing(j2) =g= vm_land(j2,"crop") * s29_fallow_long_threshold - vm_ q29_fallow_max(j2)$(s29_fallow_max > 0) .. vm_fallow(j2) =l= vm_land(j2,"crop") * s29_fallow_max; ``` Both shortfalls are priced in `q29_cost_cropland`. The marginal cost of removing one hectare of fallow is therefore a step function: | fallow share of cropland | marginal cost of removing 1 ha | |---|---| | >= 0.66 (`s29_fallow_long_threshold`) | 0 | | 0.20 to 0.66 | `s29_fallow_long_penalty` | | < 0.20 (`s29_fallow_short_threshold`) | long + short penalty | Both penalties fade from their start value to `*_target` between `s29_fallow_scenario_start` (2025) and `s29_fallow_scenario_target` (2050), so scenarios can ramp the incentive over time. `s29_fallow_max = 0` is a clean off-switch: it fixes `vm_fallow` and both penalty variables to zero and deactivates all three equations. ### Initialisation consistency Fallow previously started at zero. It is now initialised as the residual of the land initialisation, so that cropland = croparea + fallow + tree cover holds in the base year: ```gams im_fallow_start(j) = max(0, pm_land_hist("y1995",j,"crop") - sum((kcr,w), max(0, fm_croparea("y1995",j,w,kcr))) - pm_treecover_start(j)); ``` The inner `max(0, .)` guards against negative raw `fm_croparea` values; the outer one against croparea plus tree cover exceeding the cropland initialisation, which is possible because they originate from different data sources. `vm_area` is warm-started from `fm_croparea("y1995",...)` in `30_croparea/detail_apr24/preloop.gms`. `im_fallow_start(j)` and `pm_treecover_start(j)` are new interfaces; `29_cropland/simple_apr24` sets both to zero. ### Rotational constraints (`30_croparea/detail_apr24`) The substantive change is the denominator. Constraints are now expressed relative to total cropland instead of the sum of crop areas: ```gams q30_rotation_max(j2,rotamax_red30)$(s30_implementation = 1) .. sum((rota_kcr30(rotamax_red30,kcr),w), vm_area(j2,kcr,w)) =l= vm_land(j2,"crop") * sum((ct, cell(i2,j2)), i30_rotation_rules(ct,i2,rotamax_red30)); ``` With fallow active the two differ, and normalising by croparea would let rotation shares drift as fallow moves. Further changes: - Rules and incentives gain a regional dimension (`i30_rotation_rules(t_all,i,rota30)`) and are faded per country group via `p30_country_weight`, enabling country-differentiated rotation policy. - `i30_implementation` becomes the scalar `s30_implementation` and is no longer forced to rule-based during the historical period. - `q30_rotation_max_irrig` is restricted to the penalty-based case. - The unused bioenergy tree (betr) target and penalty machinery is removed. ### Multiple cropping (`18_residues`, `53_methane`) `f18_multicropping(t_all,i)` is replaced by the cellular, crop- and water-supply-specific `fm_multicropping(t_all,j,w,kcr)`. Aboveground residue biomass and rice CH4 emissions now scale with harvested rather than physical area, which is the counterpart to fallow on the other side of the physical/harvested distinction. ### Soil carbon (`59_som/cellpool_jan23`) Fallow previously borrowed the maize land-use stock change factor. It now has its own (`ch5_F_LU_2019_fallow.csv`), differentiated by climate zone through the new set `climate59moist`: - dry zones: bare fallow, full tillage, low input - moist zones: set-aside, reduced tillage, medium input The initial cropland soil carbon pool now also includes fallow and tree cover. Both enter `q59_som_target_cropland` but were previously missing from initialisation, which left a spurious gap between the initial stock and its own target. ## Changes to the default configuration | Switch | Old | New | |---|---|---| | `croparea` realization | `simple_apr24` | `detail_apr24` | | `s29_fallow_max` | 0 (off) | 0.8 | | `s30_implementation` | 1 (rules) | 0 (penalty) | | `c30_rotation_incentives` | `none` | `default` | | input data | `rev4.132` | `rev4.134cropUp8` | | additional data | `rev4.67` | `rev4.71` | Reference runs will differ from previous versions even where no scenario setting is touched. ## Known limitations MEA behaves strangely. Likely connected to minimum yields in calcFAOYield which is not consistent with production/croparea. Will be fixed in upcoming PRs connected to lpj2magpie ## Results: ### Difference in the default scenario substantially less land expansion compared to runs without land fallow New data fits good to organge data. Exception is India, where fallow might be underestimated by Ostberg (see fallow validation and good match to FAO data) overall level matches good in initialisation (there is no calibration of this level) partly a too fast reduction in fallow (India, Japan, SSA), but still overall OK --> Less tau with pasture (green is new) -->Yields (green is new). Physical yields are higher. --> Cereal areas match well. Croparea diversity: (green is new). Used to look better in FSEC runs. ### Difference between mitigation and NPI, blue and orange are

author: gaborbernat
body:
The monolithic `__init__.py` (~1450 lines) mixed annotation formatting, type hint resolution, docstring injection, numpydoc conversion, and Sphinx setup into a single file. This made it difficult to reason about individual concerns, add new docstring format support, or test components in isolation. ♻️ The growing feature set (overload signatures, type alias preservation, `annotationlib` support) made the sprawl increasingly painful.

The refactoring extracts three focused modules behind a `DocstringFormat` ABC. `_annotations.py` is a leaf module handling all annotation formatting and inspection. `_resolver.py` handles type hint resolution, `TYPE_CHECKING` guard imports, and backfill logic. `_formats/` provides the abstraction layer with `SphinxFieldListFormat` as the default handler and `NumpydocFormat` that converts numpydoc sections to Sphinx field lists before delegating. ✨ The slim `__init__.py` (~400 lines) becomes a pure orchestrator that detects the docstring format and delegates injection to the appropriate handler.

Dead code that accumulated over time was removed during the extraction: the `_TYPE_GUARD_IMPORTS_RESOLVED_GLOBALS_ID` set with no remaining readers, the `hasattr(obj, "__module__")` fallback (always True on 3.12+), the non-iterable args `try/except` in `format_annotation` (args are always tuples), the Sphinx <9 import guard in `patches.py` (minimum requirement is `sphinx>=9.1`), unreachable overload length checks, and a dead `type_annotation` truthiness guard. Interpreter-specific branches use `covdefaults` markers (`# pragma: <3.14 cover`) instead of blanket `# pragma: no cover`.

All public symbols are re-exported from `__init__.py` for backward compatibility — no downstream code changes are needed. The dependency graph is acyclic: `_annotations` has no internal imports, `_resolver` imports only from `_annotations`, and `_formats` imports from `_annotations` and `_parser`. This structure makes it straightforward to add new format handlers (e.g., Google-style) by implementing the ABC without touching the orchestrator.

Fixes #347

author: vkochev
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a headless service that appears as an OpenAI-compatible model but internally runs a ReAct/tools loop and calls tools via MCP.
- Stream interim progress and status updates to clients in OpenAI-style SSE chunks while enforcing request-wide timeouts and tool-output limits.
- Support MCP tool discovery and invocation over simple `stdio` and HTTP transports so the agent can orchestrate external tools.

### Description
- Add an HTTP server in `src/server.ts` exposing `GET /healthz`, `GET /v1/models` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` with SSE streaming in OpenAI `chat.completion.chunk` format and a final `data: [DONE]` marker.
- Implement the agent orchestration in `src/agent.ts` as `runAgent`, which emits `[STATUS]...[/STATUS]` tags, discovers tools via MCP, calls tools in a ReAct loop, applies `max_steps`, `request_timeout_ms` and `max_tool_output_bytes`, and forwards tokens via `onChunk`.
- Implement `src/mcp.ts` with `McpManager` and two transports (`stdio` and HTTP), each supporting `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` and honoring a `Mcp-Session-Id` for HTTP sessions.
- Add configuration handling with `config.yaml` (and `{env:VAR}` interpolation), a minimal YAML parser fallback, test harness `test/integration.test.ts`, TypeScript shims in `src/shims.d.ts`, and packaging entries in `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` which successfully compiled the project to `dist` without TypeScript errors after adding minimal shims. (success)
- Ran `npm test` which executed the integration test `test/integration.test.ts` (via compiled `dist/test/integration.test.js`) and the test passed. (success)
- The integration test verifies `GET /healthz`, `GET /v1/models`, non-stream and stream flows, presence of `[STATUS]...[/STATUS]` chunks, a `[DONE]` terminator, and a successful MCP `initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call` loop. (success)

author: plariono
body: This PR introduces a new geometry-building option: `createIRISGeometry3InclinedWalls(TGeoVolume* motherVolume);` The new option builds the same full cylindrical IRIS geometry as `createIRISGeometryFullCyl`, and additionally inserts three inclined wall structures in the barrel region that correspond to the petal design with the inclined walls. ## ✨ Key Features - Adds **3 equally spaced inclined ribs** (120° apart in _φ_). - Each rib is composed of **two `TGeoBBox` segments**: - **Segment 1:** from tangency near L0 to the inner surface of L1. - **Segment 2:** from the outer surface of L1 to the inner surface of L2. - Walls are: - Tangentially oriented, - Confined strictly to the **gaps between cylindrical layers**, - Constructed with finite thickness (0.4 mm) of Al 5083, - Implemented with **thickness-aware geometric bounds** to avoid overlaps with L0/L1/L2. - Uses the same cylindrical shell thickness and Z-extent as the existing full-cylinder geometry. - Fully integrated into the existing vacuum cutout / boolean solid logic. Usage: `--configKeyValues "TRKBase.layoutVD=kIRISFullCyl3InclinedWalls"`

author: copilot
body:
The chatbot in thinking mode was answering local/specific queries (e.g. store opening hours) from training data instead of searching the web. The chat history copy button also passed through URL-encoded characters (`%20`) verbatim instead of decoding them.

## Thinking mode: AI agent enforcement (`ai-agent-endpoint/index.ts`)

All three thinking-mode system prompts now identify the model as a `KI-Agent` (not `KI-Assistent`) and mandate active web search:

- **Initial system prompt** – explicitly forbids falling back to training data for local businesses, opening hours, events, or current facts; requires `web_search` for those categories
- **Phase 1 analysis** – instructs the model to plan concrete `web_search` queries for each step when tools are available
- **Execution phase** – requires calling `web_search` for every plan step that needs information; answer must be grounded in retrieved results only:

```ts
execSystemContent +=
  ' Führe JEDEN Schritt deines Plans aus und rufe web_search für JEDEN Schritt auf, der Informationen erfordert.' +
  ' Beantworte die Frage NUR auf Basis der tatsächlich gefundenen Informationen – NICHT aus deinen Trainingsdaten.'
```

## Copy button: URL-decode message content (`AiAgentTile.tsx`)

`handleCopyHistory` now runs `decodeURIComponent` on each message's content before building the clipboard string, so any `%20`-encoded characters (e.g. from URLs surfaced in AI responses) are decoded to plain text. Invalid percent-sequences are left untouched via try-catch.

```ts
let content = m.content
try { content = decodeURIComponent(content) } catch { /* ignore invalid encoding */ }
```

### Motivation
- Stripe `checkout.session.completed` webhooks were returning 200 even when Airtable updates failed, masking root causes and preventing Orders from moving to `PAID` in Airtable.
- Add temporary, explicit debug output and make the webhook fail-fast on Airtable errors so Stripe shows a non-200 response and logs contain the real Airtable error.

### Description
- Added debug logs in `checkout.session.completed` to print the Stripe session id via `console.log("[webhook] session.id", session.id)`, the session `metadata`, and the Airtable env identifiers (`AIRTABLE_BASE_ID`, `AIRTABLE_ORDERS_TABLE`, `AIRTABLE_CENTERS_TABLE`).

- Kept Stripe signature verification and `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(...)` unchanged and left the `checkout.session.expired` path behavior as-is.

##### Highlights

Flux v2.8.0 is a feature release. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

For a compressive overview of new features and API changes included in this release, please refer to the [Announcing Flux 2.8 GA blog post](https://fluxcd.io/blog/2026/02/flux-v2.8.0/).

Overview of the new features:

- Helm v4 support, including server-side apply and kstatus-based health checking (`HelmRelease`)
- Readiness evaluation of Helm-managed objects with CEL expressions (`HelmRelease`)
- Improved observability of Helm releases with inventory tracking in `.status.inventory` (`HelmRelease`)
- Reduced the mean time to recovery of Flux-managed applications via `CancelHealthCheckOnNewRevision` feature gate (`Kustomization`, `HelmRelease`)
- Support for commenting on Pull Requests directly from Flux notifications (`Provider`)
- Custom SSA apply stages for ordering resource application in kustomize-controller (`Kustomization`)
- Automatic GitHub App installation ID lookup from the repository owner (`GitRepository`, `ImageUpdateAutomation`, `Provider`)
- Support for Cosign v3 for verifying OCI artifacts and container images (`OCIRepository`)
- ArtifactGenerator support for extracting and modifying Helm charts (`ArtifactGenerator`)
- Bypass cache when fetching source objects via `DirectSourceFetch` feature gate (`Kustomization`, `HelmRelease`, `ArtifactGenerator`)

❤️ Big thanks to all the Flux contributors that helped us with this release!

##### Kubernetes compatibility

This release is compatible with the following Kubernetes versions:

| Kubernetes version | Minimum required |
| ------------------ | ---------------- |
| `v1.33`            | `>= 1.32.0`      |
| `v1.34`            | `>= 1.34.1`      |
| `v1.35`            | `>= 1.35.0`      |

> \[!NOTE]
> Note that the Flux project offers support only for the latest three minor versions of Kubernetes.
> Backwards compatibility with older versions of Kubernetes and OpenShift is offered by vendors such as
> [ControlPlane](https://control-plane.io/enterprise-for-flux-cd/) that provide enterprise support for Flux.

##### OpenShift compatibility

Flux can be installed on Red Hat OpenShift cluster directly from OperatorHub using [Flux Operator](https://operatorhub.io/operator/flux-operator). The operator allows the configuration of Flux multi-tenancy lockdown, network policies, persistent storage, sharding, vertical scaling and the synchronization of the cluster state from Git repositories, OCI artifacts, and S3-compatible storage.

##### Upgrade procedure

:warning: The Flux APIs `v1beta2` and `v2beta2` (deprecated in 2024) have reached end-of-life and have been removed from the CRDs.

Please follow the [Upgrade Procedure for Flux v2.7+](https://redirect.github.com/fluxcd/flux2/discussions/5572) for a smooth upgrade from older versions of Flux to v2.8.

author: yuksel-arslan
body:
## Summary
Significantly enhanced the authentication service with comprehensive security features including account lockout protection, two-factor authentication (2FA), email verification, password reset functionality, and audit logging. Extracted security utilities into a dedicated library and consolidated auth logic into the user-service.

## Key Changes

### Security Infrastructure
- **New security library** (`lib/security.ts`): Centralized security utilities including:
  - Password hashing with bcrypt (12 rounds)
  - Token generation and hashing
  - Email verification token creation
  - Password reset token management
  - Account lockout mechanisms with configurable thresholds
  - 2FA support (TOTP-based with speakeasy)
  - Backup code generation and verification
  - Admin email detection

### Authentication Service Enhancements
- **Register**: Added email verification tokens, admin role detection, and audit logging
- **Login**: Implemented:
  - Account lockout after configurable failed attempts (default: 5)
  - Lockout duration management (default: 30 minutes)
  - 2FA requirement detection with partial response
  - Login attempt tracking and reset on success
  - IP and user agent logging
  - Audit event logging
- **New endpoints**:
  - `logout`: Token blacklisting with expiration tracking
  - `forgotPassword`: Password reset token generation
  - `resetPassword`: Secure password reset with token validation
  - `verify2FA`: 2FA code verification
  - `setup2FA`: 2FA setup with QR code generation
  - `verifyBackupCode`: Backup code verification
  - `verifyEmail`: Email verification with token validation

### Token Management
- Added `TokenBlacklist` model for logout token revocation
- Token verification now checks blacklist before validating
- Sensitive user fields (passwordHash, 2FA secrets, tokens) excluded from responses

### Controller Updates
- Added rate limiting for register (5 attempts/hour) and login (10 attempts/minute)
- IP and user agent extraction from requests
- Proper error handling and HTTP status codes
- 2FA requirement signaling in login response

### Database Schema Updates
- User model extended with:
  - `emailVerificationToken`, `emailVerificationExpires`
  - `passwordResetToken`, `passwordResetExpires`
  - `twoFactorSecret`, `twoFactorEnabled`, `twoFactorBackupCodes`
  - `accountLocked`, `accountLockedUntil`, `loginAttempts`
  - `lastLoginAt`, `lastLoginIp`, `lastLoginDevice`
  - `isAdmin` flag
- New `TokenBlacklist` model for logout tracking
- New `AuditLog` model for security event tracking
- `TeamStats` now includes `leagueId` relationship

### Service Consolidation
- Removed duplicate auth logic from match-service
- Centralized all authentication in user-service
- Updated match-service to use user-service for auth operations

### Dependencies Added
- `speakeasy`: TOTP-based 2FA implementation
- `qrcode`: QR code generation for 2FA setup

## Notable Implementation Details
- Account lockout uses exponential backoff calculation
- 2FA uses time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) with 30-second window
- Backup codes are 8-character hex pairs (e.g., "AB12-CD34")
- All sensitive tokens are hashed before storage
- Audit logging captures authentication events with IP and device info
- Rate limiting is IP-based for registration and login attempts

body:
## 🎯 Overview

Implements a comprehensive timeout mechanism for agent execution to prevent long-running LLM calls and tool executions from hanging the backend. This addresses issue #65 (High Priority).

## 📋 Changes

### Core Implementation

**New Files:**
- [src/utils/timeout.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/utils/timeout.ts:0:0-0:0) - Reusable timeout utility with [withTimeout()](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/utils/timeout.ts:16:0-77:1), [TimeoutError](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/utils/timeout.ts:2:0-7:1), and [TimeoutManager](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/utils/timeout.ts:79:0-127:1)
- [tests/unit/timeout.test.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/tests/unit/timeout.test.ts:0:0-0:0) - Comprehensive timeout utility tests (40+ test cases)
- [tests/unit/agent_timeout.test.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/tests/unit/agent_timeout.test.ts:0:0-0:0) - LLM timeout integration tests
- [tests/unit/execution_timeout.test.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/tests/unit/execution_timeout.test.ts:0:0-0:0) - Agent execution timeout tests

**Modified Files:**
- [src/config/config.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/config/config.ts:0:0-0:0) - Added agent timeout configuration
- [src/Agents/agent.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/Agents/agent.ts:0:0-0:0) - Integrated timeout into LLM calls
- [src/Agents/registry/ToolRegistry.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/Agents/registry/ToolRegistry.ts:0:0-0:0) - Added timeout to tool execution
- [src/Agents/agents/exectutionagent.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/Agents/agents/exectutionagent.ts:0:0-0:0) - Implemented agent execution flow timeout
- [.env.example](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/.env.example:0:0-0:0) - Added timeout configuration variables

### Key Features

**Multi-Level Timeout Protection:**
- ✅ **LLM Call Timeout** (30s default) - Prevents hanging on slow API responses
- ✅ **Tool Execution Timeout** (60s default) - Prevents individual tools from blocking
- ✅ **Agent Execution Timeout** (2min default) - Prevents entire workflows from hanging
- ✅ **Plan Execution Timeout** (3min default) - Timeout for multi-step operations

**Smart Timeout Management:**
- Remaining time calculation for sequential operations
- Configurable timeouts via environment variables
- AbortSignal support for operation cancellation
- Proper resource cleanup on timeout

**Error Handling:**
- Custom [TimeoutError](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/src/utils/timeout.ts:2:0-7:1) class with operation context
- Graceful degradation with user-friendly error messages
- Detailed logging for debugging and monitoring
- No resource leaks on timeout

## 🔧 Configuration

New environment variables in [.env.example](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/isaac/Desktop/chenpilot/.env.example:0:0-0:0):

```bash
AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT=30000          # 30 seconds
AGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT=60000         # 60 seconds
AGENT_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT=120000   # 2 minutes
AGENT_PLAN_TIMEOUT=180000        # 3 minutes
```

## 🧪 Testing

- **Timeout Utility Tests**: Core timeout functionality, abort signals, concurrent operations
- **LLM Timeout Tests**: LLM call timeout scenarios, error handling
- **Execution Timeout Tests**: Agent workflow timeouts, remaining time calculation

## 📊 Impact

- **Prevents Backend Hangs**: Long-running operations now fail gracefully instead of blocking indefinitely
- **Improved Reliability**: Configurable timeouts for different operation types
- **Better UX**: Users receive timeout errors instead of waiting indefinitely
- **Monitoring**: Detailed logging helps identify slow operations

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] Core timeout utility implemented
- [x] LLM call timeout integrated
- [x] Tool execution timeout integrated
- [x] Agent execution timeout integrated
- [x] Configuration added to config system
- [x] Environment variables documented
- [x] Comprehensive tests created
- [x] Error handling implemented
- [x] Logging added

## 🚀 Usage Example

```typescript
// Timeout is automatically applied to all LLM calls
const result = await agentLLM.callLLM(userId, prompt, input, true, 5000);

// Tool execution with timeout
const toolResult = await toolRegistry.executeTool(toolName, payload, userId, 10000);

// Agent execution with timeout
const agentResult = await executionAgent.run(plan, userId, input, 60000);
```

Closes #65

author: grapebaba
body:
**Motivation**
In beam sim, gossip blocks, RPC-fetched blocks, and cached descendant blocks can arrive before the forkchoice clock ticks to their slot, causing FutureSlot rejection. The previous workaround queued blocks via expensive sszClone and had documented race conditions.

**Description**
Add forkChoice.onInterval(slot * INTERVALS_PER_SLOT, false) before every onBlock call to pre-advance the forkchoice clock, matching the existing produceBlock pattern. This is idempotent (no-op if clock already past target) and thread-safe (holds forkchoice mutex internally).

Fix #590

author: zaichu
body:
## 概要
国内株式CSV取込で、次の3点を両立するように実装を更新しました。
- 同一内容の行が複数ある場合は、CSV内の件数どおり全件保存する
- 同一CSVを再アップロードした場合は重複挿入を防止する
- 既存データを含む再アップロード判定を、移行前データにも整合する形にする

## 変更種別
- [ ] 新機能
- [x] バグ修正
- [ ] リファクタリング
- [x] 設定/依存整理

## 主な変更内容
- `backend/migrations/0010_drop_domestic_stocks_unique.sql`
  - 旧ユニークインデックスを削除し、CSV内重複行の全件保存を可能化
- `backend/migrations/0011_add_content_hash_to_domestic_stocks.sql`
  - `content_hash` / `occurrence_index` を追加し、既存データをバックフィル
- `backend/migrations/0012_add_batch_fingerprint_to_domestic_stocks.sql`
  - 一度導入した `import_batch_fingerprint` 方式
- `backend/migrations/0013_remove_batch_fingerprint_from_domestic_stocks.sql`
  - `import_batch_fingerprint` を廃止
  - `occurrence_index` を `(user_id, content_hash)` 単位のグローバル通番に再採番
  - ユニークインデックスを `(user_id, content_hash, occurrence_index)` に戻し、再取込時の整合を担保
- `backend/src/services/domestic_stock.rs`
  - `compute_batch_fingerprint` を削除
  - CTEで `batch_occurrence_index` とDB既存件数 `existing_count` を比較し、`batch_occurrence_index > existing_count` の行のみ挿入
  - `db_counts` は `user_id + content_hash` 単位で集計し、他ユーザーの件数影響を排除
- `backend/Cargo.toml`, `backend/Cargo.lock`
  - `md5` クレート依存を削除

## テスト
- [x] `cd backend && cargo fmt -- --check`
- [x] `cd backend && cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cd backend && cargo test`（Docker必須テストは `ignored` 扱い）
- [x] `cd backend && cargo build`

## 備考
- 純増分CSV（新規分のみ）で既存行と同一 `content_hash` が含まれる場合、
  `batch_occurrence_index <= existing_count` でスキップされます。
  このケースを厳密に扱うには外部キー（取引ID等）による識別が別途必要です。

author: theforgivenone
body:
## TLDR

Fixes #1873 - The LSP `documentSymbol` operation fails for non-TypeScript LSP servers (clangd, pyls, etc.) by sending the required `textDocument/didOpen` notification before requesting symbols.

## Dive Deeper

The LSP protocol requires `textDocument/didOpen` to be sent before requesting document symbols. Previously, this notification was only sent for TypeScript servers during warmup via `warmupTypescriptServer()`. This method explicitly returns early for non-TypeScript servers (line 102 checks `isTypescriptServer()`), causing clangd, pyls, and other LSP servers to fail with error `-32602: trying to get AST for non-added document`.

The fix:
1. Adds `openDocument()` method to `LspServerManager` that sends `textDocument/didOpen` for any file and any LSP server
2. Adds `getLanguageId()` helper to map file extensions to LSP language IDs (e.g., `.c` → `c`, `.cpp` → `cpp`, `.py` → `python`)
3. Calls `openDocument()` in `documentSymbols()` before making the symbol request

## Reviewer Test Plan

1. Set up a non-TypeScript LSP server (e.g., clangd for C/C++, pyls for Python)
2. Create a test file for that language (e.g., `test.c`, `test.py`)
3. Run the LSP `documentSymbol` tool on that file
4. Verify symbols are now returned (previously returned empty)

author: copilot
body:
Expands unit test coverage from ~600 tests to 850 tests (2021 assertions) across 35 suites, targeting all remaining pure-logic functions that can be validated without hardware/SDL dependencies.

### New test suites

- **test_volume.c** (13 tests) — Logarithmic volume curve `round(48 * log10(1 + v))`, clamping, monotonicity, all 21 mapping points
- **test_display.c** (16 tests) — Brightness exponential/log inverse pair roundtrip, `display_readOrWriteBuffer` pixel ops (rotation, masking, clipping, memcpy fast path)
- **test_lang.c** (16 tests) — `lang_get()` fallback lookup (NULL list, NULL entry, unicode, hidden-label spaces), `lang_free()` double-free safety, init→get→free lifecycle
- **test_signal_handler.c** (10 tests) — `signal_handler_quit()` sets flag on SIGINT/SIGTERM, ignores SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2/SIGHUP/SIGALRM/0, flag persistence
- **test_battery.c** (16 tests) — Extracted `elapsed_ms` calculation from `battery_isCharging()` cache: nanosecond borrow, exact 2000ms boundary, clock-backward rejection
- **test_playactivity_paths.c** (13 tests) — `__ensure_rel_path()` normalization: `../../Roms/` split, `/mnt/SDCARD/Roms/` replace, passthrough, UTF-8 filenames
- **test_game_entry.c** (18 tests) — `JsonGameEntry` fromJson/toJson roundtrip, emupath extraction
- **test_state_security.c** (18 tests) — `write_mainui_state` JSON output, page calculations, `state_getAppName` edges
- **test_config_security.c** (18 tests) — `file_parseKeyValue`, `file_changeKeyValue`, `file_cleanName`
- **test_str/file/json_security.c** — Buffer overflow prevention, NULL safety, path traversal, malformed JSON

### Approach

Pure calculation logic is inlined from source headers to avoid pulling in hardware-dependent code (ioctl, mmap, GPIO, SDL). Functions like `file_path_relative_to()` are stubbed to exercise fallback paths:

```c
// Stub forces fallback path normalization logic in __ensure_rel_path
static bool file_path_relative_to(char *path_out, const char *dir_from, const char *file_to)
{
    (void)dir_from; (void)file_to;
    path_out[0] = '\0';
    return false;
}
```

### Remaining untestable areas

Hardware-dependent code (axp/I2C, GPIO rumble, SDL framebuffer init, UDP/socket, RetroArch subprocess commands) cannot be unit tested without device access — these are intentionally excluded.

   Jupyter Notebook 7.5 is based on JupyterLab 4.5, and includes a number of new features, bug fixes, and enhancements for extension developers. This release is compatible with extensions supporting JupyterLab 4.0. Extension authors are recommended to consult the [Extension Migration Guide](https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extension/extension_migration.html#jupyterlab-4-4-to-4-5) which lists deprecations and changes to the public API.

Below are a few highlights for this new release. Most of the new features and improvements come from the update to JupyterLab 4.5, although they may not all be supported in Notebook 7.5.

For reference you may have a look at the [JupyterLab 4.5 changelog](https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting_started/changelog.html#v4-5) to learn more.

 Notebook improvements

The default windowing mode is now `contentVisibility` which improves cell rendering and alleviates previously reported issues. The minimap can be enabled for all windowing modes and all notebooks via the `Settings` menu, or by toggling the minimap per notebook with the `View` -> `Show Minimap` option.

Additional fixes improve layout containment and scrollbar behavior when working with long cells.

 Debugger and console enhancements

The debugger's evaluate dialog has been replaced with an interactive console featuring syntax highlighting and code completion. The variables panel now preserves state when switching editors. Visual improvements include highlighted selected breakpoints, improved empty line handling, and a paused indicator. Debugger panels now reference cell execution counts.

<img alt="Debugger panels with reference to execution counts and paused indicator as well as console evaluation"

- There is a new `allowFileUploads` setting to control upload permissions.
- Menu options for creating Python, R, or Julia files are now available from the New menu.
- The "Select All" command is now available with the Ctrl + A (or Cmd + A on macOS) keyboard shortcut in the file browser.
- Breadcrumbs are now configurable through `breadcrumbsLeftItems` and `breadcrumbsRightItems` settings.

 Settings editor improvements

The `addExtraLineOnCellMerge` setting removes extra lines when merging cells, matching classic notebook behavior.

 Cell toolbar settings

The cell toolbar settings are now exposed in the Settings Editor, making it easier to customize the cell toolbar appearance and behavior.

 Keyboard shortcuts

The `O` key has been defined as the keyboard shortcut to toggle cell outputs, restoring this familiar functionality from the classic notebook.

 User interface and accessibility

Automatic theme switching between light and dark modes is now available when system synchronization is enabled. Dialog components display buttons and checkboxes on separate lines for improved readability. Terminal selections show better visibility under high-contrast themes. Keyboard navigation and status bar tab ordering have been improved.

 Breaking changes

Python 3.8 support has been dropped in this release.

### All Submissions:

2. Confirm the dominant pattern template matches the convention used by existing classes (EOF `::init()` call, namespace, etc.).
3. Verify recipe steps: e.g., adding a provider requires registration in `Providers::init()`, not just an `include_once`.
4. Check that no information in the file duplicates the workspace-level `AGENTS.md`.

- Added a `gamebench_healthz_url` variable and explicit `http(s)` format validation for `gamebench_url`, introducing the `missing_gamebench_url` preflight reason and associated config error payload.
- Reworked `preflight_gamebench_smoke_check` to call the validated `gamebench_healthz_url` and to attach an encoded `detail` field (via `json.encode` + `text.decode(json.encode(e))`) to error/warning payloads so DNS/timeout/401/404/etc. are distinguishable.
- Kept fail-closed semantics when `require_gamebench_healthz=true` while ensuring `require_gamebench_healthz=false` only logs warnings and preserves downstream Gamebench ingestion and data-quality steps.
- Propagated the `preflight_status.gamebench.reason` into Gamebench branch skip logs and updated the README workflow section to document `QA_METRICS_GAMEBENCH_URL` and `require_gamebench_healthz` behavior.

### Testing
- Parsed and validated the modified workflow YAML using Ruby with `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file("workflows/qa_metrics_ingestion.yaml"); puts "YAML OK"'`, which succeeded.

### Motivation
- Replace hard-coded UI with domain-driven, testable ViewModel/Repository flows so screens render from real data and are easier to validate. 
- Provide lightweight in-memory `Repository`/`UseCase` stubs to allow deterministic UI/demo flows and unit testing without external dependencies. 
- Establish a simple navigation/store foundation and CI/pr-scope rules to make future feature work safer and reviewable.

### Description
- Add domain layer types and protocols in `Sources/ClosetWeek/Domain` including `Models.swift`, `Repositories.swift`, and `UseCases.swift` to define the core interfaces. 
- Add in-memory implementations and test stubs in `Sources/ClosetWeek/Data` (`InMemoryRepositories.swift`, `StubUseCases.swift`) to simulate data and success/failure paths. 
- Implement `ViewModel` and `View` scaffolding for `Week`, `Closet`, `Suggestion`, and `Settings` under `Sources/ClosetWeek/Features`, and wire them to simple `Views` that use `State/Event` patterns. 
- Introduce `WeekPlanStore` as a single source of truth, `Coordinators` and `Routes` for navigation, plus `ClosetWeekApp` and `MainTabView` to compose the app. 
- Add package manifest `Package.swift`, CI workflow `ci.yml`, PR-scope check `pr-scope-check.yml`, docs (`docs/実装指針.md`, `docs/PR分割ルール.md`), and a comprehensive set of unit tests under `Tests/ClosetWeekTests` covering ViewModels, Store, Repositories, and Coordinators.

author: udaykiran243
body:
## Description

This PR implements the requested feature to permanently delete notifications from the database when a user marks them as "read". Previously, notifications were only updated with an `is_read` flag. This change optimizes database storage by removing processed notifications entirely.

Fixes #406 

## Changes

- **Backend (`server/backend-api/app/api/routes/notifications.py`)**:
    - Replaced the `PATCH /notifications/in-app/{id}/read` endpoint with `DELETE /notifications/in-app/{id}`.
    - Added a new `DELETE /notifications/in-app/delete-all` endpoint to handle bulk deletion.
    - Updated logic to ensure users can only delete their own notifications.
- **Frontend (`frontend/src/api/notifications.js`)**:
    - Replaced `markNotificationAsRead` with `deleteNotification`.
    - Added `deleteAllNotifications` API call.
- **Frontend (`frontend/src/components/NotificationDropdown.jsx`)**:
    - Updated UI interactions to delete notifications immediately upon clicking.
    - Enhanced the "Mark all as read" button functionality to clear all notifications from the database.
- **Tests (`server/backend-api/tests/test_notification_integration.py`)**:
    - Updated integration tests to verify the existence of the new `deleteNotification` API function.

## Verification

- [x] Clicking a single notification removes it from the list and deletes it from the database.
- [x] Clicking "Mark all as read" clears all notifications for the user.
- [x] Linting checks passed for both frontend and backend.

author: osman-ibrahiem
body:
**What this PR does:**

* Restructure project into **feature-based architecture** for scalability and maintainability.
* Introduced clear separation between **presentation**, **domain**, and **data** layers within each feature.
* Created **feature modules**:

    * `auth` (Login, Register, User session)
    * `books` (Books list, Book details, Bookmarks)
    * `profile`
    * `settings`
* Added **core module** for shared components, utilities, and storage abstractions (e.g., SharedPreferences wrapper).

**Changes made:**

1. **Auth feature**

    * `features/auth/presentation/` → Login & Register screens, States, and Controllers
    * `features/auth/domain/` → UseCases, Entities, Repository abstract class
    * `features/auth/data/` → Repository implementation, Remote & Local DataSources, Models

2. **Books feature**

    * `features/books/presentation/` → Books list, Book details, Bookmarks UI
    * `features/books/domain/` → UseCases, Entities, Repository abstract class
    * `features/books/data/` → Repository implementation, Remote & Local DataSources, Models

3. **Profile feature**

    * `features/profile/...` → Profile screens, UseCases, Repository abstract class

4. **Settings feature**

    * `features/settings/...` → Settings screen, UseCases, Repository abstract class
    * Settings LocalDataSource handles cached preferences (language, theme, etc.)

5. **Core module**

    * Shared utilities, Base classes, DI setup, Services abstraction for local caching.

**Notes:**

* Existing functionality is **unchanged**.
* All repository abstractions remain; only their location in feature modules changed.
* Local caching responsibilities were split:

    * Auth session → `auth/data`
    * App settings (language, theme) → `settings/data`

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a complete pipeline that receives MQTT sensor data from PI devices and stores it in InfluxDB for time-series retention and Grafana visualization.
- Expose a lightweight user-facing web UI to show current state of all sensors and embed a Grafana panel for richer visualization.
- Make service configuration flexible via environment variables to ease containerized deployment.

### Description
- Added environment-aware MQTT→Influx ingest server in `mqtt_influx_server.py` that subscribes to MQTT topics, converts readings to Influx `Point`s and writes them asynchronously to InfluxDB using `INFLUX_*` and `MQTT_*` env vars as overrides.
- Implemented a new Flask web app in `web_app.py` with routes `"/"` (UI) and `"/api/states"` (latest per-sensor state from InfluxDB), and included templates (`templates/index.html`) and styles (`static/styles.css`) for the UI.
- Provisioned Grafana with an InfluxDB datasource and a dashboard (`grafana/provisioning/*`, `grafana/dashboards/iot-overview.json`) and updated `docker-compose.yml` to deploy Mosquitto, InfluxDB, Grafana, the ingest server and the web app with appropriate environment variables and ports.
- Updated `settings.json` (added `grafana` section) and `README.md` with architecture, run instructions and configuration notes.

### Testing
- Ran Python byte-compile: `python -m py_compile mqtt_influx_server.py web_app.py settings.py` and it succeeded.
- Launched the web UI with `python web_app.py` and performed a smoke-check via browser automation (screenshot of `http://127.0.0.1:5001` was captured) which rendered the UI successfully.
- Verified graceful failure behavior: `/api/states` returns HTTP 503 with a warning when InfluxDB is not reachable (observed during local smoke test).
- Attempted `docker compose config` but Docker CLI was not available in the environment; compose configuration was nevertheless generated/updated in the repository for use in a Docker-enabled environment.

------

author: blackplume233
body:
## Summary

Fixes #155 — Agent instance status gets stuck on `error` in `.actant.json` while the backend process is actually running and responsive.

### Root Cause

When `startAgent()` spawns a backend process via `ProcessLauncher` but the subsequent ACP connection fails, the `catch` block:
- Set status to `"error"` ✅
- Disconnected ACP ✅
- **Did NOT terminate the already-spawned process** ❌ → process leak
- **Did NOT remove the process from the internal map** ❌ → stale state
- **Did NOT clear the PID from `.actant.json`** ❌ → violates INV-PID invariant

Additionally, on daemon restart, `initialize()` only corrected `running`/`starting`/`stopping` states but left `error`/`crashed` instances with stale PIDs unchecked — orphan processes were never reclaimed.

## Changes

### Fix 1: `startAgent()` error path cleanup (`agent-manager.ts`)

- Terminate the spawned process in the `catch` block before setting error status
- Remove the process from the internal `processes` map
- Clear `pid` from `.actant.json` metadata (set to `undefined`)

### Fix 2: Orphan process detection in `initialize()` (`agent-manager.ts`)

- On daemon startup, check `error`/`crashed` instances that still have a PID recorded
- If the PID is alive → reclaim: set status to `running`, register in ProcessWatcher
- If the PID is dead → clear the stale PID from metadata (satisfies `INV-PID` invariant from endurance-testing.md)

### Fix 3: Tests (`agent-manager.test.ts`)

Added 5 new test cases in two new `describe` blocks:

- **`startAgent error cleanup (#155)`** (2 tests):
  - Verifies process is terminated when ACP connection fails
  - Verifies agent can be restarted after a failed start (no stale process blocking)

- **`initialize orphan process detection (#155)`** (3 tests):
  - Verifies alive orphan with `error` status is reclaimed to `running`
  - Verifies alive orphan with `crashed` status is reclaimed to `running`
  - Verifies dead process PID is cleared from `error` status instance

## What was NOT changed

The `handleProcessExit()` exit status logic (`processOwnership === "external" ? "crashed" : "stopped"`) was initially considered for modification but was **kept as-is** after reviewing the endurance testing spec (`endurance-testing.md` shutdown behavior matrix), which explicitly states that externally-attached processes detected by the watcher should be marked as `crashed` (abnormal exit without proper `detach`).

## Test Results

- **agent-manager.test.ts**: 47/47 passed ✅
- **agent-lifecycle-scenarios.test.ts**: 8/9 passed (1 pre-existing flaky test, verified on baseline) ✅
- **endurance tests**: Pre-existing failures (unrelated: `cursor` backend lacks ACP support + hardcoded PIDs) — not introduced by this PR

---

This PR was written using [Vibe Kanban](https://vibekanban.com)

author: fabianfett
body:
Let's improve NIOAsyncChannels performance, by using UnsafeContinuations instead of CheckedContinuations.

### Motivation:

We want to improve the performance for our async APIs.

### Modifications:

- Introduce a new typealias `NIOUnsafeContinuation` that behaves like a UnsafeContinuation in release mode and like a CheckedContinuation in debug mode.
- Use the `NIOUnsafeContinuation` inside the `NIOAsyncWriter`
- Use the `NIOUnsafeContinuation` inside the `NIOThrowingAsyncSequenceProducer`

### Result:

Fewer allocations

author: ttymayor
body:
## Summary

- **feat: WelcomeDialog** — Replace `FirstLoadingAnimation` with a blocking `WelcomeDialog` that shows privacy and browser compatibility notices on first visit. Users can check "不再顯示" to opt out via `localStorage`. The dialog prevents closing via outside click or Escape key.
- **refactor: CourseSchedule status computed client-side** — Extract table rendering from the cached server component `CourseScheduleList` into a new `"use client"` component `CourseScheduleTable`. Status (`開放` / `關閉` / `結束`) is now computed from `Date.now()` vs `start_time`/`end_time` at render time instead of using the stale DB `status` field. Fixes toJSON serialization error (Mongoose ObjectId → string) and hydration mismatch (replaced `toLocaleString` with a deterministic UTC+8 formatter).
- **chore: bump dependencies** — Update Next.js 16.1.2 → 16.1.6, React 19.2.3 → 19.2.4, mongoose, motion, lucide-react, swr, tailwind-merge, animejs, axios, and related dev dependencies.
- **misc** — Remove commented-out announcement section from home page. Add `CLAUDE.md` project instructions file.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/components/WelcomeDialog.tsx` | New — blocking welcome dialog with privacy notice |
| `src/components/FirstLoadingAnimation.tsx` | Deleted — replaced by WelcomeDialog |
| `src/app/layout.tsx` | Swap `FirstLoadingAnimation` → `WelcomeDialog` |
| `src/app/page.tsx` | Remove commented-out announcement section |
| `src/components/CourseScheduleTable.tsx` | New — `"use client"` component with client-side status computation |
| `src/components/CourseScheduleList.tsx` | Trimmed to data-fetch only; delegates rendering to `CourseScheduleTable` |
| `package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Dependency version bumps |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Add project instructions for Claude Code |

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit the home page as a first-time user — WelcomeDialog should appear and block interaction until dismissed
- [ ] Check "不再顯示" and close — dialog should not appear on next visit
- [ ] Verify 選課時程 section shows correct status (開放/關閉/結束) based on current time
- [ ] Confirm no hydration mismatch errors in the browser console
- [ ] Run `pnpm build` — should complete with no TypeScript errors

author: kevinwangsheng
body:
## Problem When the GLM (Zhipu AI) model is unavailable or misconfigured, it returns an error message in Chinese: ``` 模型不存在，请检查模型代码 ``` This error was not recognized by `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage()`, preventing automatic fallback to the next configured model. ## Root Cause The `classifyFailoverReason()` function in `src/agents/pi-embedded-helpers/errors.ts` only checks for English error patterns like "model not found" and "unknown model". GLM's Chinese error message was not matched, so the error was not classified as `model_not_found` and no fallback was triggered. ## Fix Add Chinese pattern matching to `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage()`: - `模型不存在` (model does not exist) - `模型代码` (model code) Now when GLM returns a Chinese model-not-found error, it is correctly classified and triggers model fallback. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm lint` passes - [x] Code change is minimal (5 lines) ## Impact Cron jobs and other automated tasks with fallback models configured will now correctly switch to the fallback when GLM returns Chinese error messages.

Greptile Summary

Adds Chinese error pattern matching to `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage()` for GLM (Zhipu AI) model-not-found errors. The change enables failover when GLM returns Chinese error messages like "模型不存在，请检查模型代码". - Extends error detection to support Chinese model-not-found patterns - Follows existing pattern from #22855 which added Chinese context overflow detection - Missing tests for the new patterns (consider adding test cases similar to `isContextOverflowError` Chinese pattern tests in `pi-embedded-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts:204-217`)

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge after fixing the `lower` vs `raw` variable issue - The change is minimal and follows established patterns for i18n error detection, but has a minor bug where `lower.includes()` is used instead of `raw.includes()` for Chinese characters. Once fixed, the change is safe and well-motivated by the PR description. - src/agents/pi-embedded-helpers/errors.ts:839 needs the variable fix Last reviewed commit: c7b0184

author: rdjjke
body:
## Problem
1. GRES env var was used by dynamic workers that we don't support anymore. However it's still being populated in supervisord entypoint
2. The worker-init container uses two `scontrol update nodename=...` calls instead of one, increasing the load on the Slurm controller when many worker pods start at the same time.
3. It's not possible to schedule Slurm jobs to the specific IB pods

## Solution
1. Drop GRES env var from supervisord_entrypoint.sh
2. Merge two `scontrol update` calls into one
3. Support `TOPO_SWITCH_TIER2` env var evaluation in SLURM_NODE_EXTRA in slurmd_entrypoint.sh

## Testing
1. Create a new cluster
2. Make sure Slurm nodes undrain on powering up, and the topology is updated
3. Make sure TOPO_SWITCH_TIER2 is present in Slurm node extra constraints

## Release Notes
Support adding tier-2 topology switches to Slurm node extra constraints

author: konstziv
body:
Sprint Beta-0, Phase 1 — Abstractions.

Introduce a generic LLM provider interface (`LLMProvider` ABC) with a single `generate()` method that accepts an arbitrary Pydantic schema, enabling the upcoming Discovery engine and future multi-provider support.

New files:
- `llm/base.py`   — `LLMProvider` ABC with @overload (schema → T,
  None → str) and `LLMResponse[T]` frozen Pydantic generic model
  (content, tokens, cost, latency).
- `llm/gemini.py`  — `GeminiProvider(LLMProvider)` extracted from
  `integrations/gemini.py`. Includes GEMINI_PRICING, calculate_cost(),
  error conversion (fixed if→elif chain to prevent overwrite), and
  @with_retry decorator.

Refactored files:
- `integrations/gemini.py` — now a thin backward-compatible wrapper. `analyze_code_changes()` delegates to `GeminiProvider`. `GeminiClient` kept with DeprecationWarning (removal in v1.0.0 stable). All public symbols re-exported from `llm.gemini`.

Design decisions:
- PEP 695 type parameters (class LLMResponse[T], def generate[T: BaseModel])
- @overload for mypy strict: response_schema: type[T] → LLMResponse[T], response_schema: None → LLMResponse[str]
- api_key: str in GeminiProvider (caller does .get_secret_value())
- Manual parsing via response.text + model_validate_json (not SDK parsed)
- _convert_google_exception: elif chain + extracted _match_by_error_message()

Tests: 468 passed (+34 new), ruff clean, mypy clean, mkdocs --strict OK. New test files: tests/unit/test_llm/test_base.py (7), tests/unit/test_llm/test_gemini.py (27).
Updated: tests/integration/test_gemini.py (12).

## Summary

Adds a `SECURITY.md` file to provide clear guidance for security researchers on how to report vulnerabilities responsibly.

fast-xml-parser has had [multiple security advisories](https://github.com/NaturalIntelligence/fast-xml-parser/security/advisories) published over the years, but currently has no security policy document. GitHub recommends a SECURITY.md so that the "Report a vulnerability" button in the Security tab links to clear instructions.

### What's included

- **Reporting channels**: GitHub Private Security Advisory (preferred) + email fallback
- **Response timelines**: 72h acknowledgment, 14/30 day fix targets
- **Supported versions table**: v5.x full support, v4.x security-only
- **Secure configuration example**: Recommended hardening options for untrusted XML input
- **Researcher credit policy**: Opt-in credit for reporters

### Why this matters

With ~248M monthly npm downloads, having a visible security policy helps researchers find the right channel quickly, reduces noise in public issues, and signals that the project takes security seriously.

No code changes — documentation only.

author: trsenna
body:
### 🚀 O que foi feito?
  Este PR consolida o primeiro laboratório prático de Kubernetes, focado em persistência de dados e o ciclo de vida de Pods (Init Containers). Além da infraestrutura como código, foi estruturada a documentação base para o projeto.


###   Principais implementações:
   - K8s Manifests: Criação de Namespace, PVC e Deployment para um servidor Nginx.
   - Init Containers: Implementação de um initContainer que inicializa dados dinâmicos (logs de timestamp) em um volume persistente.
   - Automação: Criação de um Makefile na pasta do laboratório para agilizar comandos de apply, port-forward e clean.
   - Documentação Local: Adição de um README.md detalhado dentro de 01-persistence-init/ com o passo a passo técnico.
   - Guia do Projeto: Criação do README.md na raiz com instruções de setup do ambiente (Minikube, Ingress e Metrics Server).


###   🛠️ Como testar?
   1. Certifique-se de ter o Minikube rodando com os addons necessários (ingress e metrics-server).
   2. Acesse a pasta 01-persistence-init/.
   3. Execute make apply para subir os recursos.
   4. Use make port-forward e acesse localhost:8080 para validar que o arquivo persistente foi criado pelo Init Container.
   5. Delete o Pod e verifique se o novo Pod mantém o histórico no arquivo index.html.


###   📌 Notas
   - O laboratório utiliza provisionamento dinâmico de volumes, assumindo que o cluster possui um Default StorageClass.

Trello ticket [#1360](https://trello.com/c/8btbJC8b/1360-estimates-by-job-role-conversion-create-new-column-for-job-role-ratios)

This ticket is solved by creating a function called `get_percentage_share` which returns a `polars.Expr` which can then be used directly in the pipeline. As part of this change I've upgraded the version of `polars` to the latest because of an issue I was getting in my tests when doing division on Null values, which seemed to be fixed by the later version. ### Changes (single file: `roles.go`)

**Fix A — `Roles.Check()` duplicate detection (lines 130–143)**
Added `seen := make(map[Role]bool)` tracking map so that `Roles{RoleAuth, RoleAuth}.Check()` now correctly returns `trace.BadParameter("duplicate role %q", role)` instead of `nil`.

**Fix B — `Role.Check()` switch case (line 179)**

Replaced naive `Include()`-based loop with `map[Role]bool` set conversion on both sides, ensuring symmetric equality and correct handling of duplicates. `Roles{RoleAuth, RoleAuth}.Equals(Roles{RoleAuth, RoleProxy})` now correctly returns `false`.

flowchart TD

author: emirakdag0
body:
# Feature: Implement Conflict Resolution System for Multi-Document Field Updates

## 📋 Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive conflict resolution system that detects and manages conflicting information when multiple documents or user inputs provide different values for the same DREF form field. Users are prompted to choose which value to keep, ensuring data accuracy with a complete audit trail.

## 🎯 Problem Statement

Currently, when users upload multiple documents (PDFs, images, voice notes, etc.) containing different values for the same field, the system silently overwrites previous values without user awareness. This can lead to:

- ❌ Loss of potentially important information
- ❌ Unintentional data overwrites
- ❌ No visibility into conflicting data sources
- ❌ Difficulty tracking which document provided which value

**Example Scenario:**
1. User uploads `initial_report.pdf` → System extracts "5000 people affected"
2. User uploads `updated_assessment.pdf` → System extracts "7000 people affected"
3. **Problem:** Which value is correct? User is never asked.

## ✅ Solution

This PR adds an intelligent conflict detection and resolution workflow that:

1. **Tracks provenance** - Records which document/message each field value came from
2. **Detects conflicts** - Identifies when new values differ from existing values
3. **Prompts users** - Generates clear, user-friendly conflict resolution prompts
4. **Manages workflow** - Guides users through resolving conflicts one at a time
5. **Maintains audit trail** - Records all value changes and resolution decisions

## 🏗️ Architecture

### New Module: `backend/conflict_resolver/`

```
backend/conflict_resolver/
├── __init__.py           # Public API exports
├── detector.py           # ConflictDetector - identifies conflicts
├── manager.py            # ConflictManager - stores & resolves conflicts
└── service.py            # ConflictResolverService - integration layer
```

### Integration: `backend/services/process_user_input.py`

Modified the main service orchestrator to:
- Check for pending conflicts at the start of each request
- Detect conflicts before applying field updates
- Return enhanced responses with conflict information

## 🎨 Key Features

### 1. Smart Conflict Detection

Handles edge cases intelligently:

- **Numeric tolerance**: `5000` and `5000.0` are considered identical
- **String normalization**: `"Flood"` and `"  flood  "` match (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed)
- **List order-independence**: `[A, B, C]` equals `[C, A, B]`
- **Empty value handling**: `None`, `""`, and `[]` are treated as equivalent
- **Type compatibility**: Prevents false conflicts from type mismatches

### 2. Source Tracking & Provenance

Every field value includes rich metadata:

```python
{
  "value": 7000,
  "source": "updated_assessment.pdf",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-28T15:45:00Z",
  "message_id": "msg_456"
}
```

### 3. User-Friendly Conflict Prompts

Clear, actionable prompts with context:

```
I found conflicting information for 'Number of People Affected':

• initial_report.pdf says: 5000
  (from January 28, 2025 at 02:30 PM)

• updated_assessment.pdf says: 7000
  (from January 28, 2025 at 03:45 PM)

Which value should I use? Reply with '1' for the first option or '2' for the second option.
```

### 4. Natural Language Input

Accepts multiple ways of expressing choices:

- Direct: `"1"`, `"2"`
- Descriptive: `"first"`, `"second"`
- Natural: `"keep the first one"`, `"use new value"`, `"existing"`

### 5. Sequential Resolution Workflow

For multiple conflicts, guides users through one at a time:

```
Conflict 1 detected → User chooses → "✓ Updated field. You have 2 more conflicts."
Conflict 2 detected → User chooses → "✓ Updated field. You have 1 more conflict."
Conflict 3 detected → User chooses → "✓ All conflicts resolved!"
```

### 6. Complete Audit Trail

Tracks every change with:
- What value was chosen
- What value was rejected
- Who made the decision (message ID)
- When it was resolved
- Source of each value

## 📊 Enhanced Response Format

### Before (No Conflicts):
```json
{
  "classification": "NEW_INFORMATION",
  "reply": "I've processed your document.",
  "field_updates": [
    {"field": "people_affected", "value": 5000}
  ],
  "processing_summary": {...}
}
```

### After (With Conflicts Detected):
```json
{
  "classification": "NEW_INFORMATION",
  "reply": "I've processed your document.",
  "field_updates": [
    {"field": "location", "value": "Bangladesh"}
  ],
  "processing_summary": {...},
  "has_conflicts": true,
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "field_name": "people_affected",
      "field_label": "Number of People Affected",
      "conflict_id": "people_affected_2025-01-28T15-45-00Z",
      "existing_value": {
        "value": 5000,
        "source": "initial_report.pdf",
        "timestamp": "2025-01-28T14:30:00Z"
      },
      "new_value": {
        "value": 7000,
        "source": "updated_assessment.pdf",
        "timestamp": "2025-01-28T15:45:00Z"
      }
    }
  ],
  "conflict_prompt": "I found conflicting information for 'Number of People Affected':..."
}
```

### After (Resolution Response):
```json
{
  "resolved": true,
  "field_updates": [
    {
      "field": "people_affected",
      "value": 7000,
      "source": "updated_assessment.pdf",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-28T15:45:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "reply": "✓ Updated Number of People Affected. All conflicts resolved!",
  "remaining_conflicts": 0
}
```

## 🧪 Test Coverage

**65+ comprehensive tests** covering:

### Conflict Detection Tests (`test_detector.py` - 25 tests)
- ✅ New fields don't create conflicts
- ✅ Same values don't create conflicts
- ✅ Different values create conflicts
- ✅ Multiple conflicts detected
- ✅ Numeric tolerance (5000 == 5000.0)
- ✅ String normalization ("Flood" == "flood")
- ✅ Empty value handling (None == "" == [])
- ✅ List order-independence
- ✅ Boolean conflict detection
- ✅ Always-overwrite fields
- ✅ Conflict prompt generation

### Conflict Management Tests (`test_manager.py` - 20 tests)
- ✅ Adding conflicts to pending list
- ✅ Retrieving conflicts by ID
- ✅ Resolving with choice 1 (existing)
- ✅ Resolving with choice 2 (new)
- ✅ Invalid choice handling
- ✅ Resolution history tracking
- ✅ Multiple conflict resolution
- ✅ Audit trail generation
- ✅ State export/import

### Service Integration Tests (`test_service.py` - 20 tests)
- ✅ First input (no conflicts)
- ✅ Conflicting inputs detected
- ✅ Valid resolution choices
- ✅ Natural language parsing
- ✅ Invalid choice handling
- ✅ Sequential multi-conflict resolution
- ✅ Pending conflicts summary
- ✅ Form state management
- ✅ Field audit trail

**Run tests:**
```bash
pytest tests/test_detector.py -v
pytest tests/test_manager.py -v
pytest tests/test_service.py -v
```
## 📖 Usage Examples

### Example 1: Normal Flow (No Conflicts)

```python
result = process_user_input(
    user_message="Flood in Bangladesh, 5000 people affected",
    current_form_state={},
    files=[{"data": "...", "type": "pdf", "filename": "report.pdf"}]
)

print(result["has_conflicts"])  # False
print(result["field_updates"])  # [{"field": "people_affected", "value": 5000}]
# Apply updates normally
```

### Example 2: Conflict Detection

```python
# First upload
process_user_input(
    user_message="Initial report",
    files=[{"filename": "report1.pdf", ...}]
)
# Sets: people_affected = 5000

# Second upload with different value
result = process_user_input(
    user_message="Updated assessment",
    files=[{"filename": "report2.pdf", ...}]
)
# New value: people_affected = 7000

# Conflict detected!
print(result["has_conflicts"])  # True
print(result["conflict_prompt"])
# Output:
# I found conflicting information for 'Number of People A

author: umangyadav
body:
## Motivation

Currently for scheduleVersion =1, loop pipelining is inserting barrier before it's necessary. 

This is the output **_after_** `rock-pipeline` currently for `--schedule_version 1`
```
scf.for 
{
LDSBarrier
GlobalLoad
DSRead + MFMA
LDSBarrier
LDSWrite
}
```
Notice that LDSbarrier appears before GlobalLoad but instead it should appear after GlobalLoad. 

With this PR, it appears after GlobalLoad.  

## Technical Details

This bug is happening because currently `PushDownBarrier` runs before removal of stages and `PushDownBarrier` exits early as soon as it finds a terminator (e.g. rock.yield)

This PR fixes one more bug, if there are no "stages" found then it shouldn't do loop pipelining and it should preserve LDS Barriers in original program. But at present it first removes all the barriers and then exits, which could lead to accuracy problems. In practice we won't get a program without stages, but there was a unit-test which was removing all barriers when there were no stages. 

I've modified lit-tests to look for barriers in correct place after removal of stages.

author: filipexyz
body:
## Summary

- **Externalize `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` from the server bundle** — the bundler was inlining the SDK, which broke its runtime resolution of `cli.js` (the executable it spawns as a child process). With `--external`, the SDK resolves from `node_modules` and finds `cli.js` next to itself.
- **Sanitize `CLAUDECODE` env var** — when Omni is launched from within Claude Code (e.g. `omni install` in a Claude Code session), `CLAUDECODE=1` leaks into the server process, causing the SDK to refuse to spawn a new agent. Now always sets `CLAUDECODE=0`.
- **Bump `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`** from `^0.2.39` to `^0.2.52`

## Root cause

The `build:server` script uses `bun build` which inlines all imports. The SDK uses `import.meta.url` to resolve `cli.js` relative to itself — but after bundling, `import.meta.url` points to `dist/server/index.js` instead of the SDK directory, so `cli.js` is never found.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun run build:server` completes without errors
- [ ] `npm pack` includes `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` as a runtime dependency
- [ ] Create a Claude Code provider and send a message — agent responds instead of throwing "executable not found"
- [ ] Launch Omni from within a Claude Code session — agent still works (CLAUDECODE sanitized)

author: jmassardo
body:
## Summary

Implements Epic 40: Thread Library (#153) — a comprehensive thread standard data library, parametric geometry generator, and 3D-print optimization system supporting 8 international thread families.

## Sub-Issues Resolved

- **#247** US-41.1: Implement Thread Geometry Generator (5 SP)
- **#248** US-41.2: Create Standard Thread Library (3 SP)
- **#249** US-41.4: Add Print-Optimized Thread Profiles (3 SP)

## Changes

### Thread Data Library (`backend/app/cad/threads.py`)

- `ThreadSpec` frozen dataclass with 22 fields covering all dimensional data
- 5 StrEnum types: `ThreadFamily` (8 families), `ThreadType`, `PitchSeries`, `ThreadForm` (6 profiles), `ThreadHand`
- 8 comprehensive data dictionaries with real engineering values:
  - ISO Metric Coarse (12 sizes M2–M24) — ISO 261
  - ISO Metric Fine (6 sizes) — ISO 261
  - UNC (10 sizes) — ASME B1.1
  - UNF (7 sizes) — ASME B1.1
  - NPT (9 sizes with taper) — ASME B1.20.1
  - BSPP (6 sizes, 55° parallel) — ISO 228-1
  - BSPT (6 sizes, 55° tapered) — ISO 7-1
  - ACME (6 sizes, 29°) — ASME B1.5
  - Trapezoidal (6 sizes, 30°) — ISO 2904
- Unified `THREAD_REGISTRY` with 4 lookup functions
- Cross-validated against existing `hardware.py` tap drill/clearance values for M2–M10

### Thread Geometry Generator (`backend/app/cad/thread_generator.py`)

- `ThreadGeneratorConfig` frozen dataclass for generation parameters
- `generate_thread()` entry point using Build123d cylinder + helical groove approach
- External and internal thread support (internal returns cutting tool for `difference()`)
- Left-hand and right-hand helix support
- NPT tapered thread support
- Chamfer lead-in generation
- Safety limits: 200mm max length, 500 max revolutions, 60s timeout

### Print Optimization (`backend/app/cad/thread_print_optimizer.py`)

- `PrintProcess` (FDM/SLA/SLS/MJF), `ToleranceClass` (tight/standard/loose), `PrintFeasibility` enums
- Process-specific clearance defaults per tolerance class
- `optimize_thread_for_print()` — applies clearance adjustments to thread diameters
- `get_print_recommendation()` — feasibility ratings with alternative suggestions
- `get_orientation_advice()` — print orientation recommendations with reasoning
- Minimum printable pitch validation per process

### API Layer (`backend/app/api/v2/threads.py`)

7 endpoints on `/api/v2/threads`:

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/families` | Public | List all thread families |
| GET | `/standards/{family}` | Public | List sizes in a family |
| GET | `/standards/{family}/{size:path}` | Public | Get full thread spec |
| GET | `/tap-drill/{family}/{size:path}` | Public | Tap drill + clearance data |
| POST | `/generate` | Required | Generate thread geometry |
| POST | `/generate/print-optimized` | Required | Generate print-optimized thread |
| GET | `/print-recommendations/{family}/{size:path}` | Public | Print feasibility rating |

### Schemas (`backend/app/schemas/threads.py`)

11 Pydantic v2 models with validation constraints (length ≤ 200mm, segments 16–256, etc.)

### Seeds (`backend/app/seeds/threads.py`)

Idempotent seed function upserting thread specs into `ReferenceComponent` table.

### Frontend

- **Types:** `frontend/src/types/threads.ts` — TypeScript interfaces for all thread types
- **API Client:** `frontend/src/lib/api/threads.ts` — 7 functions using `/api/v2` base
- **Hooks:** `frontend/src/hooks/useThreads.ts` — React Query hooks for all endpoints
- **ThreadWizard:** 4-step dialog (Family → Size → Configure → Generate)
- **TapDrillReference:** Read-only table showing tap drill + 3 clearance hole sizes

### Modified Files

- `backend/app/cad/exceptions.py` — Added `ThreadDataError`, `ThreadGenerationError`
- `backend/app/api/v2/__init__.py` — Registered threads router

## Test Results

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Thread data library | 51 | All passing |
| Thread geometry generator | 54 | All passing |
| Print optimizer | 44 | All passing |
| API endpoints | 30 | All passing |
| ThreadWizard (frontend) | 12 | All passing |
| TapDrillReference (frontend) | 7 | All passing |
| **Total** | **198** | **All passing** |

## Security

- POST generation endpoints require JWT authentication via `get_current_user`
- All inputs validated via Pydantic constraints (bounded numerics, enum whitelists)
- Thread family/size validated against in-memory registry (whitelist approach)
- No user input used in file paths or shell commands
- Hard 60s timeout on geometry generation
- Structured logging on all generation requests

## Planning Documents

author: kogum4
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes Windows VEH lifecycle handling for repeated runtime/thread-env init-destroy cycles.

On Windows host integrations that repeatedly unload/reload WASM runtime users, stale VEH state could remain and later crash in `ntdll` exception dispatch.

## Reproduction (before)

On Windows, in a host-like lifecycle that repeatedly creates/destroys runtime usage contexts (including thread env init/destroy churn), intermittent crashes were observed in exception dispatch (`ntdll`, access violation path) after unload/reload cycles.

## Changes

File:
- `core/iwasm/common/wasm_runtime_common.c`

What changed:
- add Windows-only VEH ref count
- guard VEH lifecycle updates with a mutex
- register VEH only when ref count transitions `0 -> 1`
- remove VEH only when ref count transitions `1 -> 0`
- if `RemoveVectoredExceptionHandler` fails, keep retry-able ownership state instead of dropping handler state

## Behavior change

- Before: VEH lifecycle could become inconsistent under repeated init/destroy cycles, leading to intermittent post-unload crash behavior.
- After: VEH registration/removal is reference-counted and synchronized, with robust failure handling on removal.

## Validation

- rebuilt WAMR on Windows
- rebuilt downstream integration
- passed downstream C++ tests
- reran host-style repeated unload/reload + open/close loop; crash no longer reproduced in the previously failing scenario

## Notes

No new WAMR-internal test is included in this patch; validation was performed in the integration lifecycle where the issue reproduces.  
If maintainers prefer, I can submit a follow-up PR with a WAMR-side regression test for this lifecycle pattern.

author: oseltamivir
body:
## Motivation

The `bootstrap_room` buffer in `MetadataBuffers` was recently changed to `torch.uint64` dtype (#17430), but the scalar assignment in `set_buf` still overflows for values exceeding `2^63-1`:

```python
# This overflows when req.bootstrap_room > 2^63-1
self.bootstrap_room[req.metadata_buffer_index, 0] = req.bootstrap_room
```

PyTorch's `Tensor.__setitem__` converts Python int scalars through C `long long` (`THPUtils_unpackLong`) **regardless of tensor dtype**, causing `ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long`. This is a known PyTorch limitation: [pytorch/pytorch#159168](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/159168).

This affects PD disaggregation when external orchestrators (e.g. [NVIDIA Dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo)) generate `bootstrap_room` as random `u64` values — roughly 50% of values exceed signed int64 max.

```
ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long
  File "sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py", line 244, in set_buf
    self.bootstrap_room[req.metadata_buffer_index, 0] = (
```

## Modifications

Use `numpy` + `torch.from_numpy` + `copy_` to write the uint64 value as a tensor-to-tensor copy, bypassing PyTorch's broken scalar unpacking path entirely:

```python
_br = req.bootstrap_room if req.bootstrap_room is not None else 0
self.bootstrap_room[req.metadata_buffer_index, 0:1].copy_(
    torch.from_numpy(np.array([_br], dtype=np.uint64))
)
```

No changes needed on the decode side — `output_bootstrap_room[0].item()` on a `uint64` tensor already returns the correct unsigned Python int.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: GB200 multi-node
- **Model**: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (BF16)
- **Transfer backend**: NIXL (but affects all backends
- **Orchestrator**: NVIDIA Dynamo (`ai-dynamo/dynamo`), which generates `bootstrap_room` via `rand::rng().random::<u64>()` in Rust ([source](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/kv_router/prefill_router.rs#L311))

Relates to #19045

body:
### Motivation
- Закрепить доменный инвариант «у грузчика может быть не более одного активного заказа» и предотвратить ситуации, когда диспетчер может назначить/запустить одного и того же грузчика в нескольких заказах одновременно. 
- Устранить некорректный бейдж «Отклики», который иногда показывал неподтверждённые или stale значения.
- Сделать надёжный, без рывков и реверса, поиск по истории (корректная работа курсора и debounce).

### Description
- Введён typed-паттерн для операций выбора и старта заказа: `SelectApplicantResult` и `StartOrderResult` используются в соответствующих use-case (файлы: `SelectApplicantUseCase.kt`, `StartOrderUseCase.kt`), и конфликтные ситуации возвращают предсказуемые результат-значения вместо исключений. При конфликте SELECT возвращается `AlreadyAssigned`, при конфликте START — `AssigneeAlreadyBusy` (заказ не стартует). 
- Добавлен bulk-API в репозиторий для проверки занятости: `getBusyAssignments(loaderIds: Collection<String>): Map<String, Long>` и соответствующая реализация в DAO/репозитории (`AssignmentsDao.findActiveAssignmentsByLoaders`, `OrdersRepositoryImpl.getBusyAssignments`, тест/фейк-реализации). Это устраняет N+1 обращения при проверках занятости. 
- Responses UX: новый use-case `GetRespondersWithAvailabilityUseCase` делает bulk lookup занятости, `ResponsesViewModel` использует его и прокидывает флаг `isBusy` в `ResponseRowUiModel`; UI (`ResponsesScreen`) показывает метку «В работе» и отключает кнопку «+» для занятых грузчиков. 
- Badge «Отклики»: введён `ResponsesBadgeState(totalResponses:Int)` в `OrdersUiState`, badge считается только из активных/видимых заказов (sum of visible applicants для availableOrders), при NotSelected/смене пользователя состояние сбрасывается в 0; `MainScreen` читает новое поле. 
- История / поиск: в `DispatcherScreen` ввод теперь хранится локально как `TextFieldValue` (stabilizes selection/cursor), VM получает plain `String` и применяет `trim -> distinctUntilChanged -> debounce(250)` и тяжёлую фильтрацию/группировку выполняет в `Dispatchers.Default` через `mapLatest`, что устраняет реверс/рывки и снижает лаги. 
- Тесты: добавлены и обновлены юнит-тесты, покрывающие критичные инварианты и поведение UI-модели (см. список ниже). 
- Основные изменённые файлы (не исчерпывающий список):
  - app/src/main/java/.../SelectApplicantUseCase.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../StartOrderUseCase.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../GetRespondersWithAvailabilityUseCase.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../OrdersRepository.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../AssignmentsDao.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../OrdersRepositoryImpl.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../ResponsesViewModel.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../ResponsesUiState.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../OrdersViewModel.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../DispatcherScreen.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../ResponsesScreen.kt
  - app/src/main/java/.../ResponsesBadgeState.kt
  - тесты: несколько файлов в app/src/test/... (см. изменения в PR diff). 

### Testing
- Тесты добавлены/обновлены (unit):
  - `SelectUnselectApplicantUseCaseTest` — добавлен сценарий: при busy-грузчике `select()` возвращает `AlreadyAssigned` и репозиторий не мутируется. 
  - `StartOrderUseCaseBusyTest` — новый тест: если среди selected есть busy-грузчик, `start()` возвращает `AssigneeAlreadyBusy` и заказ не стартует. 
  - `OrdersViewModelTest` — проверяет корректность нового `responsesBadge.totalResponses` (пусто → 0, суммирование из активных заказов, reset при сбросе пользователя).
- Запуск автоматических тестов в этой среде не удался: команда `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` была запущена, но окружение не содержит корректного Gradle wrapper runtime (ошибка: "Could not find or load main class org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain"), поэтому unit-тесты в CI/локально не выполнялись здесь. 
- Рекомендация: запустить полную батарею unit-тестов в CI/local окружении с рабочим Gradle wrapper; все добавленные тесты предназначены для прохождения и покрывают критичные инварианты (select/start busy checks, badge computation, history search behaviour).
