- Pin `xcode-version` from `latest-stable` back to `16.4` in all iOS/tvOS build workflows
- Change default `runner-label` from `macos-latest` to `macos-15` in reusable workflow inputs and `deploy-static-main.yml` fallback
- Document macOS runner and Xcode version constraints in CLAUDE.md

## Context
The `macos-15` runner now ships Xcode 26.3 RC alongside 16.x, and `latest-stable` resolves to 26.3 RC — which is incompatible with Expo SDK 52 / React Native 0.76 (Apple skipped versions 17–25). This broke all iOS/tvOS builds in downstream branded app repos despite `PREFERRED_MACOS_RUNNER` already being set to `macos-15`.

Build log from cust-app-xrtube confirming the issue: https://github.com/OwnTube-tv/cust-app-xrtube/actions/runs/22347211910/job/64664815299

Reverts the `latest-stable` change from #463. Fixes #485.

## Test plan
- [ ] Trigger iOS simulator build from a downstream branded app repo (e.g. cust-app-xrtube) and verify it completes successfully
- [ ] Verify `grep -r "latest-stable" .github/workflows/` returns no results
- [ ] Verify `grep -r "macos-latest" .github/workflows/` returns no results from iOS/tvOS/deploy workflows

author: buropotok
body:
### Причина
- При сборке `word/numbering.xml` критично гарантировать, что для каждого уровня списка внутри одного `abstractNum` присутствует ровно один `<w:lvl w:ilvl="...">`.
- Дублирующиеся уровни (в том числе при эквивалентных ключах вроде `"1"` и `"01"`) могут приводить к неверной интерпретации мультилевел-геометрии в Word.

### Что исправлено
- В `src/reconstructor.py` (`_build_numbering_xml`) добавлена локальная защита от дублей `ilvl` в рамках одного `abstractNum`.
- Перед эмиссией `<w:lvl>` уровень нормализуется и проверяется через `seen_ilvls`; повторные значения пропускаются.
- Все элементы уровня (`start`, `numFmt`, `lvlText`, и опциональные `tab/lvlJc/suff/pStyle/pPr/rPr`) продолжают писаться в единственный `lvl_el`.

### Как проверить
1. Запустить реконструкцию на RAW с мультилевел-нумерацией.
2. Открыть `word/numbering.xml` и убедиться, что в каждом `abstractNum` нет дубликатов `<w:lvl w:ilvl="X">`.
3. Проверить выравнивание уровней (например `1)`, `2)`, `a)`) в reconstructed DOCX.

### Scope
- Изменён только `src/reconstructor.py`.

author: copilot
body:
`reflect.StructOf` requires `PkgPath` to be set for lowercase-named fields, which causes Go's reflection API to treat them as unexported. PR #846's `IsExported()` check in the checker then silently skips these fields, producing an "unknown name" compile error for what is a valid runtime-accessible field.

## Changes

- **`checker/nature/utils.go`**: Scope the `IsExported()` guard to named struct types only (`s.rType.PkgPath() != ""`). Anonymous types (including all `reflect.StructOf` outputs, whose type-level `PkgPath()` is always `""`) allow all fields through. The #844 fix for regular Go structs is fully preserved.

- **`vm/runtime/runtime.go`**: Add exported `ValueInterface(reflect.Value) any` that falls back to type-specific getters (`Bool()`, `Int()`, `String()`, etc.) when `Interface()` would panic on an unexported field. Update `FetchField` and `Fetch` to use it; extend the `IsExported` gate in `Fetch` to also pass anonymous-struct fields.

- **`builtin/lib.go`**: Mirror the same gate change and switch to `runtime.ValueInterface` in the `get` function.

## Example

```go
dynType := reflect.StructOf([]reflect.StructField{
    {Name: "value", Type: reflect.TypeFor[bool](), PkgPath: "github.com/some/package"},
})
env := reflect.New(dynType).Elem().Interface()

// Was: "unknown name value" in v1.17.7+
// Now: compiles and evaluates correctly
program, err := expr.Compile("value", expr.Env(env))
result, err := expr.Run(program, env) // → false (zero value)
```

`ValueInterface` covers all primitive kinds; non-primitive unexported fields in anonymous structs (e.g. nested struct, slice) will still panic with a descriptive message, as there is no way to retrieve them without `unsafe`.

author: copilot
body:
The engine conflated thermal mass (τ/inertia) with fabric heat loss — solid masonry was implicitly scored "best" because high mass ≠ low heat loss. This splits them into two independent physics dimensions.

## New: `FabricModelModule`

`src/engine/modules/FabricModelModule.ts` exports `runFabricModelV1(input)`:

```ts
// Solid brick: heavy inertia but still high heat loss when uninsulated
runFabricModelV1({
  wallType: 'solid_masonry', insulationLevel: 'poor',
  glazing: 'single', roofInsulation: 'poor', airTightness: 'leaky',
  thermalMass: 'heavy',
})
// → { heatLossBand: 'very_high', lossIndex: 0.74, tauHours: 34, inertiaBand: 'moderate' }
```

- **Heat-loss** (`heatLossBand` / `lossIndex`): weighted score across `wallType + insulationLevel + glazing + roofInsulation + airTightness`
- **Inertia** (`tauHours` / `inertiaBand`): derived from `thermalMass × insulationLevel × airTightness` — explicitly not an efficiency signal

## Contract (`EngineInputV2_3`)

Added optional `building` sub-object:
- `building.fabric.{ wallType, insulationLevel, glazing, roofInsulation, airTightness }`
- `building.thermalMass` — independent of wall type
- `FullEngineResultCore.fabricModelV1?: FabricModelV1Result`

## Engine + OutputBuilder

- `Engine.ts` computes `fabricModelV1` when `input.building` is present
- `OutputBuilder.ts` emits two context bullets — both labelled **"modelled estimate"**

## Step 1 UI rewrite (`FullSurveyStepper.tsx`)

- **Section A (heat loss)**: wall type · insulation · glazing · roof · airtightness
- **Section B (inertia)**: standalone thermal mass selector; τ now derived from `thermalMass` not `wallType`
- Right panel shows **two** live outputs: heat-loss band + τ/inertiaBand
- `FABRIC_PRESETS` updated to seed all new fields on "Load example"

## Removed

- Hardcoded `£40/yr "British Gas Mixergy Extra rebate"` badge and `british_gas` installer dropdown option
- "Full Job (British Gas)" label → **"Low flow temp design (35–40°C)"**; "Fast Fit" → **"High temp retrofit (50–55°C)"**

feat(build): fix TS6133 unused pressureAnalysis in OutputBuilder

Change
- In src/engine/OutputBuilder.ts, remove unused `pressureAnalysis` destructure OR rename to `_pressureAnalysis`.

Implementation
1) Open src/engine/OutputBuilder.ts
2) Find the line that looks like:
   const { ..., pressureAnalysis, ... } = core;
3) Either:
   A) Delete `pressureAnalysis,` from the destructure list; OR
   B) Rename it to `_pressureAnalysis` (and keep it unused for now).

Notes
- This is a compile-only failure; no runtime logic change intended.
- Prefer option A unless you’re about to surface pressureAnalysis in visuals/bullets in the next PR.


⸻

2) “Fabric madness” fix (the real one)

You’ve nailed the core issue: thermal inertia (mass/τ) ≠ heat loss. Solid brick can have high mass and still leak heat like a sieve if uninsulated / leaky.

Right now Step 1 effectively lets “solid masonry” look “best”, because the UI is mixing “good to live with (inertia)” with “cheap to run (fabric heat loss)”.

What the model should do

Split building physics into two independent outputs:
	1.	Heat-loss driver (how hard the building leaks energy)

	•	wall insulation / wall type (U-ish proxy)
	•	roof insulation proxy
	•	glazing proxy
	•	airtightness / infiltration proxy
	•	exposure proxy (optional)

	2.	Thermal inertia driver (how spiky demand feels)

	•	thermal mass (light / medium / heavy)
	•	then derive τ from mass + insulation + airtightness (or keep τ as an output, not an input)

So: solid brick = “heavy mass” (inertia) but could still be “high heat loss” until insulation/airtightness improves.

⸻

PR: Fix Fabric Inputs so they match reality

Outcome
	•	UI stops presenting “construction type = performance”
	•	Engine receives a fabric loss estimate and a thermal inertia estimate
	•	ASHP/boiler behaviours can react differently to each (exactly what you wanted)

Codex-ready

feat(fabric): separate heat-loss fabric model from thermal inertia (mass/τ)

Problem
- Step 1 conflates thermal mass (τ/inertia) with fabric heat loss, making solid masonry appear “best” even when uninsulated/leaky.
- We need independent levers for “how much heat leaks” vs “how spiky the demand feels”.

Contract changes (EngineInputV2_3)
1) Add fabric inputs (loss-focused):
- building.fabric.wallType?: 'solid_masonry' | 'cavity_unfilled' | 'cavity_filled' | 'timber_frame' | 'unknown'
- building.fabric.insulationLevel?: 'poor' | 'moderate' | 'good' | 'exceptional' | 'unknown'
- building.fabric.glazing?: 'single' | 'double' | 'triple' | 'unknown'
- building.fabric.roofInsulation?: 'poor' | 'moderate' | 'good' | 'unknown'
- building.fabric.airTightness?: 'leaky' | 'average' | 'tight' | 'passive' | 'unknown'

2) Add inertia input (mass-focused):
- building.thermalMass?: 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy' | 'unknown'

Engine: new module
- src/engine/modules/FabricModelModule.ts
Exports runFabricModelV1(input) returning:
{
  heatLossBand: 'very_high'|'high'|'moderate'|'low'|'very_low'|'unknown',
  lossIndex: number | null,          // 0–1-ish proxy (internal)
  tauHours: number | null,           // derived (inertia), not “picked from decade”
  inertiaBand: 'spiky'|'moderate'|'stable'|'unknown',
  notes: string[]                    // customer-safe explainers
}

Logic (deterministic, simple, honest)
- lossIndex derived from wallType + insulation + glazing + roof + airtightness
- thermal mass sets inertia baseline; tauHours = f(thermalMass, insulationLevel, airtightness)
- IMPORTANT: tauHours does not imply “efficient”; it only implies “slow response”.

Wiring
- Engine.ts: compute fabricModelV1 and store in FullEngineResultCore
- OutputBuilder.ts:
  - Add 1–2 bullets:
    - “Fabric heat-loss estimate: High/Moderate/Low (modelled).”
    - “Thermal inertia: Heavy/Medium/Light — affects how spiky heating feels (modelled).”
  - Feed tauHours into any existing response-curve visuals.
- Any ASHP suitability logic that currently uses τ as a “goodness” signal must instead use:
  - heatLossBand for running cost / required output
  - inertiaBand/tauHours only for “control style / comfort profile” messaging

UI: Step 1 rewrite (FullSurveyStepper.tsx)
- Replace current “archetype cards” with 2 sections:
  A) Fabric heat-loss controls (wall type, insulation, glazing, roof, airtightness)
  B) Thermal inertia (thermal mass selector)
- Right-side panel shows TWO outputs:
  - Heat-loss band (Very high → Very low)
  - τ badge + “response feel” (spiky vs stable) + existing decay chart

Remove
- Any decade-labelled presets as primary selection
Keep
- Preset buttons as “Load example” only (pr...

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduz um serviço de localização de CDs com um pipeline orientado por API para upload de dados, previsão de demanda, cálculo de custos de transporte, otimização de locais de CDs e persistência e auditoria das execuções de análise.

Novos recursos:
- Adiciona uma aplicação FastAPI com endpoints para enviar conjuntos de dados de entrada, executar análises de otimização síncronas/assíncronas, consultar status/resultados de execuções e expor métricas básicas.
- Implementa um mecanismo de otimização baseado em MILP com fallback ganancioso (*greedy*), utilitários de simulação de cenários e geração de relatórios para sites selecionados, alocações e detalhamento de custos.
- Introduz cálculo de matriz de custos com backends de roteamento plugáveis (haversine, OSRM, GraphHopper) e previsão de demanda com *clustering* e fallbacks Prophet/SARIMAX.
- Adiciona uma camada de validação para clientes, sites, fornecedores e regras fiscais usando contratos Pydantic, incluindo *stubs* de geocodificação e saídas em parquet limpas.
- Persiste o estado de projetos e execuções por meio de um repositório leve baseado em SQLite e trilha de auditoria JSONL apenas-apêndice (*append-only*) para eventos de governança.

Melhorias:
- Adiciona *logging* estruturado em JSON com mascaramento de campos sensíveis e o integra ao ciclo de vida da aplicação FastAPI.
- Fornece ajudantes de ingestão e exportação de modelos CSV para padronizar os formatos de dados de entrada.
- Documenta a execução local e baseada em Docker, uso da API, configuração e próximos passos voltados à produção para escalabilidade e governança.

Build:
- Adiciona Dockerfile do backend e configuração de docker-compose para executar a API junto com serviços de suporte e volumes compartilhados.
- Define dependências Python para o serviço de backend em um arquivo de requisitos dedicado.

CI:
- Adiciona fluxo de trabalho do GitHub Actions para instalar dependências e executar a suíte de testes do backend em *pushes* e *pull requests*.

Documentação:
- Adiciona README do projeto descrevendo a API do CD Locator, principais endpoints, opções de configuração e interpretação das saídas.
- Adiciona documento NEXT_STEPS descrevendo futuras melhorias de robustez para produção e trabalhos de integração.

Testes:
- Adiciona teste de pipeline de ponta a ponta com exemplo simplificado que exercita validação, previsão, cálculo de matriz de custos, otimização e endpoints da API, ignorando quando pandas não estiver disponível.
- Adiciona testes de unidade para o otimizador, a fim de comparar custos MILP vs ganancioso (*greedy*), e para o validador, para verificar o comportamento de geocodificação e as saídas limpas.

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a CD locator service with an API-driven pipeline for uploading data, forecasting demand, computing transport costs, optimizing DC locations, and persisting and auditing analysis runs.

New Features:
- Add FastAPI application with endpoints to upload input datasets, run synchronous/asynchronous optimization analyses, query run status/results, and expose basic metrics.
- Implement MILP-based optimization engine with greedy fallback, scenario simulation utilities, and report generation for selected sites, allocations, and cost breakdowns.
- Introduce cost matrix calculation with pluggable routing backends (haversine, OSRM, GraphHopper) and demand forecasting with clustering and Prophet/SARIMAX fallbacks.
- Add validation layer for customers, sites, suppliers, and tax rules using Pydantic contracts, including geocoding stubs and cleaned parquet outputs.
- Persist project and run state via a lightweight SQLite-backed store and append-only JSONL audit trail for governance events.

Enhancements:
- Add structured JSON logging with masking of sensitive fields and wire it into the FastAPI app lifecycle.
- Provide ingestion helpers and CSV template export to standardize input data formats.
- Document local and Docker-based execution, API usage, configuration, and production-oriented next steps for scaling and governance.

Build:
- Add backend Dockerfile and docker-compose setup to run the API alongside supporting services and shared volumes.
- Define Python dependencies for the backend service in a dedicated requirements file.

CI:
- Add GitHub Actions workflow to install dependencies and run the backend test suite on pushes and pull requests.

Documentation:
- Add project README describing the CD Locator API, main endpoints, configuration options, and output interpretation.
- Add NEXT_STEPS document outlining future production hardening and integration work.

Tests:
- Add end-to-end toy pipeline test that exercises validation, forecasting, cost matrix calculation, optimization, and API endpoints, skipping when pandas is unavailable.
- Add unit tests for the optimizer to compare MILP vs greedy costs and for the validator to assert geocoding behavior and cleaned outputs.

author: lenaxia
body:
## Summary

- Adds `mendabot.io/enabled: "false"` annotation support — suppresses all investigations for a resource permanently
- Adds `mendabot.io/skip-until: "YYYY-MM-DD"` annotation support — suppresses investigations until the end of the given date (inclusive, midnight UTC)
- Adds `mendabot.io/priority: "critical"` annotation support — bypasses the stabilisation window for immediate investigation

## Changes

### `internal/domain/annotations.go` (new)
Three typed constants (`AnnotationEnabled`, `AnnotationSkipUntil`, `AnnotationPriority`) and `ShouldSkip(annotations map[string]string, now time.Time) bool` helper. Pure domain logic, no external imports beyond `time`.

### All 6 native providers (`pod`, `deployment`, `statefulset`, `job`, `node`, `pvc`)
`domain.ShouldSkip(obj.GetAnnotations(), time.Now())` added as the **first statement** in each `ExtractFinding`, before any type assertion. Returns `(nil, nil)` when suppression is active.

### `internal/provider/provider.go`
`priorityCritical := obj.GetAnnotations()[domain.AnnotationPriority] == "critical"` guard wraps the stabilisation window block. When `priority=critical`, `firstSeen` is never consulted and no requeue is issued — execution falls through directly to dedup + RemediationJob creation.

## Tests

- 8 unit tests for `ShouldSkip` (boundary cases, nil map, malformed date)
- 2 annotation tests per provider (12 total) using **unhealthy** objects that prove the gate fires
- 2 unit tests for priority bypass in reconciler
- 1 e2e integration test: real `podProvider` + annotated CrashLoopBackOff pod + reconciler → zero RemediationJobs

All 12 packages pass `go test -timeout 60s -race -count=1 ./...`, race detector clean.

## Closes

Epic 16 (FT-A2) — all 3 stories complete.

body:
This PR updates [SQLAlchemy](https://pypi.org/project/SQLAlchemy) from **1.3.19** to **2.0.47**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.0.47
   ```
   :released: February 24, 2026

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm
        :tickets: 13104

        Fixed issue when using ORM mappings with Python 3.14's :pep:`649` feature
        that no longer requires "future annotations", where the ORM's introspection
        of the ``__init__`` method of mapped classes would fail if non-present
        identifiers in annotations were present.  The vendored ``getfullargspec()``
        method has been amended to use ``Format.FORWARDREF`` under Python 3.14 to
        prevent resolution of names that aren't present.


    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 13105

        Fixed an issue in the PostgreSQL dialect where foreign key constraint
        reflection would incorrectly swap or fail to capture ``onupdate`` and
        ``ondelete`` values when these clauses appeared in a different order than
        expected in the constraint definition. This issue primarily affected
        PostgreSQL-compatible databases such as CockroachDB, which may return ``ON
        DELETE`` before ``ON UPDATE`` in the constraint definition string. The
        reflection logic now correctly parses both clauses regardless of their
        ordering.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 13107

        Fixed issue in the :ref:`engine_insertmanyvalues` feature where using
        PostgreSQL's ``ON CONFLICT`` clause with
        :paramref:`_dml.Insert.returning.sort_by_parameter_order` enabled would
        generate invalid SQL when the insert used an implicit sentinel (server-side
        autoincrement primary key). The generated SQL would incorrectly declare a
        sentinel counter column in the ``imp_sen`` table alias without providing
        corresponding values in the ``VALUES`` clause, leading to a
        ``ProgrammingError`` indicating column count mismatch. The fix allows batch
        execution mode when ``embed_values_counter`` is active, as the embedded
        counter provides the ordering capability needed even with upsert behaviors,
        rather than unnecessarily downgrading to row-at-a-time execution.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 13110

        Fixed issue where :meth:`_postgresql.Insert.on_conflict_do_update`
        parameters were not respecting compilation options such as
        ``literal_binds=True``.  Pull request courtesy Loïc Simon.


    .. change::
        :tags: bug, sqlite
        :tickets: 13110

        Fixed issue where :meth:`_sqlite.Insert.on_conflict_do_update`
        parameters were not respecting compilation options such as
        ``literal_binds=True``.  Pull request courtesy Loïc Simon.

    .. change::
        :tags: usecase, engine
        :tickets: 13116

        The connection object returned by :meth:`_engine.Engine.raw_connection`
        now supports the context manager protocol, automatically returning the
        connection to the pool when exiting the context.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 13130

        Fixed issue where :meth:`_postgresql.Insert.on_conflict_do_update`
        using parametrized bound parameters in the ``set_`` clause would fail
        when used with executemany batching. For dialects that use the
        ``use_insertmanyvalues_wo_returning`` optimization (psycopg2),
        insertmanyvalues is now disabled when there is an ON CONFLICT clause.
        For cases with RETURNING, row-at-a-time mode is used when the SET
        clause contains parametrized bindparams (bindparams that receive
        values from the parameters dict), ensuring each row's parameters are
        correctly applied. ON CONFLICT statements using expressions like
        ``excluded.<column>`` continue to batch normally.


    .. change::
        :tags: bug, sqlite
        :tickets: 13130

        Fixed issue where :meth:`_sqlite.Insert.on_conflict_do_update`
        using parametrized bound parameters in the ``set_`` clause would fail
        when used with executemany batching. Row-at-a-time mode is now used
        for ON CONFLICT statements with RETURNING that contain parametrized
        bindparams, ensuring each row's parameters are correctly applied. ON
        CONFLICT statements using expressions like ``excluded.<column>``
        continue to batch normally.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, mysql
        :tickets: 13134

        Fixed issue where DDL compilation options were registered to the hard-coded
        dialect name ``mysql``. This made it awkward for MySQL-derived dialects
        like MariaDB, StarRocks, etc. to work with such options when different sets
        of options exist for different platforms. Options are now registered under
        the actual dialect name, and a fallback was added to help avoid errors when
        an option does not exist for that dialect.

        To maintain backwards compatibility, when using the MariaDB dialect with
        the options ``mysql_with_parser`` or ``mysql_using`` without also specifying
        the corresponding ``mariadb_`` prefixed options, a deprecation warning will
        be emitted. The ``mysql_`` prefixed options will continue to work during
        the deprecation period. Users should update their code to additionally
        specify ``mariadb_with_parser`` and ``mariadb_using`` when using the
        ``mariadb://`` dialect, or specify both options to support both dialects.

        Pull request courtesy Tiansu Yu.

.. changelog::
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.0.46
   ```
   :released: January 21, 2026

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, sqlite
        :tickets: 13039

        Fixed issue in the aiosqlite driver where SQLAlchemy's setting of
        aiosqlite's worker thread to "daemon" stopped working because the aiosqlite
        architecture moved the location of the worker thread in version 0.22.0.
        This "daemon" flag is necessary so that a program is able to exit if the
        SQLite connection itself was not explicitly closed, which is particularly
        likely with SQLAlchemy as it maintains SQLite connections in a connection
        pool.  While it's perfectly fine to call :meth:`.AsyncEngine.dispose`
        before program exit, this is not historically or technically necessary for
        any driver of any known backend, since a primary feature of relational
        databases is durability.  The change also implements support for
        "terminate" with aiosqlite when using version version 0.22.1 or greater,
        which implements a sync ``.stop()`` method.

    .. change::
        :tags: usecase, mssql
        :tickets: 13045

        Added support for the ``IF EXISTS`` clause when dropping indexes on SQL
        Server 2016 (13.x) and later versions. The :paramref:`.DropIndex.if_exists`
        parameter is now honored by the SQL Server dialect, allowing conditional
        index drops that will not raise an error if the index does not exist.
        Pull request courtesy Edgar Ramírez Mondragón.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 13059

        Fixed issue where PostgreSQL JSONB operators
        :meth:`_postgresql.JSONB.Comparator.path_match` and
        :meth:`_postgresql.JSONB.Comparator.path_exists` were applying incorrect
        ``VARCHAR`` casts to the right-hand side operand when used with newer
        PostgreSQL drivers such as psycopg. The operators now indicate the
        right-hand type as ``JSONPATH``, which currently results in no casting
        taking place, but is also compatible with explicit casts if the
        implementation were require it at a later point.

author: tzjames
body:
### Features and Changes
`sql-formatter` is slow and has brought down the website before when we allowed it to format large queries.  Also the version we had didn't support Clickhouse, but we have upgraded in this PR to a version that does. 
`polyglot` is a [new package ](https://github.com/tobilg/polyglot) that does the formatting much more quickly. However it can't parse everything yet so we fallback to `sql-formatter`.  

Unfortunately polyglot ESM version has a top-level await. Since shared package is CJS, the shared sql.ts can't load polyglot EMS version from the front end.  For now we check whether the function exists, and so for the front-end we just fall back to the sql-formatter.  As most front-end queries are small, the sql-formatter probably works fine.  If we ever change our mind we have two options:
- Make polyglot a dependency of front-end and just import it and use it there instead of calling the shared version.
- Compile a ESM version of sql.ts which the front-end uses, in addition to the cjs for the back-end.  Then import it dynamically if and only if window is set (being called from the front-end).  See https://github.com/growthbook/growthbook/pull/5406 for a possible implementation)

In full this PR:
- Adds polyglot to the sharedPackage with a fallback if polyglot doesn't load ok (front-end) or if it fails to format to sql-formatter.
- Adds metrics for formatting so we can keep track of how often formatting succeeds
- Adds simple tests to confirm new functionality is working.
- Updates sql-formatter

### Testing
`pnpm build`
`pnpm start:with-datadog`
start datadog agent locally
refresh an experiment and see new formatting metrics in datadog.
Go create a new dashboard and make a new sql query, type in a query and click format and see it format it in the 
For sql-formatter format:
```
SELECT
  *
FROM
  growthbook.public.pages
LIMIT
  1;
```

If polyglot formatted it, it would have looked like:
```
SELECT
  *
FROM growthbook.public.pages
LIMIT 1;
```
However that doesn't work on the front-end.

body:
## Summary
Without gradient clipping, training on truncated or ill-conditioned distributions can produce exploding gradients that destabilise optimisation.

**Changes:**
- Add `max_grad_norm` (`Optional[float]`, default `None`) to `TRAINER_DEFAULTS`
- Apply `clip_grad_norm_` inside `make_closure` after `loss.backward()` and before returning, so clipping is applied on every optimizer step (including multi-step optimizers like L-BFGS)
- When `max_grad_norm is None` (the default), no clipping is applied and existing behaviour is unchanged

**Usage:**
```python
args = Parameters({"optimizer": "sgd", "lr": 1e-2, "max_grad_norm": 1.0, ...})
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Train with `max_grad_norm=1.0` and verify all recorded `grad_norms` are ≤ 1.0
- [ ] Train without `max_grad_norm` — confirm behaviour is identical to before

author: le-who
body:
This PR fixes a High-severity Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the `markdown_to_html` utility function.

**Vulnerability Details:**
The previous implementation of `markdown_to_html` used a simple regex to replace Markdown links `[text](url)` with HTML `<a>` tags without validating the URL scheme. This allowed attackers to inject malicious schemes such as `javascript:alert(1)` or `data:text/html,...`.

**Fix:**
I have modified `app/utils/text_format.py` to:
1.  Import `urlparse` from `urllib.parse`.
2.  Use a callback function in `re.sub` to inspect the URL before replacement.
3.  Enforce a strict allowlist of schemes: `http`, `https`, `tg`, and `mailto`.
4.  Strip the link (returning only the text) if the scheme is not in the allowlist.

**Verification:**
*   Added `tests/test_text_format.py::test_markdown_to_html_xss_prevention` which tests:
    *   Valid schemes (`http`, `https`, `tg`, `mailto`) are preserved.
    *   Dangerous schemes (`javascript`, `vbscript`, `data`, `file`) are stripped.
    *   Relative URLs (empty scheme) are stripped (policy choice for this bot context).
    *   Case insensitivity (e.g., `JaVaScRiPt`).
*   Ran existing tests to ensure no regressions.

body:
# Security Vulnerability Fix

## 🔒 Vulnerability Summary

**CVE ID:** CVE-2026-26996  
**Severity:** High  
**Package:** `minimatch`  
**CVSS Score:** 8.7 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N)

### Description
**Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)** vulnerability that allows attackers to cause denial of service by providing specially crafted glob patterns with many consecutive `*` wildcards followed by a literal character that doesn't appear in the test string. 

When minimatch compiles a glob pattern, each `*` becomes `[^/]*?` in the generated regex. For patterns like `***************X***`, the regex engine must try every possible way to distribute characters across all the `[^/]*?` groups before concluding no match exists. This results in **exponential time complexity O(4^N)** where N is the number of `*` characters.

**Attack Vector:** Any application that passes user-controlled strings to `minimatch()` as the pattern argument is vulnerable, including:
- File search/filter UIs that accept glob patterns
- `.gitignore`-style filtering with user-defined rules
- Build tools that accept glob configuration
- Any API that exposes glob matching to untrusted input

---

## 🔄 Changes Made

### Dependency Update
- **Package:** `minimatch`
- **Previous Version:** `9.0.5`
- **Wiz Recommended Version:** `10.2.1`
- **Actual Version Applied:** `10.2.2`
- **Update Type:** Major version update (9.x → 10.x)

### Version Selection Rationale
Wiz recommended 10.2.1 as the minimum fixed version, but 10.2.2 is the latest backward-compatible patch version available in the 10.2.x line. Using 10.2.2 ensures we get the security fix plus any additional bug fixes and improvements included in the latest patch release.

### Files Modified
- `package.json` - Added `resolutions` field to force minimatch to 10.2.2
- `yarn.lock` - Updated all minimatch dependencies to 10.2.2 (consolidated from versions 3.1.2, 5.1.6, and 9.0.5)

---

## 🛡️ Security Impact

### What This Fixes
1. **The Vulnerability**: Inefficient regular expression complexity in glob pattern matching that allows exponential backtracking when processing patterns with many consecutive wildcards.

2. **The Risk**: Attackers could exploit this by providing crafted glob patterns (e.g., through search filters or configuration files) to cause the application to hang or become unresponsive, effectively creating a denial of service condition. With N=15 wildcards, a single `minimatch()` call takes ~2 seconds. With N=34, it hangs indefinitely.

3. **The Fix**: Version 10.2.1+ includes a fix that prevents exponential backtracking in the regex engine when processing patterns with repeated wildcards, as documented in [commit 2e111f3](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/commit/2e111f3a79abc00fa73110195de2c0f2351904f5).

### Breaking Changes
- [x] This update includes breaking changes - Major version jump from 9.x to 10.x
  - However, minimatch is a **transitive dependency** (not directly used by this codebase)
  - It's pulled in through `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` and other dev dependencies
  - The yarn `resolutions` field forces all consumers to use the patched version
  - No code changes required in this repository

### Affected Components
This is a **transitive dependency** used by:
- `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` (multiple instances)
- `eslint` and related plugins
- `jest` test infrastructure
- `ts-jest` build tooling

These are all **development dependencies** used for linting, testing, and building. The vulnerability would only be exploitable if an attacker could control glob patterns passed to these tools during development/CI, which is a low-risk scenario.

---

## ✅ Validation

### Automated Checks
- [x] Dependency version updated in package.json (via resolutions)
- [x] Lock file regenerated successfully
- [x] Package manager resolved dependencies without conflicts (warnings expected for cross-major-version resolutions)

### Compatibility Assessment
Based on the dependency chain analysis, all affected packages are development dependencies. The forced resolution to 10.2.2 consolidates three different major versions (3.x, 5.x, 9.x) into a single patched version. While this is a major version jump, minimatch maintains a stable API and the yarn resolutions mechanism handles the compatibility layer.

---

## 📚 References

- **CVE Details:** https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-26996
- **GitHub Advisory:** https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26
- **Security Fix Commit:** https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/commit/2e111f3a79abc00fa73110195de2c0f2351904f5
- **Package Changelog:** https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/releases
- **JIRA Ticket:** ENG-41388

---

For questions or issues, please contact the Security or DevOps team.

brew install ghinks/review-classification

Homebrew resolves `owner/name` → `github.com/owner/homebrew-name` automatically, so no explicit `brew tap` is needed.

body:
## Summary

- Return 503 when rebuild is triggered but library isn't initialized yet (matching the create endpoint behavior)
- Move `clone_library` call before setting workspace status to "Building" so no status rollback is needed on early return

## Problem

When the server restarts, the library is initialized asynchronously (git clone in a background task). There's a ~2-3 second window where the HTTP server accepts connections but the library isn't ready. If a rebuild is triggered during this window, all init script fragments are silently skipped — the workspace ends up "ready" but missing SSH keys, git config, base packages, etc.

The create endpoint already guards against this with a 503 response, but the rebuild endpoint did not.

## Reproduction

Confirmed on dev deployment:
1. Remove library directory, restart server
2. Immediately trigger rebuild → journal shows `WARN Init script fragments specified but library not available`
3. Workspace completes as "ready" but `/root/.ssh/` doesn't exist, git isn't installed

- [x] `cargo test` — 420 tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean

Read on for the full breakdown! > \[!NOTE] > When in doubt, check the [examples](https://redirect.github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/tree/v2-exp/examples) for reference — they've all been updated for v2. #### 🏠 New Home Bubbles v2 now lives at `charm.land`: ```go import "charm.land/bubbles/v2" ``` All sub-packages follow the same pattern: `charm.land/bubbles/v2/viewport`, `charm.land/bubbles/v2/list`, etc. #### 🎨 Light and Dark Styles Some Bubbles, like `help`, offer default styles for both light and dark backgrounds. Since Lip Gloss v2 removes `AdaptiveColor`, choosing light or dark is now a manual process. You've got a couple of options. ##### 🎩 The Best Way Have Bubble Tea query the background color for you. This properly queries the correct inputs and outputs, and happens in lockstep with your application: ```go func (m model) Init() tea.Cmd { return tea.RequestBackgroundColor } func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { switch msg := msg.(type) { case tea.BackgroundColorMsg: m.help.Styles = help.DefaultStyles(msg.IsDark()) return m, nil } // ... } ``` If you're using [Wish](https://redirect.github.com/charmbracelet/wish) you *must* do it this way to get the background color of the client. ##### 🤠 The Quick Way Use the `compat` package in Lip Gloss. It's less recommended because it contains blocking I/O that operates independently of Bubble Tea, and when used with Wish it won't detect the client's background: ```go import "charm.land/lipgloss/v2/compat" var hasDarkBG = compat.HasDarkBackground() h := help.New() h.Styles = help.DefaultStyles(hasDarkBG) ``` ##### 👀 Or Just Pick One ```go h.Styles = help.DefaultLightStyles() // light mode! h.Styles = help.DefaultDarkStyles() // jk dark mode ``` This pattern applies to `help`, `list`, `textarea`, and `textinput`. #### 🔑 The Init You Know and Love is Back After experimenting with a few different forms of `Init` during the alphas, we decided the v1 signature was the right call after all. `Init` was a bit too redundant for our tastes given that initialization already happens in `New`: ```go func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd ``` #### ✨ The Big Highlights ##### Getters and Setters Everywhere All components now use getter/setter methods instead of exported `Width` and `Height` fields. This lets us do internal bookkeeping when things change, and it makes the API consistent across every Bubble: ```go // Before vp.Width = 40 fmt.Println(vp.Width) // After vp.SetWidth(40) fmt.Println(vp.Width()) ``` Affected: `filepicker`, `help`, `progress`, `table`, `textinput`, `viewport`. ##### Functional Options Constructors now use the functional options pattern instead of positional args or separate constructor functions: ```go vp := viewport.New(viewport.WithWidth(80), viewport.WithHeight(24)) sw := stopwatch.New(stopwatch.WithInterval(500 * time.Millisecond)) t := timer.New(30*time.Second, timer.WithInterval(100*time.Millisecond)) ``` ##### DefaultKeyMap is a Function Now All `DefaultKeyMap` package-level variables are now functions, so you get fresh values every time: ```go km := textinput.DefaultKeyMap() // was textinput.DefaultKeyMap km := textarea.DefaultKeyMap() // was textarea.DefaultKeyMap km := paginator.DefaultKeyMap() // was paginator.DefaultKeyMap ``` ##### Real Cursor Support 🖱️ Both `textarea` and `textinput` now support real terminal cursors! The feature is opt-in, so by default your programs will continue to use the easy-breezy virtual cursor. Set `VirtualCursor` to `false` and use `Model.Cursor()` for t

author: fmmartinez
body:
### Motivation
- Allow focused mapping initialization to pick one occupied state at random from a user-specified set so ensemble workflows can start trajectories with different focused states without changing the CLI per-run.

### Description
- Added a new CLI option `--occupied-state-set` to `generate_solvent_initial_config.py` which accepts a comma-separated list of 1-based state indices and is parsed by `_parse_occupied_state_set`.
- Converted and validated the provided indices to zero-based `occupied_state_choices` and passed them into `run_nve_md(...)` so dynamics can receive the choice set.
- Extended `run_nve_md` in `pbme/dynamics.py` with an `occupied_state_choices` parameter and used the mapping RNG (seeded by `--mapping-seed`) to randomly select `selected_occupied_state` from the choices when `mapping_init_mode == 'focused'` before sampling focused mapping variables.
- Updated logging and trajectory comment output to report the actually selected occupied state (`occ=...`) and added user-facing startup messages that indicate when a random focused-state set was provided.

### Testing
- Compiled updated modules with `python -m compileall generate_solvent_initial_config.py pbme/dynamics.py` and the compilation completed successfully.
- Ran single-trajectory spot checks using the Python backend with `generate_solvent_initial_config.py --mapping-init-mode focused --occupied-state-set 1,3 --mapping-seed <seed> ...` and observed differing `occ` values across different `--mapping-seed` runs, confirming random selection from the provided set.
- Performed a multi-seed loop (`mapping_seed=100..110`) that produced both `occ=1` and `occ=3`, confirming per-trajectory random selection behavior; all runs using the Python backend succeeded.
- The Numba-accelerated backend was not exercised in these spot checks (environment uses the Python backend).

To ensure that all generated go files are free of compilation errors, I have added a preflight check that compiles them prior to officially writing them. It can be bypassed using a config flag.

Locally generation passes compilation checks:
`make generate`
`make regenerate-golden-test-files`
If I add a bug that causes a compilation error, the check fails as expected

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complete Slack Daily Summary system that automatically fetches messages from Slack channels, categorizes them using Claude AI, and generates a beautiful Apple-style HTML dashboard. The tool can optionally push categorized items to Notion.

## Key Changes

- **Slack Client** (`lib/slack-client.js`) — Fetches recent messages from Slack channels with thread replies and reactions, includes user resolution and rate limiting
- **AI Categorizer** (`lib/categorizer.js`) — Uses Claude to classify messages into 5 categories (ACTION_ITEM, DECISION, ANNOUNCEMENT, QUESTION, FYI) with fallback to rule-based categorization
- **Notion Integration** (`lib/notion-client.js`) — Pushes daily summaries and individual items to a Notion database with rich formatting
- **HTML Renderer** (`lib/html-renderer.js`) — Generates a polished, responsive HTML dashboard with interactive elements (checkboxes, thread toggles, Notion buttons)
- **Main Generator** (`generate-summary.js`) — Orchestrates the full pipeline with CLI options for dry-run, custom time ranges, channel filtering, and Notion integration
- **HTML Template** (`lib/template.html`) — Apple-inspired design with CSS variables, animations, responsive layout, and client-side interactivity
- **Configuration** (`.env.example`, `package.json`) — Environment setup guide and npm scripts for easy execution
- **Test Data** (`test-data/mock-messages.json`) — Sample Slack messages for testing without API calls
- **Documentation** (`README.md`) — Comprehensive setup guide, usage instructions, and automation examples

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Graceful Degradation** — Works without Anthropic API key by falling back to regex-based categorization
- **Rate Limiting** — Built-in delays to respect Slack API rate limits
- **Mock Data Support** — `--dry-run` flag enables testing without API credentials
- **Flexible Filtering** — CLI options for time range, specific channels, and Notion integration
- **Client-Side State** — Uses localStorage to remember which items were saved to Notion
- **Responsive Design** — Mobile-friendly HTML with adaptive grid layouts and hidden actions on small screens
- **Dutch Localization** — All UI text, categories, and documentation in Dutch

author: copilot
body:
A sitemap makes all pages explicitly discoverable by search engines rather than relying solely on link crawling from `index.html` and `blog/index.html`.

## Changes

- **`sitemap.xml`** — New sitemap at repo root listing the homepage (`priority=1.0`) and blog index (`priority=0.8`)
- **`robots.txt`** — New robots.txt file with `Sitemap:` directive for proper sitemap discovery by search engines

## Note on hash-based URLs

Blog post URLs use fragment routing (`/blog/post.html#slug`). The Sitemap protocol explicitly disallows fragment identifiers in URLs, so only the blog index page is included in the sitemap. Search engines will discover individual blog posts by crawling the blog index, which contains links to all posts.

author: copilot
body:
Three independent issues: auto-advance to red status silently failing for Canadian visa renewal after questionnaire submission, info sheet CRUD permissions being asesor-only, and the `/solicitudes` filter lacking a flow selector.

## Bug: Canadian renewal auto-advance on questionnaire completion

`PublicFormController` was fetching only `status, subtype` and evaluating standard-flow logic (`visa_anterior`) when the client completed the questionnaire — no Canadian branching at all. The other two triggers (doc upload, info sheet save) already had the correct dual-branch logic.

```php
// Before — only fetched subtype, always checked visa_anterior
$stmtApp = $this->db->prepare("SELECT status, subtype FROM applications WHERE id = ?");

// After — also fetches Canadian fields and branches accordingly
$stmtApp = $this->db->prepare(
    "SELECT status, subtype, is_canadian_visa, canadian_modalidad, canadian_tipo FROM applications WHERE id = ?"
);
// ... then checks visa_canadiense_anterior / eta_anterior for Canadian renewal
```

## Info sheet permissions

Previously, only `ROLE_ASESOR` could create or edit the info sheet; admin/gerente had no UI access at all.

New rules:
- **Create** (no existing sheet): all roles
- **Edit** (existing sheet): only `ROLE_GERENTE` / `ROLE_ADMIN`

`show.php` button/modal visibility now gates on `!$infoSheet || $isAdmin` (where `$isAdmin` covers both admin and gerente). Controller enforces the edit restriction server-side with an early redirect for asesor when a sheet already exists.

## Flow filter in `/solicitudes`

- Added a **Flujo** dropdown (Todos / Flujo normal / Flujo canadiense 🍁) as the primary filter.
- Status dropdown is JS-driven: options and labels update when flow changes (e.g., `STATUS_LISTO_SOLICITUD` renders as "Listo para carga en portal" under the Canadian flow).
- `STATUS_TRAMITE_CERRADO` and `STATUS_FINALIZADO` are excluded from both status lists for `ROLE_ASESOR`.
- Controller applies `is_canadian_visa = 1` / `(is_canadian_visa = 0 OR IS NULL)` WHERE clauses based on the selected flow.
- Pagination links carry the `flow` parameter.

author: ksuchak1990
body:
## Summary

This PR provides support for extracting, attaching, and serialising door geometries in the floorplan pipeline. It refactors configuration handling, fixes multiple structural issues in door extraction and attachment, and extends YAML serialisation to include doors per room.

## Key Changes

### Configuration and API refactor

- Introduced a top-level `ExtractionConfig` to separate polygon extraction concerns from door attachment behaviour.
- Moved DXF layer selection (door_layer_name) out of `DoorAttachmentConfig` and into extraction-level configuration.
- Updated `config_from_yaml()` to load nested polygons and optional doors blocks.
- Updated all call sites to reflect the new config structure.

### Door extraction and attachment

- Fixed `_generate_doors()` to correctly handle `GeometryCollection`, `LineString`, and `MultiLineString` geometries without violating GeoPandas geometry invariants.
- Ensured centroid coordinates $(x, y)$ are always attached before spatial joins.
- Corrected spatial join behaviour so doors lying on polygon boundaries are correctly matched.
- Fixed a critical dataflow bug where the result of `attach_room_doors()` was previously discarded.
- Ensured door endpoints remain paired via `EntityHandle` and are attached to the appropriate rooms.

### YAML serialisation

- Extended `polygons_to_rooms()` to optionally include door geometries.
- Serialised door endpoints as flow-style `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` lists, consistent with wall segments.
- Updated example usage to pass door column information through to YAML construction.

### Tests

- Updated configuration tests to reflect the new nested config model.
- Updated YAML construction tests to remain compatible with optional door support.
- Added coverage for door serialisation behaviour.

## Result

The pipeline now correctly supports:

- Door extraction from DXF linework
- Robust spatial association of doors with rooms
- Deterministic pairing of door endpoints
- Inclusion of doors in the final YAML output
- All existing functionality remains intact, and the codebase is now cleaner, more explicit, and easier to reason about.

Adds Forward/Reverse/Ping-Pong loop modes and optional in/out loop range points, enabling bounded and reverse playback for animation review workflows.

## Player (`player.rs`)

- **`LoopMode` enum** — `Forward` (default), `Reverse`, `PingPong`; with `next()` cycle and `label()` display methods
- **New `Player` fields** — `loop_mode: Mutex<LoopMode>`, `loop_in/loop_out: Mutex<Option<u64>>` (µs), `ping_pong_forward: AtomicBool`
- **`advance_frame()` updated** — honors loop mode and range:
  - *Forward*: wraps at `loop_out` → `loop_in`
  - *Reverse*: wraps at `loop_in` → last frame before `loop_out`
  - *PingPong*: bounces between range endpoints with saturating overflow protection
- **Public API** — `get/cycle_loop_mode()`, `get/set_loop_in()`, `get/set_loop_out()`, `clear_loop_range()`
- **Helper** — `last_time_point_before(sorted_times, bound)` for reverse-wrap snapping

## App (`app.rs`)

- **Keyboard shortcuts** — `M` cycle mode · `,` set loop-in · `.` set loop-out · `/` clear range
- **Loop state HUD** — semi-transparent top-right overlay, visible whenever mode ≠ Forward or a range is active; shows mode label and `in–out` times in seconds
- **Help overlay** — new "Loop Mode & Range" section; window height increased to fit

…r auth

The previous pattern called redirect() inside a Server Action after signInWithPassword(). In some Next.js versions the Set-Cookie headers from the action are not guaranteed to reach the browser before the redirect fires, so getUser() in middleware sees no session and sends the user back to /login.

Fix: extract the login logic into a separate server action (actions.ts) that returns success/error instead of calling redirect(). The login page is now a Client Component that uses useActionState to call the action, then navigates with router.push("/") only after the action response (and its Set-Cookie headers) has been fully processed by the browser.

Also shows inline error messages instead of redirecting to /auth/error.

### Motivation
- Change the team "power" UX from a pickup-driven one-off to a global-per-team ability with a deterministic cooldown so teams can use a single global action (reshuffle) and see immediate feedback in the web UI. 
- Use a fixed 15s cooldown to simplify game flow and prevent repeated immediate reuse. 
- Prevent team color tinting from obscuring team-provided ball sprites by using a neutral tint when a sprite is applied.

### Description
- Backend (`backendAWSEC2Hot/games/facechinko.js`):
  - Added `TEAM_POWER_COOLDOWN_MS = 15000` and a helper `getPowerCooldownInfo` to compute cooldown state and remaining time. 
  - Reworked team power state shape to remove pickup/available flags and instead track `cooldownUntilMs` and `powerId` per team. 
  - Replaced `grantTeamPower`/`powerReady` pickup flow and updated `consumeTeamPower` to: allow use only when cooldown is clear, set `cooldownUntilMs` on use, emit `powerActivated` with cooldown metadata, and return cooldown fields in the `powerUseResult` payload. 
  - Updated `getWebPlayerState` to expose cooldown fields (`powerCooldownMs`, `powerCooldownRemainingMs`, `powerCooldownUntilMs`, `powerCooldownUntilIso`) and to derive `canUsePower` from cooldown state. 
- Web UI (`webappHot/index.html`, `webappHot/app.js`):
  - Renamed the control button label from `POWER` to `BOIL!!` and updated the hint copy. 
  - Added `cooldownText(ms)` and `renderPowerState(playerState)` helpers to render friendly cooldown messaging and to disable (grey out) the button during cooldown. 
  - Updated websocket handling to immediately show cooldown when a `powerActivated` event is received for the same team and polling to use the new cooldown-aware player-state fields. 
- Unity (`unityHot/RaceBall.cs`):
  - Fixed sprite tinting by making `ApplyTeamSprite` return a `bool` and setting `SpriteRenderer.color` to `Color.white` when a team sprite is applied, otherwise falling back to the team color; also clear stale sprite references when none are found.

### Testing
- Ran JavaScript static checks with `node --check webappHot/app.js` and `node --check backendAWSEC2Hot/games/facechinko.js`, both succeeded. 
- Served the web UI with `python3 -m http.server 4173` and captured a Playwright screenshot to verify the button text and hint, which completed successfully. 
- Verified runtime-ish behavior by exercising the websocket handling and polling code paths in `app.js` via the local page load and observed expected disabled/cooldown UI updates on `powerActivated` messages.

author: copilot
body:
Power users need workflow-specific key bindings. All keyboard shortcuts were previously hardcoded with no override mechanism.

## Approach

Introduces a `KeyConfig` struct (`src/key_config.rs`) that maps `VirtualKeyCode → KeyAction`. Defaults are unchanged when no config is provided. A `--key-config <FILE>` flag loads overrides; invalid action names or unrecognised key names emit `warn!` and are skipped.

## Config format

Plain text, one binding per line, `#` for comments:

```ini
# action = Key1[, Key2, ...]
zoom_in = E, Up
play_pause = Space
```

Full list of action names and supported key names documented in README.

## Key changes

- **`src/key_config.rs`** — `KeyAction` enum (27 actions), `KeyConfig` with `default()` and `load(path)`, `parse_key`/`parse_action` helpers, 12 unit tests. New actions aligned with the current main branch: `CycleComparisonMode` (replaces `ToggleFlipDiff`), `PeekZoom` (hold-to-activate, Z key), `DecreasePeekZoom` (−), `IncreasePeekZoom` (=), `SaveCombinedScreenshot` (U), `ResetZoom` (R), `ToggleHud` (O). `Minus`/`Equals` added to supported key names.
- **`src/app.rs`** — `handle_event` keycode dispatch replaced by `key_config.bindings` lookup; `esc_key_down` renamed `quit_key_down` (now tracks whichever key is bound to `Quit`); `peek_zoom_active` field added to track Z-key hold state; key-release handler deactivates peek zoom; `ResetZoom` fully implemented; `key_config` field added to `AppConfig` and `AppState`; in-app help overlay updated to list all current shortcuts.
- **`src/main.rs`** — `--key-config <FILE>` CLI argument wired through to `AppState`
- **`README.md`** — new *Keyboard Remapping* section with format spec, complete action table (27 actions with defaults), key name reference, and usage example

author: zahidb0nd
body:
## 💡 What
Extracted the tab button rendering logic from `ExpandableTabsComponent` into a new, memoized `TabButton` component within the same file.

## 🎯 Why
The previous implementation defined the button rendering logic inline within the `map` loop. This caused all buttons to re-render whenever the parent `ExpandableTabsComponent` re-rendered (e.g., when the `selected` state changed), even if their individual state didn't change. Additionally, passing a new arrow function `onClick={() => handleSelect(index)}` to each button broke potential memoization.

## 📊 Impact
- **Reduces Re-renders:** Only the tab being selected and the tab being deselected will re-render. All other tabs remain untouched.
- **Stable Handlers:** The `TabButton` now receives a stable `onSelect` callback (from `useCallback`) and an `index`, allowing `React.memo` to work effectively.

## 🔬 Measurement
- Validated with existing unit tests (`npm test src/components/ui/expandable-tabs.test.tsx`).
- Visually verified functionality (tab switching, animations) using a temporary Playwright script.

These components are `Client Components` in `NextJS`, and as a result, they **SHOULD** only really be rendered on the `Client` side.  However, in practice this does not seem to be the case.  Instead they are being called, and unhandled errors are being thrown.  To help prevent this from occurring server-side, we add a guard on the `contract` call, to check for something that should **ONLY** exist in the client's browser.

body: Na tela principal do **Big Kernel Manager**, consta o quanto seguinte: Com base nisso, humildemente, entendi por reescrever algumas partes e explicitar um pouco mais para o usuário final acerca das versões de kernel e do Mesa, justamente com o escopo de facilitar ao máximo possível a tomada de decisão. Sem mais rodeios, segue a minha sugestão de nova redação para a primeira tela que aparece ao abrir o novo aplicativo do BigLinux: **Gerenciamento do kernel e de drivers gráficos (Mesa)** Alterar o kernel ou os drivers gráficos (Mesa) pode impactar a estabilidade geral do sistema e a compatibilidade em aplicações gráficas. Em razão disso, por favor, revise as seguintes recomendações: - (emoji) Mantenha sempre pelo menos uma versão de kernel funcionando e que esteja devidamente instalada (a versão) como alternativa. - **Kernels LTS (Long Term Support):** recebem backports de segurança e correções por mais tempo. São recomendados para servidores, produção e sistemas que priorizam estabilidade com mudanças mínimas. - **Kernels estáveis (mainline/stable):** trazem suporte a hardware mais recente, melhorias de performance e correções. São adequados para uso desktop geral. (emoji) Teste seu sistema completamente após alterações no kernel. (emoji) Se um novo kernel causar problemas, você pode selecionar o kernel anterior no menu de inicialização — desde que ele ainda esteja instalado. - **Kernels com PREEMPT_RT (tempo real):** otimizados para tarefas que exigem execução no momento exato, sem atrasos — como edição de áudio profissional, automação industrial e sistemas críticos. No uso diário (navegação, jogos, escritório), pode reduzir o desempenho geral por priorizar a pontualidade em vez da velocidade ou da quantidade de tarefas processadas simultaneamente. Use apenas se você realmente precisa de tempo real. **Gerenciamento de drivers gráficos (Mesa)** - Mesa é uma implementação open source das APIs OpenGL, Vulkan, OpenCL (via rusticl) e outras, fornecendo aceleração gráfica 2D/3D para GPUs AMD, Intel, NVIDIA e outras. - A alteração de versões do Mesa pode afetar desempenho, corrigir ou introduzir _bugs_ em jogos e em aplicações gráficas. Logo, alterações manuais devem ser feitas com cautela.

author: izmalk
body:
Add a GitHub workflow that automatically opens a PR in the [opensearch-operator](https://github.com/canonical/opensearch-operator) repository to update the OpenSearch Dashboards docs submodule whenever changes are pushed to the `docs` directory on the `2/edge` branch.

## How it works

1. Triggered on push to `2/edge` when `docs/**` files change, or manually via `workflow_dispatch`.
2. Checks out `canonical/opensearch-operator` at `2/edge` with its submodules initialised.
3. Reads the target repo's `.github/CODEOWNERS` to find owners of the `docs/dashboards`
   submodule path and automatically assigns them as reviewers on the opened PR.
4. Updates the submodule pointer to the triggering commit SHA.
5. Signs the commit using the `canonical-data-platform-bot` SSH signing key.
6. Opens a PR against `2/edge` in the OpenSearch operator repo with the submodule bump.

## Prerequisites

The following secrets must be configured in the repository settings before
this workflow can run successfully:

- `PAT` — a Personal Access Token with `repo` scope for `canonical/opensearch-operator`
- `CI_COMMITS_SSH_SIGNING_KEY` — the bot's SSH private key for signed commits

## Notes

- The autogenerated PR branch name includes the triggering SHA (`auto/update-dashboards-docs-submodule-<sha>`) to avoid collisions between concurrent runs.
- The workflow will fail early if the branch already exists on the remote.

author: kodanda10
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix Insecure Deserialization in VectorStore

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `VectorStore` was using `numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=True)` to load vector indices. This allows arbitrary code execution if the index file is tampered with (e.g., via file upload vulnerability or compromised storage).
🎯 Impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) if an attacker can modify the vector index file.
🔧 Fix:
    - Changed storage format from pickled dictionary in `.npy` to zip-compressed arrays in `.npz` using `numpy.savez_compressed`.
    - Updated loader to prefer `.npz` and use `allow_pickle=False`.
    - Implemented a migration path: legacy files are loaded (with warning) and immediately re-saved in the new secure format.
✅ Verification:
    - Added `Pinak_Services/memory_service/tests/test_security_migration.py` which verifies:
        1. Legacy pickle files can be loaded and migrated.
        2. New files are saved as `.npz`.
        3. New files can be loaded with `allow_pickle=False`.
    - Ran full regression suite (74 tests passed).

body: ### Motivation - Continue ANN SOTA audit P1 work by making two-stage SIMD reranking adaptive to observed latency so query-time quality policies respect soft latency targets. - Reduce risk of long-tail latency spikes during large candidate re-ranking by tracking rerank costs and shrinking/expanding the candidate count (`rerank_k`) automatically. ### Description - Added two atomic fields to `HnswIndex`: `rerank_latency_target_us` and `rerank_latency_ema_us` to store a soft latency SLO (microseconds) and an EMA of observed rerank latency. - Initialized the new fields in all constructors and load paths so newly created and loaded indices start with sane defaults (`0` = disabled). - Exposed a small public API to configure/read the target via `set_rerank_latency_target_us()` and the getters `rerank_latency_target_us()` and `rerank_latency_ema_us()`. - Implemented `adapt_rerank_k_to_latency()` and `update_rerank_latency_ema()` and wired sampling around the SIMD re-rank phases (`search_with_rerank_with_ef` and `search_with_rerank_quality`) using `Instant` to measure rerank time and adapt `rerank_k` when appropriate. - Added unit tests `test_rerank_latency_target_configuration_roundtrip` and `test_rerank_latency_ema_updates_after_two_stage_search` to validate configuration and EMA update behavior. ### Testing - Ran `cargo fmt --all` successfully to format the changes. - Ran `cargo test -p velesdb-core rerank_latency_target_configuration_roundtrip` and it passed. - Ran `cargo test -p velesdb-core rerank_latency_ema_updates_after_two_stage_search` and it passed. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/tasks/task_e_699e2440d69c832aa9f44759d998dcec) ---

body:
Closes #145

## Summary

Remove `filterByFactoryPhase` and all related types/functions from the scheduler. The dependency graph (`dependsOn`/`blockedBy`) already encodes the real ordering between issues. The phase gate over-applied by treating ALL issues in a phase as a blocker, not just those in the candidates dependency chain.

### Problem

An issue in phase N was blocked if ANY open issue existed in phase N-1, even if the candidates actual dependencies were satisfied. Example: #1178 (audit) depends on #1170 (build, stack-ready), but was blocked by #1236 (unrelated build meta-issue with no PR).

### Changes

**`src/scheduler/graph.ts`** (-131 lines)
- Removed: `filterByFactoryPhase`, `FactoryPhaseRejection`, `FactoryPhaseFilterResult`, `STANDARD_PHASE_ORDER`, `parseFactoryLabel`, `getIssueFactoryPhase`, `FactoryPhase`

**`src/scheduler/watcher.ts`** (-6/+4 lines)
- Removed `filterByFactoryPhase` call site and `FactoryPhaseRejection` import
- Stack-unblocked candidates now pass directly to the queue filter
- Added comment explaining phase ordering is handled by dependencies
- Removed `factoryPhaseBlocked` from debug output

**`src/scheduler/graph.test.ts`** (-230/+32 lines)
- Removed all `parseFactoryLabel`, `getIssueFactoryPhase`, and `filterByFactoryPhase` test suites
- Added regression tests confirming phase-labeled issues are not spuriously blocked by unrelated issues in earlier phases

- Corrigir o runtime `Uncaught SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list` causado por um grande `<script type="module">` inline que estava gerando erro de parsing no HTML.
- Simplificar a organização do código JavaScript para tornar a inicialização assíncrona mais robusta e manter intacto o fluxo de autenticação/calendário.

### Description

- Extraí toda a lógica JavaScript inline de `index.html` para um novo arquivo `app.js` e substituí o bloco inline por `<script type="module" src="./app.js"></script>`.
- Preservei a guarda `window.__dexterCalendarAuthInit`, a integração com Supabase (URL / anon key) e o fluxo de signup/login/confirm/logout e carregamento de eventos da planilha.
- Validei o arquivo JS com `node --check` e removi trechos duplicados/ruidosos do HTML que causavam fechamento de blocos incorreto.
- Centralizei a inicialização assíncrona em `async function init()` e tratei erros de startup via `init().catch(...)`.

### Testing

- `node --check app.js` executou com sucesso e não reportou erros de sintaxe.
- A aplicação foi servida localmente com `python3 -m http.server 8000` e a página carregou usando um navegador controlado por Playwright.
- O script Playwright abriu `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, monitorou `pageerror`/`console.error` e gerou uma screenshot, sem erros JS da aplicação além de um `404` para favicon.

body:
### Motivation
- Make `--headed` startup failures actionable by explaining common causes (missing DISPLAY/WAYLAND or reusing a headless session) instead of showing a generic "Failed to start session server" error.
- Canonicalize user-provided navigation input so CLI navigation works consistently for shorthand or slightly malformed URLs.
- Give operators finer-grained control over cloud sync so they can disable specific event types without turning off sync entirely.

### Description
- CLI diagnostics: enhanced `ensure_server()` in `browser_use/skill_cli/main.py` to print a helpful hint when `--headed` is requested but no desktop display is available and to point users to session logs via `browser-use --session <name> server logs`, and added a warning when a user requests `--headed` but an existing session with the same name is running headless.
- URL normalization: added `browser_use/skill_cli/url_utils.py` with `normalize_navigation_url()` and wired it into `browser_use/skill_cli/commands/browser.py` and `browser_use/skill_cli/direct.py` to prepend `https://` or normalize `http:/`/`https:/` style inputs.
- Cloud sync flags: added per-event env flags in `OldConfig` and `FlatEnvConfig` in `browser_use/config.py` and introduced `EVENT_SYNC_FLAGS` and per-event gating checks in `browser_use/sync/service.py` so specific event types (session/task/step/output) can be disabled independently.
- UX and docs: updated `README.md` to clarify how to run a visible browser (mention `Browser(headless=False)` and `--headed`), added a note recommending `uv run --active ...` to avoid `VIRTUAL_ENV` mismatch warnings, and documented that browser visibility is model-independent.
- No-LLM guidance: improved the local-agent error text in `browser_use/skill_cli/commands/agent.py` to call out manual browser commands (`open`, `state`, `click`, `type`, `screenshot`) as an alternative when no LLM is configured.

### Testing
- Compiled the modified CLI module with `python -m py_compile browser_use/skill_cli/main.py`, and compilation succeeded.
- Attempted `pre-commit run --files browser_use/skill_cli/main.py README.md` but it failed because `pre-commit` is not installed in this environment (automated check failed).

body:
### Motivation
- Evitar que AUTO/CANARY queden bloqueados pidiendo 85% cuando el modo operativo post-n15 tiene piso en 75%, lo que impedía promociones legítimas a REAL.
- Reducir oscilaciones y reinicios de confirmación por micro-ruido en la selección del mejor bot del techo dinámico.
- Evitar que el `TEST` temporal acabe con una sola clase cuando hay diversidad en el histórico moviendo fronteras sin mezclar datos.

### Description
- Alineé los umbrales de bypass fuerte a `IA_ACTIVACION_REAL_THR_POST_N15` cambiando `AUTO_REAL_UNRELIABLE_GATE_MIN_PROB` y `CANARY_STRONG_GATE_MIN_PROB` para usar ese valor y permitir escapes coherentes en modo B (post-n15). 
- Añadí lógica de escape para CANARY que permite habilitar REAL si la `dyn_gate` indica `allow_real`, `trigger_ok`, confirmaciones y `p_best` >= umbral post-n15, y añadí mensajes diagnósticos correspondientes.
- Implementé el bypass controlado para `reliable=false` evaluando `gate_strong_unrel` (comprueba `allow_real`, `trigger_ok` y `p_best`) y permitiendo promoción si se cumplen condiciones y/o bypass fuerte en warmup.
- Mejoré `_actualizar_compuerta_techo_dinamico` añadiendo parámetros de clustering (`DYN_ROOF_CLUSTER_*`), tolerancia de empate `DYN_ROOF_TIE_KEEP_CONFIRM_TOL`, ajustes de GAP/cluster para evitar oscilaciones por micro-ruido, y refiné el cálculo de `trigger_ok` según modo (A/B/C y warmup).
- Agregué `_expand_test_hasta_doble_clase()` al cálculo temporal de `TRAIN/CALIB/TEST` para desplazar fronteras sin mezclar y evitar que `TEST` quede con una sola clase.

### Testing
- Compilé el archivo con `python -m py_compile 5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py` y la compilación completó correctamente.
- Verifiqué presencia de los nuevos símbolos con `rg -n "AUTO_REAL_UNRELIABLE_GATE_MIN_PROB|CANARY_STRONG_GATE_MIN_PROB|IA_ACTIVACION_REAL_THR_POST_N15|DYN_ROOF_TIE_KEEP_CONFIRM_TOL" 5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py` y los patrones aparecieron según lo esperado.
- Ejecuté una segunda compilación tras los cambios con `python -m py_compile 5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py` para confirmar estabilidad de sintaxis y ambos pasos fueron exitosos.

author: moukrea
body:
## Summary

Major upgrade to git-pilot implementing six new features from the v2 technical specification:

- **Branch freshness detection**: auto-fetch on session start, fast-forward behind branches, warn on divergence
- **Base branch drift detection**: detect when the base branch has advanced, auto-rebase before push with configurable conflict strategy
- **Intelligent rebase & conflict resolution**: structured conflict details with recommendations, tri-state `protectDefaultBranch` (warn/block/off)
- **Unrelated work detection**: `UserPromptSubmit` hook provides branch context so Claude can detect off-topic requests
- **Agent Teams support**: suppress interactive prompts for spawned agents, orchestrator-only operations, git worktree management
- **Automatic stash management**: auto-stash/restore on branch switches

### Changes

- **3 new library scripts**: `agent.sh`, `rebase.sh`, `worktree.sh`
- **1 new hook**: `prompt-context.sh` (UserPromptSubmit)
- **6 modified hooks**: session-start, session-stop, pre-commit, post-bash, post-write, hooks.json
- **3 new skills**: `/stash`, `/worktree`, `/rebase`
- **3 modified skills**: `/branch`, `/finish`, `/configure`
- **Updated config schema**: 13 new config keys across `rebase`, `worktree`, `agentTeams` sections
- **CLAUDE.md**: expanded from 6 to 10 rules
- **Plugin version**: 1.1.0 → 2.0.0
- **Test suite**: 74 bats test cases across 9 test files

## Test plan

- [ ] `bash -n plugins/git-pilot/scripts/*.sh` passes (verified)

body:
**Steps to reproduce:**
- Create a DB with l10n_ar and l10n_ar ecommerce
- Go to Settings > Invoicing > Fiscal Localization
- Select the 'Argentina - Argentine Generic Chart of Accounts for Registered Accountants' package
- Create a website, and a portal user
- Add a main and a secondary address to the user using the website form in 'My Account'
- Go to the secondary address and change any field
- Click on Save Address
- Multiple errors will appear on the form (reproducible with other similar config)
(and in logs: `UserWarning: unsupported operand type(s) for "==": 'l10n_latam.identification.type()' == '1'`)

**Issue:**
In `address_form_fields` some hidden input field are used to add specific non-editable values to the forms.

This breaks the address validation of `CustomerPortal` in `def _validate_address_values` due to the following comparison: `partner_sudo[commercial_field_name] != address_values[commercial_field_name]`
which try to compare recordsets with the given ids.

**Fix:**
Cast relational field to their id values to ensure they can be properly compared to the website form values.

Adds sharing functionality to activity cards via Twitter, Facebook, email, and clipboard.

## Implementation

- **Share buttons**: Four icon-based buttons added below participants list on each card
  - Twitter: Opens intent URL with activity name and description
  - Facebook: Standard sharer dialog

  ```javascript
  data-activity="${name}" 
  data-description="${details.description.replace(/"/g, '"')}"
  data-schedule="${formattedSchedule.replace(/"/g, '"')}"

Summary:
The combo kernel always use the tunable config. This tunable config applied to tunable kernel is ok, but when we apply this config to a persistent kernel, we can generate large tiles during autotuning
{F1985914623}

The fix passes the persistent sub-program's fixed block size (max_persistent_rblock) from the combo kernel to the config generator via inductor_meta. body:
This pull request significantly improves the **robustness, safety, and observability** of **soilmoistureprofiles**. It introduces the **EWTS logging framework**, strengthens runtime validation, fixes multiple memory-management issues, and replaces unsafe assertions and direct `stderr` usage with structured logging and exceptions.

Overall, the changes harden the code against invalid inputs, memory leaks, and silent failures while improving diagnosability during runtime.

---

### Additions

* Added initial integration of the **EWTS Logger**.
* Added missing logger methods to complete logging support.
* Added structured **log entries** around key operations and error conditions.

---

### Changes

#### Runtime Validation & Error Handling

* Converted `assert()` usage to **runtime error throws** to ensure errors are handled in production builds.
* Added explicit runtime errors for:
  * Invalid wetting front sizes
  * Missing SMP file names
* Logged error conditions **before throwing exceptions** for better traceability.
* Replaced `std::cerr` usage with structured logging via `LOG`.

#### Memory Management & Safety

* Fixed multiple **memory leaks** related to dynamically allocated arrays.
* Corrected array destruction logic by using `delete[]` where required.
* Ensured local dynamically allocated arrays are properly deleted during resizing and cleanup.

#### Code Quality

* Applied formatting-only changes for readability and consistency.

---

### Removals

* Removed unsafe reliance on `assert()` for runtime validation.
* Removed direct `stderr` (`cerr`) logging in favor of centralized EWTS logging.

The `a2a/` core types package does not include testable examples (`Example_*` functions). Usage snippets exist in the README and `doc.go`, but they are not executable, not validated by `go test`, and do not render as function-level examples on [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev).

author: admackin
body:
## Problem

`col['key.with.period']` silently returns `NULL` instead of the key's value.

This affects any Snowflake VARIANT column whose JSON was produced by a system that uses dotted strings as flat key names — a common pattern in tracing and observability platforms (e.g. OpenTelemetry attributes, Braintrust span metadata).

## Root cause: two separate bugs in `indices_to_json_extract`

### Bug 1 — dot in key name treated as JSONPath path separator

`col['a.b']` was transformed to:

```sql
col -> '$.a.b'
```

DuckDB's JSONPath engine interprets `.` as a path separator, so this traverses *into* a nested object (`a` → `b`) rather than looking up the literal key `"a.b"`. If no nested structure exists the result is `NULL`.

The fix exploits a DuckDB feature: [a path that does not start with `$` is treated as a direct key name](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/json#json-extraction-functions), bypassing JSONPath interpretation entirely. Keys that aren't simple identifiers (`[A-Za-z0-9_]+`) now omit the `$.` prefix:

```
col['simple']   → col -> '$.simple'   (unchanged)
col['a.b']      → col -> 'a.b'        (direct key lookup, no JSONPath)
```

### Bug 2 — `::string` / `::text` not recognised as string casts

In Snowflake, `::varchar`, `::string`, and `::text` are all equivalent string casts. However sqlglot parses them to different `DataType` values:

| Snowflake syntax | sqlglot `DataType.Type` |
|---|---|
| `::varchar` | `VARCHAR` |
| `::string` / `::text` | `TEXT` |
| `::nvarchar` | `NVARCHAR` |

The existing check was `== exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR` only, so `::string` fell through to `JSONExtract` (`->`) instead of `JSONExtractScalar` (`->>`). This returned the JSON-encoded value (e.g. `'"sess1"'` with surrounding quotes) rather than the plain string (`'sess1'`).

The fix introduces `_STRING_CAST_TYPES = {VARCHAR, TEXT, NVARCHAR}` and checks `in _STRING_CAST_TYPES`.

**Note:** these two bugs interact. In the common real-world pattern `metadata['request_context.channel_session_id']::string`, both bugs fire simultaneously — the key returns `NULL` (bug 1), and even if it didn't, the string value would still be returned JSON-quoted (bug 2).

## Changes

**`fakesnow/transforms/transforms.py`**
- Add `import re`
- Add module-level `_SIMPLE_JSON_KEY` regex and `_STRING_CAST_TYPES` set
- `indices_to_json_extract`: expand string-type check from `== VARCHAR` to `in _STRING_CAST_TYPES`
- `indices_to_json_extract`: for string keys that don't match `_SIMPLE_JSON_KEY`, emit the key directly instead of prefixing with `$.`

**`tests/test_semis.py`**
- `test_object_key_with_period`: end-to-end test — inserts a row with a period-containing key, asserts correct values for bare access (JSON-typed result with surrounding quotes) and `::string`-cast access (unquoted plain string), and `NULL` for a missing dotted key

**`tests/test_transforms.py`**
- `test_indices_to_object`: two new assertions — `->` output for a period key without cast, and `->>` output for a period key with `::varchar` cast

## Verification

```
310 passed, 1 xfailed in 26.84s
```

No regressions against the existing suite.

author: richlander
body:
The CI failure on main (run [22372894569](https://github.com/richlander/markout/actions/runs/22372894569/job/64756142564)) was caused by a test parallelism race condition. Five test classes redirect `Console.SetError` to capture warning output, but xUnit v3 runs test classes in parallel. When two such tests run simultaneously, one overwrites the other's `Console.Error`, causing the assertion to find an empty string.

**Fix:** Add `[Collection("ConsoleError")]` to all 5 affected test classes, serializing their execution:
- `ShapeSupportTests`
- `IgnoreFieldsTests`
- `IgnoreColumnWhenTests`
- `OneLineWriterTests`
- `DiagramWriterTests`
